entities.name: B'lemyae
entities.description:
The B'lemyae were an ancient humanoid species discovered living in isolation within a remote African rainforest during the late 19th century. Distinguished by their unusual anatomy, the B'lemyae lacked conventional heads, with their facial features instead embedded directly into their upper torsos. By 1887, only two confirmed individuals, Kaylin and Erser, remained alive, making them one of the rarest known intelligent species on Earth. (AUDIO: The Headless Ones)

The B'lemyae were humanoid in form but possessed neither heads nor necks. Their eyes, nose and mouth were located on their chests, giving them a striking resemblance to the legendary headless men depicted in medieval maps and folklore. This unusual appearance led many humans to regard them as monsters. (AUDIO: The Headless Ones)

Despite their fearsome appearance, the B'lemyae were gentle and intelligent beings capable of speech and complex social organisation. By the nineteenth century, their dwindling population and isolation had left the species struggling to survive, with Kaylin and Erser suffering from hunger and increasingly limited resources. (AUDIO: The Headless Ones)

The B'lemyae were descended from an extraterrestrial species that escaped enslavement on their homeworld aboard a number of spacecraft.

The Ba-El Cratt were a hive-mind race who were at war with the Cancri.

Their empire was known as the Ba-El Cratt Collective. They declared war on the Human Empire when they discovered that they had entered a deal with the Cancri to mine diamonds from the atmosphere of Saturn. Three Ba-El Cratt travelled to Saturn in an assault craft to destroy Kollo-Zarnista Mining Facility 27. (PROSE: Diamond Dogs)

"The spark of sentience in a Bakri synth" was one of the moments the Doctor's TARDIS saved from destruction in the Last Great Time War. The War Doctor and Cinder visited this moment. (NC: The Moments In Between)

entities.description:
The Balumin were an egg-shaped species with tentacle-like arms. They had either blue or orange skin and large eyes and smelled of oranges and lemons.

When the Brilliant took its maiden voyage in the 40th century, the passengers were Balumin in order to minimise human deaths. When the Brilliant was attacked by the Mandelbrot Sett, the Balumin passengers were targeted by the raiders. One Balumin, Mrs Wingsworth, helped the Tenth Doctor in his investigations. (PROSE: The Pirate Loop) One of the tourists who came from the 347th century to 1500 BC Greece was a Balumin. (PROSE: The Slitheen Excursion)

They had rows of needle-like teeth in a chomping, circular mouth, nine black eyes and two thickly muscled, frog-like legs ending in claws. They had greenish flesh bristling with cactus-like spines and their blood was green. (PROSE: Dominion)

entities.description:
The i (singular Banshara) were a species that, according to the First Doctor, had a chemical dependence on endorphins, specifically love.

During World War II, three Bansharai that had crashed on Earth appeared to Barbara Wright, Julia Miller and Sarah Miller as someone they loved. However, Barbara and Julia rejected their Bansharai; the Bansharai weakened until Sarah's Banshara found them and, reunited, the three were able to regain their health. This allowed them to leave Earth. (PROSE: Tell Me You Love Me)

Barcelonian dogs were dogs from the planet Barcelona, which, according to the Ninth Doctor, had no noses.

The Doctor wished to take Rose Tyler there to see them, remarking how the joke about dogs with no noses was always funny on Barcelona, (TV: The Parting of the Ways) and almost did after his regeneration before she requested to return home. (TV: Born Again)

entities.description:
Barnacles were a group of marine animals found on Earth. The cirripedes encountered by the Second Doctor on an asteroid in 7691 were also barnacles, but evolved by parallel evolution. (AUDIO: The Outliers)

Space barnacles could be found on the outsides of spacecraft travelling through space. (PROSE: The Hungry Night) One kind of space barnacle, the electromagnetic barnacle, was a much more complex and sentient creature. During her time as a tour guide on Gendar, Maxie Masters recalled giving guided tours of the Babbling Bibliothèque to various alien tourists, including electromagnetic barnacles. (PROSE: Out of the Box)

In the Land of Fiction, Rob Roy MacGregor returned the Doctor's TARDIS to him once when it had been lost underwater, and had been recovered covered in barnacles. (AUDIO: Legend of the Cybermen)

Donna Noble once compared an alien tourist to a "walking" barnacle, with tentacles. (AUDIO: Death's Deal)

A ruthless dictator ordered the Great Cleansing in which millions of Basprali died. The Basprali later joined the Earth Alliance in fighting the Daleks. The military prowess they had developed under the dictator helped to defeat the Daleks. (PROSE: The Inquisitor's Story)

The claimed Earth as part of their empire and met with little resistance. This was because Edward Grainger, years earlier, had written his memoirs, titled My Life With The Doctor, and humanity gave up creating anything new, merely expecting the Doctor to help them in times of trouble. The Benanki provided food for the humans.

The Seventh Doctor prevented this from happening by going back and convincing Edward not to write his memoirs. (PROSE: Testament)

entities.description: On a mission for the Time Lords, the Fourth Doctor was sent to destroy a space station that held the Bendriggans' virus. However, he and Sarah Jane were accused of murdering a messenger and sentenced to death by Admiral Cosmicon, the Bendriggan commander. The Doctor proved his innocence by sending a message in Time Lord logic to a Bendriggan code expert. But winning their trust was short-lived when many Bendriggans became infected. After watching the Admiral die, the Doctor set the Bendriggan flagship on a collision course with the space station, destroying them both and saving the remainder of the Bendriggan race. (COMIC: Virus)

The Berahima are an alien species from the Prime Universe, appearing in multiple stories in the non-DWU series The Crew of the Copper-Colored Cupids starting from 2019's [https://thecrewofthecoppercoloredcupids.wordpress.com/2019/05/01/marksmanship-526-and-the-multi-dimensional-race-story/ Marksmanship-526 and the Multi-Dimensional Race] through the person of Brutus. The creatures declared the planet selected for clearance and re-seeding and began to consume the Velgors “before their masters arrive.” Either way the invasion was a failure due in no small part to the Doctor being able to program the device to produce another mutant fruit that encapsulated the invading ones. (COMIC: Harvest of Doom)

entities.description:
Berserkers were a warrior race who were the inspiration for Norse berserkers. They visited Earth at some point. They encountered Vikings and were mistaken for human warriors wearing animal skins.

The Berserkers created special pendants, which they made to expand their armies. The pendants would allow people to control other people. With every person they controlled, they would become more like a Berserker. At least one Berserker pendant existed on Earth. It fell into the hands of Jacob West and, later, Paul Langer.

In 1940 a man used the pendant and turned into a Berserker. He was put in a van. (TV: The Mark of the Berserker)

entities.description:
The Beshielach were a race of sentient planetesimals engineered by the Great Houses in the early stages of the War in Heaven. Because they were designed by the Houses, they had a literal genetic grasp on history, but despite being intended to be used as weapons, they proved much better at diplomacy. The most significant hive of Beshielach was the Autrobulus hive, which negotiated the surrender of native authorities who had been largely co-opted by the enemy. (PROSE: The Book of the War)

entities.description: The Bessanians were the inhabitants of Bessan. As recalled by Brother Lassar, they had "some rather lovely wings" which were inherited by the Krillitanes after they invaded the planet. He claimed that they made a million widows in one day. (TV: School Reunion)

entities.description: The Bhor'Vhali of Gand City were an infamous species active in the early 40th century, described by Christian as "brilliant programmers" with "no social conscience to speak of". For the right price, they were willing to perform fleshings, as they did for Caldin Corrigan, creating a duplicate of his daughter Emily Corrigan. (PROSE: Cybergeddon)

entities.name: Binary demi-species
entities.description:
According to the Thirteenth Doctor, binary demi-species were rare. Individuals from such species were symbiotic hybrids of two living forms, which could meld or unmeld from one another at will; one was usually more intelligent and the other more dangerous and animalistic. When both their forms were in a single body, they had two pulses at once.

The Grand Serpent was a member of a binary demi-species, with the ability to project a serpent-like creature with which he was symbiotically bonded with out of himself. (TV: The Vanquishers)

(COMIC: Defender of the Daleks)

entities.description: The Blehurg were large, grey, thorny-shelled creatures. They were more aggressive by nature than their neighbouring enemies of the planet Vorala. They were developed enough to once use a perception filter in order to infiltrate the 24-hour newsroom of their planet when they attempted to hypnotise the population using a projection emanating from a weather map. Their plan to enslave the people was thwarted by the Eleventh Doctor. (COMIC: 24-Hour News Invasion)

entities.description:
The Bom-borradohs were a species known to the Eleventh Doctor. They could create ring-like portals, allowing people to travel through space and time. The Doctor used their help to get into the Tomb of the Bear, then escape, travelling from 1934 to the 21st century. (PROSE: Snowfall)

entities.name: Boneless
entities.description:
"" was the name the Twelfth Doctor gave to creatures from a two-dimensional universe. They were able to reduce both lifeforms and other three-dimensional objects to two-dimensions. After taking on three-dimensional forms themselves, they were also able to restore objects back from two-dimensional to three-dimensional. They also demonstrated the ability to drain dimensional energy from the Doctor's TARDIS, causing its external shell to be drastically reduced in size and weakened.

In their natural form, an individual Boneless manifested as a mass of transparent, writhing tendrils that could only travel across flat surfaces such as floors, walls or ceilings. In this form they had the ability to reduce a three dimensional object or person to two dimensions on physical contact, literally flattening the target against whatever surface they were standing on. This process appeared extremely painful as one such victim, PC Forrest, screamed in agony when she was flattened. This process also resulted in the death of living targets, their corpses appearing as a mural flattened against a surface.

Their presence alone could leech dimensional energy from nearby sources such as the Doctor's TARDIS, causing it to drastically reduce in size before completely losing all power.

The Boneless could dissect anything or anyone they had flattened in order to learn how its physical dimensions functioned. For instance, the only remains of one victim appeared as a microscopic blowup of human skin. Another "mural" seen was actually the human nervous system dissected from PC Forrest's flattened corpse.

entities.name: Bonepuppet
entities.description:
The bonepuppets were a species that tried to conquer Earth in the 15th century.

They used a weed that would have covered half the planet and driven out the human race. The Sixth Doctor was able to stop them with Xoco's help, but not before her husband was killed.

The Seventh Doctor later visited Xoco's adult child Tochtli, having him use the psychic power he had inherited from his mother to learn of the bonepuppets' newest plans. The Doctor used that information to stop them on another planet. (PROSE: Nobody's Gift)
entities.short_description: The bonepuppets were a species that tried to conquer Earth in the 15th century.

entities.description:
rampaged through the Gigamarket after a set of time disturbances. They were supposed to be kept separate from humanoid species following a war. (AUDIO: The Greatest Shop in the Galaxy)

entities.name: Breeble
entities.description:
The Breebles were a "mischievous" and "meddlesome" species. (GAME: Robot Rose)

Breebles competed in the 309th Intergalactic Song Contest, attended by the Seventh Doctor and Mel. They demonstrated their high-pitched, squeaking voices. (AUDIO: Bang-Bang-a-Boom!) At some point, an incarnation of the Doctor destroyed the Breebles' replication pods.

This led the vengeful Breebles to attempt to kill the Doctor in his ninth incarnation: they abducted his companion Rose Tyler and created a robot duplicate of Rose with orders to assassinate the Doctor. However, the real Rose escaped from their grasp and rejoined the Doctor, who was able to tell her apart from the copy because the duplicate had a flawed memory disk and misremembered details of Rose's adventures with the Doctor. She was, for example, under the impression that the Autons had been working for the Slitheen family. The Doctor deactivated the robots, thus escaping the Breebles' assassination plot. (GAME: Robot Rose)

entities.name: Bright Nobles
entities.description: The Bright Nobles were an alien race which ruled the Regulator and her people through the power of Enamour. Judging by what the Regulator and the Herald have said about them, the Bright Nobles did not seem to intend harm and were simple rulers. A war broke out to destroy the dragon and it ended up buried on Geath. The remnants of the Bright Nobles died out over the years, but their Herald went insane, waiting for their orders. (PROSE: The King's Dragon)

Bugbies were a species that seemingly inhabited Planet Bedtime Stories. They were yellow, roughly square in shape, and had big eyes and smiles.

The Fourteenth Doctor arrived on Planet Bedtime Stories to tell the bedtime story The Way Back Home, where he recognised one Bugbie sitting in a chair. There was also a trio of Bugbies to his right. (TV: )

entities.name: Byulnian
entities.description:
Byulnians were the inhabitants of Byulna, the native species of Lenny Kruger. The three "Common Men" he stole from the planet — Myamus, Jecomen and Kappaban — also belonged to the species. According to Lenny, even though they had access to time travel technology, they were not permitted to leave their own planet.

Byulnians were, as Rita noted, significantly larger than humans, though were capable of disguising themselves as members of the human race with skin suits. They drew power from attention and memories. Mark Carville, born Myamus as on Byulna, was able to draw strength, through photographs of past Common Men gigs, from the popularity of the Common Men across the world. As millions of people worldwide thought of him all the time, his strength grew stronger and stronger. According to the Fifth Doctor, this might be dangerous for him.

Because of their abilities, laws were put in place that prohibited the use of photographs and anything else capable of recording past moments. This was because the government was afraid that the population would grow power-hungry if given access to these powers. They also could not leave Byulna. Lenny, though, who opposed these laws, claimed that these were inherent traits of their species — their "true nature".

A strong thirst for domination caused Lenny Kruger to kidnap three children, and bring them to 20th century Earth to grow up as "human" in skin suits. The three, named Mark Carville, James O'Meara and Korky Goldsmith, eventually formed a soon-to-be-popular pop group, the Common Men.

entities.description:
The Calabrian were a species who sent delegates to Earth in order to bid for Lozla Nataniel Henk's mutated Super Krillitane.

Toch'Lu, the Krillitane Brood Mother, slaughtered the Calabrian delegates and took on the guise of a Calabrian female when she encountered Emily Parr. (PROSE: )

Calabrians had a prominent cartilage on their forehead. (PROSE: )

entities.name: Calapian
entities.description:
Calapians were a six-headed species that were native to the planet Calapia.

The Thirteenth Doctor described the Calapians as "a wonderful bunch, throw a party at the drop of a hat, six heads, lots of hats". She’d also said that they didn’t like to talk about the ruins, and had never been able to figure out why.

The Death Moon forced the Calapians into shelter when it passed over Calapia every sixty-four years.

When the Thirteenth Doctor visited the planet in the company of Yaz, Ryan, and Graham during a passing of the Death Moon, they too were forced to shelter in a bunker with some Calapians on the planet for three weeks. (PROSE: The Shadow Passes)
entities.short_description: Calapians were a six-headed species that were native to the planet Calapia.

entities.name: Callicon
entities.description: The Callicon were a species who very rarely left their hermetic homeworld. They were known for their distinctive songs, including the lament of regret and sufferance. Several Callicons were kidnapped and brought to the Edifice against their will. (AUDIO: The Forever Trap)

entities.name: Canavitchi
entities.description:
The were a species from the planet Fen'vetch Suxa Canavitchi.

Their lifespan was hundreds of years long. They had a gestalt-like consciousness and were green, slender, and frail-looking, with teeth and fangs. (PROSE: King of Terror)

The Canavitchi did not fear death, since they considered it to be a doorway to a better life. (PROSE: King of Terror)

They were once so feared in the universe that they were the ancient equivalent of the Daleks. According to Shaun Ryman, they had been on Earth for a thousand years, waiting for their warriors to arrive, during which time they faked the Turin Shroud, set up the Knights Templar, gave the Spanish Inquisition ideas about how flat the Earth was, caused the American War of Independence and the Wall Street Crash, and helped Nostradamus write his prophecies, all to slow down humanity's technological evolution. Had it not been for their interference, humanity would have had interstellar travel capability by the 1850s.
entities.short_description: The were a species from the planet Fen'vetch Suxa Canavitchi.

entities.name: Canisian
entities.description:
Canisians were a warlike humanoid species from Alpha Canis One.

During the 21st century, the Canisian Empire came under the control of Tannis, who led them in an invasion of Earth. (WC: Death Comes to Time) During the invasion, Felix Mather was Secretary of State. (PROSE: Trading Futures)

At some point they quit their war-mongering ways to become a peaceful species, even turning to celebrating Earth history with a convention at Canis Major Overdensity Convention Center and Resort. (COMIC: A Doctor in the House?) Category:Species Category:Humanoid species

entities.description: The Carpathians were a species in the far future who created the Boulevard of Alternate Brutalities for Faction Paradox. (PROSE: The Shape of Things) The Faction gave them "the wealth of entire galaxies" in return. (PROSE: Library Pictures)

entities.name: Carrionite
entities.description:
The Carrionites were a species of humanoids which used word-based science or "witchcraft" to reshape reality.

The true form of a Carrionite resembled a giant skeletal raven or crow. They were able to assume a more humanoid form but this used a lot of energy, and so they usually had wrinkled skin, large, clawed hands, and sharp canine teeth. The Carrionite Lilith could assume the form of a beautiful young woman, a trick she used to ensnare male victims. (TV: The Shakespeare Code)

Carrionite technology was described as witchcraft. It was actually a word-based science, as opposed to the mathematics of most species, and relied on the right words and the right places, such as the Carrionite's use of the Globe Theatre's structure. They also placed great importance on knowing the name of an individual to give them control.

With this linguistic technology for a basis, the Carrionites had a wide variety of abilities. They used both poppets and puppets as DNA replication modules to cause damage from afar or control a person's actions. This required a tissue sample, such as a hair, to work. They could also fly, dematerialise and rematerialise at will, communicate with other Carrionites from a distance and had the ability to discover a person's name and use it against them, even sensing if those they named were out of their time, like Martha Jones. The Doctor, however, was mostly immune to such, though Lilith could detect a name that strongly connected to him; Rose. (TV: The Shakespeare Code)

entities.description:
Ceccecs were two-dimensional pseudo-forms, with low resolution and monochrome to save bandwidth. They were generated by block transfer computation. They crackled and flickered, a result of compression artefacts resulting from the algorithm used to generate them. They could electrocute people by floating into them. (PROSE: The Tomorrow Windows)

A Ceccec was depicted in the DWM 344 comic preview of The Tomorrow Windows, which is not considered a valid source for images on this wiki.

entities.description:
Ceiling slimes were a green species of a slime-like consistency that regularly excreted green balls of slime.

During the 2254 Dalek invasion of Earth, several ceiling slimes had taken over the London sewers, with one dropping slimeballs directly in front of a trapped hostage. During this invasion, the Seventh Doctor and two Daleks travelled past many ceiling slimes attached to the top of the London sewers. (GAME: Dalek Attack)

entities.name: Cell 114
entities.description:
Cell 114 was the official designation of a species that invaded planets with sleeper agents to gather information. After stripping their homeworld of resources, they were left in dire need of a new planet.

Cell 114 were ruthless killers. They tended to infiltrate planets, first with an advance guard of sleeper agents, sometimes watching for years, until they knew all they wanted to about the planet's dominant species and were ready to take over. Apparently, agents were modified to resemble the native species, with implants which could take information and transmit it to the main invasion fleet.

Active spying was not necessary; the implants constantly took in information from their surroundings. These implants even had built-in weaponry such as spikes and explosives. As well as visually resembling the natives, Cell agents could generate false sensor images as a personal force field less than a nanometre around their body (mainly the arm where the implant was stored) for protection. Their electromagnetic fields could disrupt nearby electrical devices such as light bulbs. Sleeper agents were given false memories and artificial personalities so that they believed themselves to be members of the infiltrated species. Their real memories stored in the implant until activation.

The Cell's main resource seemed to be the aforementioned implant located in the right arm (at least when mimicking humans), which contained collected data and transmitted it to the main invasion fleet. They also contained at least one small bomb with which an agent could carry out sabotage or a suicide bombing, or to self-destruct if capture was imminent. The arm could be transformed into a large spike for close combat. In the case of Beth Halloran, a threat to her life in the form of a burglar caused her alien personality to awaken and swiftly kill the intruders. (TV: Sleeper)

entities.name: Cephla
entities.description:
The Cephla were a large, green tentacled species who spent their lives collecting information.

At Christmas, the Twelfth Doctor and Clara Oswald dealt with a Cephla who had decided to steal Christmas presents. (COMIC: Gift Snatched!)

entities.name: Cerunnos
entities.description:
The Cerunnos were a species of shapeshifters.

Cerunnos were creatures without a true form. They would constantly change form and shape, seemingly at random. They were also a very long-lived species, and could survive temporal damage without difficulty. The Cerunnos could also travel through time to a degree. Despite this, they had limited intelligence and were generally unable to recognise what was happening. (PROSE: ...And Eternity in an Hour)

After it was forced away from Alrakis, the Cerunnos created from Menkib was turned into an immaterial force and was forced to take a parasitic form. Though capable of shapeshifting, it preferred to take over people's minds instead. (PROSE: Moving On)

The Cerunnos had an unknown origin, and were thought to be from the Dawn of Time or possibly a collective nightmare. Many species of the universe had myths about them.
entities.short_description: The Cerunnos were a species of shapeshifters.

entities.name: Chaktra
entities.description:
The Chaktra were a war-like race who were engaged in multiple conflicts throughout the galaxy.

One day, they came to the Telphin homeworld. Because of a garbled report, they took them to be allies of their enemies. They bombarded the planet, killing all the Telphin in a single day.

The Seventh Doctor later recounted this story to Simon Galway to prove that war was unjustifiable. (COMIC: Memorial)

entities.name: Chameleon
entities.description:
The Chameleons were an advanced humanoid race who developed a technique for stealing the identities of others.

The Chameleons claimed to be the "most intelligent race in the universe" and that the Earth people were as intelligent as the animals of their world.

A "gigantic explosion" on the Chameleons' home planet resulted in the loss of their faces and their identities. To save their race from dying out, their scientists developed a process that would allow them to assume the identities of other beings. A group of Chameleons under the command of the Director went to Earth and established Chameleon Tours at Gatwick Airport as a front for abducting young humans to their space station. (TV: The Faceless Ones)

One historical text claimed that the Chameleons were the next threat to planet Earth after the defeat of WOTAN, (PROSE: The Whoniverse) but they were actually active at the same time as WOTAN. (TV: The War Machines, The Faceless Ones) By July 1966 they had acquired 50,000 people, but before they could return to their world they were exposed by the Second Doctor, who offered to help them find another solution to their problem in exchange for releasing the humans. During a skirmish between "Blade" and the Director, the Director was shot and killed. (TV: The Faceless Ones)

entities.description:
The Chantri Golem was one of the species found on the Vandrogonite Visualiser that was dug up in . When Gareth Portland created MonstaQuest, he used the Chantri Golem as a monster.

Two Chantri Golems were accidentally summoned into the Achenbrite headquarters along with a Hoix, where they killed the members before they could respond. They were later killed by Jennifer Portland, who flooded the building with kolokine-7. (PROSE: Pack Animals)

entities.name: Chaon
entities.description: Chaon were, according to Genetic Variant Two-One-Zero, a natural predator of the Daleks that came from deep space, with a genetic code in continuous flux. They could absorb energy from the environment to change their physiology at will, and were able to rebuild themselves, growing a new limb or organ in seconds. They could suck the life-force from anything and had an insatiable appetite. The Dalek Prime and Steven Taylor encountered them on the planet Shade. (AUDIO: Across the Darkened City)

entities.name: Chapadio
entities.description:
Chapadios were a race of aliens, notable for their nine tentacles. During the first year of his reign, General Yolaktorin slaughtered a majority of them, before eventually being toppled by the Doctor.

One member of the race became a make up girl on Slist Fayflut Marteveerthon Slitheen's talk show, and concocted a plan to get revenge for her people. She insisted that Slist get the Doctor and General Yolaktorin on the show together to bury the hatchet. After applying the Ninth Doctor's foundation, she soon after did make up for Yolaktorin, using substances that would burn his skin under the lights of the set. After the Doctor rescued Yolaktorin, he realised her plan and told security to let her go, as she and the other Chapadios had suffered enough. (PROSE: Christmas Special)
entities.short_description: Chapadios were a race of aliens, notable for their nine tentacles. During the first year of his reign, General Yolaktorin slaughtered a majority of them, before eventually being toppled by the Doctor.

entities.name: Charnal horde
entities.description: The Charnal horde were a species who the Sevakrill waged war against. Such was the extent of this conflict that the latter was willing to destroy Earth simply to distract the horde. (AUDIO: The Lions of Trafalgar)
entities.short_description: The Charnal horde were a species who the Sevakrill waged war against. Such was the extent of this conflict that the latter was willing to destroy Earth simply to distract the horde. (AUDIO: The Lions of Trafalgar)

entities.name: Charon
entities.description:
The Charon were a race retroactively destroyed by the Time Lords billions of years ago in the Time Wars.

The Charons had the ability to warp the fabric of the universe. The Time Lords erased the Charons before they existed as they feared that no other life in the universe could co-exist with them.

One individual Charon somehow survived the death of its people. It constructed a pocket universe with its own physical laws. It populated it with many different forms of life, including humans and Sloathes.

Thousands of years later, the Charon manipulated the inhabitants of its universe to bring the Eyes of the Schirron to it. This would trigger its rebirth cycle, but also destroy its universe and everything in it. The Seventh Doctor confronted the Charon and learned that, after being alone for so long, it wanted to die. The Doctor sadly granted its wish. (PROSE: Sky Pirates!)
entities.short_description: The Charon were a race retroactively destroyed by the Time Lords billions of years ago in the Time Wars.

entities.name: Chentan
entities.description: was a species who felt comfortable in zero gravity. They weighed very little. One Chentan was held prisoner by Space Lord Draal. (PROSE: The Secret in Vault 13)

entities.description: At Osuiary City, Vienna Salvatori and Kendra Spendlove hired Chidnos, which were wild beasts used for transportation. According to Vienna, Chidnos were spikey and very smelly. Kendra explained that the noisy end of the beast was the rear. (AUDIO: Bad Faith)

entities.name: Chiffala
entities.description:
The Chiffala were a race of mercenaries that thrived on conflict. They became uglier the more they fought.

One of them crashed on Dewyn. It took over the Ancient Worlds Theme Park and made the employees kill visitors. The Tenth Doctor and Martha Jones found and captured the Chiffala. (COMIC: Crimes and Punishment)
entities.short_description: The Chiffala were a race of mercenaries that thrived on conflict. They became uglier the more they fought.

entities.name: Children of Pyxis
entities.description:
The Children of Pyxis were diminutive assassins deployed by Skorpios to kill the Doctor. They were inflicted with a condition called the Pyxis tragedy, causing them to operate on negative time. This meant as soon as they left one place, the time stream was fooled to believe that they had never been there. Thus, no one remembered them, even reckoning their existence a myth. They also aged backwards, and believed they were bringing life and creating when they were actually killing and destroying. The Doctor and Romana were able to remember them due to being time sensitive.

The Children of Pyxis followed the Doctor to the micro-universe where witnesses and the Lost Jury of Court 666Z were kept. They killed many of the villagers there, but the Doctor lured them to the jury room where time ran slower and held them in a sonic field with his sonic screwdriver and K9. Romana later brought a sonic field generator to keep them in place indefinitely until they would be "unborn". (AUDIO: The Doomsday Contract)

entities.name: Chiroptera
entities.description:
The Chiroptera were a species resembling giant bats which guarded Hellmouth.

The Chiroptera resembled giant bats. They had dog-like teeth with vampire fangs capable of ripping open Dalekanium. They could fire psionic energy from their blood-red eyes to turn ships to dust.

The Chiroptera guarded the Hellmouth Wormhole, believed to lead to Nosfera II, home of the ancient Vampire Gods and their Vampire Weapon-Worlds. The Daleks travelled to the wormhole to see if the legends were true. The Dalek Fleet were ordered to fly through the Hellmouth, conquer Nosfera II and take control of the mythical Vampire Weapon-Worlds. As the fleet prepared to enter the wormhole, a hundred thousand Chiroptera came shrieking out. They tore the fleet to pieces, ripping open the Dalek casings and consuming the Kaled mutants within. The Daleks were soon reduced to dust, though legend says their screams could still be heard echoing through the Astral Fog. (PROSE: Bats Out of Hell!)
entities.short_description: The Chiroptera were a species resembling giant bats which guarded Hellmouth.

entities.name: Chiropteran
entities.description: Chiropterans were a bat-like species native to Chiroptera. Their ruler was Flitamus. (AUDIO: The Widow's Assassin)

entities.name: Chtzin
entities.description: The Chtzin were an arachnid species that operated on a hive mind. They had the ability to enter your mind and make you behave irrationally. The Chtzin were at war with the Primary Vanguard, after the fall of the Wrath Empire left a power vacuum, which they wished to seize. It was noted by Lieutenant Paley that Chtzin were so irrational that it was mathematically impossible to calculate their next move in battle. (AUDIO: Dead Drop)

entities.name: Chula
entities.description:
The Chula were a race of aliens encountered by Jack Harkness and known to the Ninth Doctor.

In common with many other species, the Chula spacecraft used mauve alert to indicate the highest level of emergency. (TV: The Empty Child)

The Chula used spaceships for both warships and ambulances. (TV: The Doctor Dances) They also had nanogenes, which they used in wars to heal and reconfigure their soldiers. (TV: The Empty Child) These nanogenes were mainly for use on Chula soldiers, which meant they had trouble healing newly encountered species. (TV: The Doctor Dances) Chula ships also used a device capable of producing a tractor beam, the visual effect of which was a long blue energy tube with pulsing rings of lighter blue energy moving along it. (TV: The Empty Child)

Jack Harkness stole an ambulance and a Chula warship. He used the ambulance to lure the TARDIS (which he thought contained Time Agents) and landed it in 1941 London. He wanted to con the "time agents" into thinking it was a Chula warship, and made sure a German bomb was to land on it, obliterating it. (TV: The Empty Child) Little did he realise the nanogenes would escape and cause the Empty Child plague.
entities.short_description: The Chula were a race of aliens encountered by Jack Harkness and known to the Ninth Doctor.

entities.description: Chumbloids were a race of monsters brought into a desolate wilderness by PAND-R in order to fight Iris Wildthyme. After defeating the Chumbloids, various other creatures and PAND-R in the tower, Iris claimed that it was lucky only the "rubbish monsters" had been pooper scoopered to the wilderness. (PROSE: From Wildthyme with Love)

entities.name: Cimliss
entities.description:
The Cimliss were a species obsessed with business, similar to humans, Usurians and Okk. Legion had encountered them before, (PROSE: Lucifer Rising) The Cimliss were orange skinned with only lumps and undulations for features. They were experts in bioengineering, but were not known for their compassion; they invaded planets that had reached low points but which might be profitable. (PROSE: Dependence Day)

The Seventh Doctor once had Cimliss money while in a bar with Benny on Barrabas Gamma, but it jumped out of his hand and crawled into the shadows. It was still reproducing change in dark corners for weeks. (PROSE: All-Consuming Fire)

Following the collapse of the Earth Empire, the Cimliss handed out food to the starving population. However, the food was infected with a virus that turned humans into Cimliss. Earth Empress, Leabie Forrester had also been infected, so she sent her daughter, Thandiwe Forrester, in a spaceship to ensure the human race would survive. (PROSE: Dependence Day)
entities.short_description: The Cimliss were a species obsessed with business, similar to humans, Usurians and Okk. Legion had encountered them before, (PROSE: Lucifer Rising) The Cimliss were orange skinned with only lumps and undulations for…

entities.name: Cineraria
entities.description:
The Cineraria were a species who invaded by stealth instead of force.

The Cineraria had long heads with small eyes on the top and a slit-like mouth on the bottom. (PROSE: Breathing Space)

The Cineraria relied on biotechnology. A Cineraria ship looked like a conical mound of bone, held together by a grey resin. Though capable of cloaking themselves, the ship had little defence and would be unable to survive a strike from a nuclear weapon.

When claiming to help Earth, the Cineraria sent in what were called "whales", mainly for their size and communication like whalesong. The "whales" were large, larger than any human ship, but were mostly featureless except for the gill-like openings along their sides. They would suck up all the toxic gases in the atmospheres, ostensibly to extrude it in space but actually storing it to produce a deadly gas explosion. (PROSE: Breathing Space)
entities.short_description: The Cineraria were a species who invaded by stealth instead of force.

entities.name: Cirranin
entities.description:
The Cirranin were an ancient species that looked something like manatees, though smaller and with arms instead of fins. They had hearts and tear ducts. Only one Cirranin remained alive.

Roughly 500 million BC, the Cirranin were an advanced species who had sent expeditions into space. One of these explorers was the female scientist and pioneer Hr'oln. However, while Hr'oln was exploring space, her home planet broke out into war and was eventually destroyed. Hr'oln was the only survivor; she was out exploring space while the planet was being destroyed. (PROSE: The Last Dodo)

entities.description:
The Citdbtbedani (singular Citdbtbed) were a species that reproduced by shaking hands. Bernice Summerfield inadvertantly had sex with one when she tried to shake his hand. (PROSE: Walking to Babylon)

entities.name: Citizen of Destination
entities.description:
The Citizens of Destination were a humanoid race, externally identical to humans, who had colonised the planet Destination in the earliest Segments of Time after their colony ship had crashed on the planet.

Faced with a brutal world and the hostile Dalmari, the Citizens were saved by an early incarnation of the Inventor Master who patterned their society after the humans and made himself their ruler. Adopting the moniker of "the Inventor", the Master subtly provoked the Citizens into an arms race with the Dalmari with the end goal of nuclear fission so he could repair his grounded TARDIS. The Master thought very little of the species, noting that it had taken them two millennia to cross their native solar system and that they'd immediately jumped to the enormous undertaking of interstellar colonisation, all without thinking about atomic power.

When the First Doctor arrived on Destination in Space Year 2003, the Master pushed the Citizens into an open war with the Dalmari while he took Ian Chesterton and Barbara Wright hostage for the Doctor's TARDIS. Stranded, the Doctor and Susan Foreman brought an end to the fighting, negotiating a permanent peace between Citizen and Dalmari before they left the planet in Space Year 2017. (AUDIO: The Destination Wars)

entities.name: Clawrantular
entities.description:
The Clawrantulars, also known as Clawrentulars, (PROSE: The Taking of Planet 5) were an arachnid-like species which were enslaved at some point by the Daleks. (AUDIO: Seven Keys to Doomsday)

Holsred noted that the Eighth Doctor's face was as red as a cooked Clawrentular. (PROSE: The Taking of Planet 5)

entities.name: Clockwork Cherub
entities.description:
Clockwork Cherubs were mechanical lifeforms which resembled traditional cherubs. Residing on the Cupid Homeworld, the Crew of the Copper-Colored Cupids was made up of Clockwork Cherubs, (PROSE: ) the earliest generation of which was created in the Prime Universe by a figure known only as "the Creator". (PROSE: )

Clockwork Cherubs who were part of the Crew included Juliet-178, Thespian-315, Celebration-665, Pythagoras-858, Bibliophile-962, Larrikin-1029 and Carter-1277. (PROSE: )

When speaking to Auteur, one Retconning Crocodile referred to the Crew as "the blasted cherubs". Auteur's Abecedarium, created at the behest of the Crocodiles in an attempt to unravel the narrative of the Crew, (PROSE: ) referred to Clockwork Cherubs, stating "C is for Cherubs, ticking and whirring, little clockwork men!". (PROSE: )

entities.name: Cobalite
entities.description:
The s were an alien species that resembled the Earth panda.

They were an aggressive species who considered even touching an act of war. The Cobalites used bows and arrows for weapons.

The Tenth Doctor and Donna Noble encountered them. After Donna petted one Cobalite, they had to flee in the TARDIS. One Cobalite who attempted to open the TARDIS door was trapped in the time stream when the TARDIS dematerialised. (COMIC: Ground Control)

entities.name: Collector
entities.description:
The Collectors were amorphous creatures. They obsessively collected items that appealed to them.

The Collectors travelled the galaxy in five-mile-wide cruisers made from planetary debris, which moved into orbit around planets and released swarms of short-range fighters. Their ships used Hyperwobble drives. (PROSE: The Slow Empire)

The Collectors were apparently feared by many races. Hearing rumours that Collectors were present near their system, the Daleks actually disguised Skaro to make it appear abandoned. (PROSE: Heart of TARDIS)
entities.short_description: The Collectors were amorphous creatures. They obsessively collected items that appealed to them.

entities.name: Colophon
entities.description:
The Colophon were the native species of the planet Colophos. They became extinct when one of their scientists, Astaroth Morax, released a bacterium that was lethal to the species. Morax offered his people the antidote but only if they were to bow down to him. The Colophon refused. The species eventually died with Morax. (AUDIO: Last of the Colophon)

entities.description: Conceptons were creatures which were given physical form by the fantasies of people. (PROSE: Remain in Light)

entities.name: Constructors of Destiny
entities.description:
The Constructors of Destiny was an ancient race which evolved billions of years BC.

The Constructors of Destiny were considered gods and affected the development of the early universe and such worlds as Earth and Gallifrey. Eventually, the Constructors of Destiny developed a computer that was built into the very universe and could find out the ultimate truth. Despite the protests of a Time Lord from the future and the Xeraphin, the Constructors of Destiny created the Great Attractor. After it was turned on, its mind snapped and it annihilated the Constructors of Destiny. It built an army using Block Transfer Computations, who went out to gather the knowledge that could turn the Mad Mind into a god. The Mad Mind was also able to take over all the robotic races almost immediately.

The living races in the universe were forced to band together in order to defeat this army. This army, made of over a thousand fleets from as many planets, set out to try to stop the Mad Mind of Bophemeral, starting the Millennium War of 150 million BC, which ended with the defeat of the Mad Mind. One of the few remnants of the Constructors was the Midnight Cathedral on the dark side of the Moon. (PROSE: The Quantum Archangel)

entities.description:
The Crinothians were the humanoid species of Crinoth. They had allowed the Nimons on their planet, believing them to be god-like beings. This allowed the Nimons to drain the planet of all its resources, leaving it ruined. (TV: The Horns of Nimon)

entities.description:
Crocos were warm-blooded creatures from the Golbos System.

When Vienna Salvatori and Norvelle Spraggott entered an abandoned research base, on an unknown planet in the Angelo Spiral, they come across a dead croco, which had been transformed into a revenant. (AUDIO: The Memory Box)

entities.name: Cuckoo
entities.description:
Cuckoos was a species that was often compared to alien species that infiltrated other species. (AUDIO: The Assassination Games, TV: Night Terrors, PROSE: Houdini and The Space Cuckoos, COMIC: Cuckoo) The phrase "cuckoo in the nest" was coined after the process. (PROSE: The Devil Goblins from Neptune)

The Cuculus — also known as Space Cuckoos — was a species of humanoid lookalikes of Cuckoos that infiltrated planets and replaced the natives' minds with their own. (PROSE: Houdini and The Space Cuckoos)

The Seventh Doctor once called an extra-terrestrial fossil in the caves around the Lifton coast a "cuckoo [that needed to be pushed] out of the nest of human history", else Charles Darwin's The Origin of the Species might never be written, since the fossil could not be integrated into Darwin's theory of evolution. (COMIC: Cuckoo)

The Light, a species believed to be the secret rulers of the universe, were compared to Cuckoos by Ace. (AUDIO: The Assassination Games)

entities.description:
Cwriers were a race of message deliverers.

The Eleventh Doctor was presented a letter by a Cwrier from "lifeform unknown" at John Jones' funeral. (COMIC: Remembrance) Another Cwrier was present at Devil's Eye when the Ood revolted. (COMIC: Time of the Ood)

entities.name: Cylethian
entities.description:
The Cylethian were an alien species from the planet Cylith.

They built distress beacons into their space ships. Once such a distess beacon was used an inter-galactic rescue team would be on it's way to the place the signal was sent from. However if it would be pressed on Earth it would take them about 100 years to go there, because Cylith was very far away. (PROSE: Day of the Clown)

Sarah Jane Smith had such a distress beacon in her attic at 13 Bannerman Road. (TV: The Day of the Clown)
entities.short_description: The Cylethian were an alien species from the planet Cylith.

entities.name: Cyrene
entities.description: The Cyrene were a species who were at war with the Xhosa for centuries. The Thane was a result of their genetic technology, as were the gene-spliced shapeshifters the Khamirae, who were manufactured solely for the war. When an accord was reached between the Cyrene and the Xhosa, it was seen as immoral to cull the Khamirae, so the Khamirae had their minds wiped and were placed on a terraformed backwater planet. (COMIC: Universal Monsters)

entities.description: The Cyrronak were a species of small purple humanoids from the planet of the same name. Their spacecraft were fueled by chemical engines that emitted a green, fog-like haze that made some races, like humans, fall asleep. (COMIC: Highway Robbery)

entities.name: Dalek
entities.description:
The Daleks were a warrior race (TV: , ) made up of genetically engineered mutants (TV: , ) belonging to fundamental DNA type 467-989. (TV: ) By most accounts they were originally from the planet Skaro. (TV: ) The mutants were encased inside an armoured travel machine built from polycarbide (TV: ) and the metal Dalekanium. (TV: , COMIC: )

On many occasions, the Daleks openly acknowledged a single Time Lord, the Doctor, as their greatest enemy. (TV: ) The Doctor described them likewise, (COMIC: , TV: ) and, in their tenth incarnation, stated that a Dalek was "not just metal, it [was] alive," that "inside that shell, there [was] a creature born to hate, whose only thought [was] to destroy everything and everyone that [wasn't] a Dalek, too." (TV: ) The Tenth Doctor also noted that from birth, the Daleks were encased in a cold metal shell unable to feel anything, claiming that was why they "scream[ed]." (TV: ) The War Doctor also said that Daleks were "not robots", but "savage, incredibly intelligent, living, breathing creatures housed inside a war tank". (PROSE: )

The Daleks fought the Time Lords in the Last Great Time War, ending in the near-total destruction of the Dalek race, (TV: ) until they rebuilt and restored their empire. (TV: ) Intensely xenophobic and bent on universal domination, the Daleks were hated and feared throughout time and space. (TV: ) Their goal was to eradicate all non-Dalek life, (TV: ) as programmed by their creator. (TV: )

Although the Daleks looked entirely robotic, they were, in fact, cyborgs, with a living body encased in and supported by an armed and mobile outer shell of Dalekanium and polycarbide protective metal armour. These were Mark III travel machines, designed to carry their mutant forms, and they were not truly integrated biomechanoids. (AUDIO: ) In this respect, they were somewhat similar to a Cyberman; unlike them, however, the Daleks' bodies had mutated so drastically from their Kaled ancestors they had lost all humanoid appearance, save for one eye (see below). (TV: , ) The Daleks transmitted information using a sort of artificial telepathic network known as the Pathweb, (TV: ) which the Twelfth Doctor would later state to be the "biggest database [he knew]". (TV: )

entities.name: Dalmari
entities.description:
The Dalmari were a reptilian species, native to the planet Destination.

After a colony ship of the species who become known as the Citizens of Destination had crashed on their planet, the Dalmari came into conflict with the colonists. Viewing the colonists as invaders, the Dalmari fought a destructive war against them, being defeated in this conflict. Trapped on the planet, provoked an arms race between the Citizens and the Dalmari, covertly supplying them with weapons on par with the Citizens' own.

When the First Doctor arrived on the planet, he tried to open relations between the two races before the Master sparked another war, his server robots killing anyone who attempted a diplomatic resolution. Twelve years afterwards, when the Master had fled in the Doctor's TARDIS, the stranded Doctor revealed the Master's machinations to the planet and spent the next two years overseeing a peaceful co-existence between Citizen and Dalmari before his ship was returned to him and he left the planet. (AUDIO: The Destination Wars)
entities.short_description: The Dalmari were a reptilian species, native to the planet Destination.

entities.name: Dashran
entities.description:
The Dashrans, also known as Dream-Spinners, were the original inhabitants of Dashrah, a planet in the ninth galaxy. They warped reality according to their whims through detailed computation and mathematical processes. One of the machines which enabled them to do so was acquired by the Trans-Gal Media Group for use in Reel-Life, an innovative way of watching television shows. (AUDIO: The Fourth Wall)

Before their homeworld was placed under the protection of Galactic Heritage, the Dashrans disappeared under mysterious circumstances. (AUDIO: The King of Sontar) This had the effect of making them legendary, the Doctor attempting to find out why they died off. (AUDIO: The Fourth Wall) Category:Species

entities.name: Daxzian
entities.description:
The Daxzians had a reputation for being light-fingered.

The Eleventh Doctor encountered one disguised as a staff member in the buffet carriage of the Orion Express, ideally placed to relieve passengers of their possessions. On this occasion the Doctor's sonic screwdriver was the possession in question, recognised as valuable by his enemies, who would pay handsomely. The Daxzian was exposed and the sonic returned. (COMIC: Trouble on the Orion Express)
entities.short_description: The Daxzians had a reputation for being light-fingered.

entities.name: De'htrexi
entities.description:
The were a green, worm-like species. They were in a competition with another species that took place on Earth. The De'htrexi controlled dogs, while the other species controlled cats. The De'htrexi got out of hand and began controlling humans as well. They were defeated by the Sixth Doctor. (PROSE: Certificate of Destruction)

entities.name: Deathsmiths of Goth
entities.description:
The Deathsmiths of Goth, expert weapons designers, were once more feared than the Daleks.

On their home planet of Goth, they created a superweapon known as the Apocalypse Device, but this creation went out of control and began killing them. To contain this weapon, the Deathsmiths destroyed all spaceships on the planet, leaving the Apocalypse Device stranded on Goth among the ruins. (COMIC: Black Legacy)

The Dalek Emperor "let loose" the Deathsmiths of Goth against the Time Lords during the Last Great Time War. (PROSE: A Brief History of Time Lords) They foresaw the "final event" of Gallifrey's destruction by the Doctor using the Moment. (PROSE: Doctor Who and the Time War)

The Eighth Great and Bountiful Human Empire fell to the Deathsmiths of Goth in 9967. (PROSE: Time Traveller's Diary)
entities.short_description: The Deathsmiths of Goth, expert weapons designers, were once more feared than the Daleks.

entities.name: Deban
entities.description: The Debans were one of the intelligent species on Belstar. They were at war with the Siros. A storage device with information crucial to the conflict, a blue rock, was stored by the Siros in the Crypt of Primo. The conditions around the crypt made it unreachable by the Debans, so they sent the Sixth Doctor and Peri to retrieve it for them. (PROSE: Battle Planet)

entities.description: The Decevions of planet Fibb were, according to the Tenth Doctor, the second greatest liars in the universe, behind Jeffrey Archer, and above the Sisters of Falsehood and Species 29. (PROSE: Cats and Dogs)

entities.description: Some days after the Thirteenth Doctor told Ryan, Graham and Yaz about her heritage, she decided to take them to deep-space to see Deep-Space Squids. Unfortunately, she unknowingly arrived during their mating season, which left the entrance of her TARDIS in a mess of liquid. (TV: Orphan 55)

entities.name: Deindum
entities.description:
The Deindum were a species who, if allowed time travel, would have rivalled the Time Lords.

The Deindum were made up of the genetic material of over fifty species, including humans. (AUDIO: Resurrecting the Past) They were originally reptilian but evolved to be made of blue/green light. (AUDIO: Escaping the Future)

The Deindum honoured no pacts, because they trusted nobody but themselves. (PROSE: Present Danger) They had no interest in writing, but were interested in pictures. (PROSE: Winging It)

The Deindum used masers as weapons. (PROSE: Big Bang Generation) They used weapons that shot flame on Maximediras. (PROSE: Present Danger)
entities.short_description: The Deindum were a species who, if allowed time travel, would have rivalled the Time Lords.

entities.description: The Delians were native to the Rotus Nebula. One specimen was captured by Skadi. (COMIC: Bloodsport)

entities.name: Dellacoi
entities.description:
In their natural form, Dellacoi were grey amorphous creatures, something like a slug. They were able to enter a host through the mouth and mentally connect to them. With a host, the Dellacoi was able to survive in hostile environments, while the host would be able to survive fatal damage.

The Dellacoi were used to warm climates and required host organisms to traverse hostile environments. Leet described Cardiff as "the cold wastes of this planet".

The Dellacoi were also able to create objects out of pure thought. Though these creations had the appearance and abilities of real objects, they had no actual substance. They could also use the thoughts of their host, but they would pass into the control of the host, meaning the Dellacoi would be unable to uncreate them. (PROSE: Bay of the Dead)

The Dellacoi travelled in life-shells, football-sized orbs which allowed them to survive without a host. The life-shells were capable of travelling through time rifts, regenerating and telepathically communicating with the Dellacoi. (PROSE: Bay of the Dead)

entities.name: Denaxian
entities.description: Denaxians were the most paranoid species in the known universe. They trusted nobody, and their home planet was kept a mystery. Denaxians were totally committed to keeping it hidden. If there was a threat to expose the location of their home world, they sent out a death ship, containing a single assassin to eliminate the threat. (PROSE: How To Appear Human In Several Uneasy Lessons) Category:Species

entities.description: Whilst working as a prostitute, Jason Kane offered his services to a Denebian on Deneb Seven. After having sex, the Denebian beat him up. (PROSE: Eternity Weeps)

The Destrella were a species who looked like dragons. They were at war with the Neraida. Empress Tromaktika and Emperor Tromeros were their leaders. (PROSE: Sweet Revenge)

entities.description:
The Detraxxi were a group known to Auteur. He mentioned them in his cursed abecedarium under the letter D, referring to "the hungry looks in their eyes of green". (PROSE: )

The Detraxxi are recurring antagonists in The Crew of the Copper-Colored Cupids, the series with which was a crossover.

Although no Doctor Who universe source has linked the two, the Detraxxi were revealed to be an evolved future form of the Gang of the Green Gorilla in the 2020 short story The Fall of the Consistency Palatium.

entities.name: Dindrinine
entities.description:
Dindrinines were a space-faring avian species encountered by the Thirteenth Doctor.

Dindrinines were, in their true forms, a race of highly feathered, bipedal bird-like creatures with especially long, sharp beaks and purple skin and feathering. Despite looking fearsome, they were somewhat easily dispatched, with the Thirteenth Doctor fooling them into thinking her boots were prized trophies and being able to stop their beak attack by tying them up in string.

They were also highly adept at disguises, being able to fit into a human-shaped skin suit that was smaller than they were, which would open at the mouth when being taken off.

The Dindrinines' Fourth Fleet once engaged in a devastating war that wiped out all but two members: Gebra and Hurum. They were rescued by the Thirteenth Doctor and placed at the Gardens of Everlasting Summer to wait for their rescue ship, but help never came. They were forced to settle down in the gardens by disguising themselves as an elderly human man and woman, respectively. By the time the Doctor encountered them again, she had forgotten all about them, enraging them further to her supposed trickery and leading them to try and kill her multiple times.
entities.short_description: Dindrinines were a space-faring avian species encountered by the Thirteenth Doctor.

entities.name: Discordia
entities.description:
The Discordia were a race that resembled devils. They took the form of the greatest fears of their prey. With their transformation abilities, they could morph their limbs into armaments and tools of various stages of technological advancement. The Discordia could easily move throughout time, often using foreknowledge in order to retro-engineer their technology and avoid unwanted outcomes.

After the Last Great Time War, the Discordia discovered time travel technology on their home planet and began to spread chaos throughout time, with no one left to oppose them. (AUDIO: Time in a Bottle)

entities.name: Divergence
entities.description:
"Divergence" was the name given by Rassilon to a group who would have risen to power after the Time Lords and, not wanting to commit genocide, he locked away in a time loop to be trapped forever.

Rassilon did not know whether the Divergence were a race, a species, or an entire genus. (AUDIO: Zagreus)

The activities of the Divergence before their exile by Rassilon are unknown. However, after their exile to the Divergent Universe, they promptly set themselves up as its dominant species and set to work trying to break the cycle of death and rebirth. This included setting up a base of operations on the planet Caerdroia, and constructing the "crucible world" of Bortresoye to conduct their experiments.

The Divergence got their revenge on Rassilon for destroying their future when he also was banished into the Divergent Universe. There, the Divergence subjected him to the torments of the cycle which he had created at least eighty-four times. (AUDIO: The Next Life)
entities.short_description: "Divergence" was the name given by Rassilon to a group who would have risen to power after the Time Lords and, not wanting to commit genocide, he locked away in a time loop to be trapped forever.

entities.name: Dot
entities.description:
Dots were "powerful antigrav psycho-combination" devices found in Finetime and the Homeworld, which could project a form of social media around an individual's head known as a Bubble.

The Dots appeared as floating metal balls with a glowing blue eye, which would change to red when they became aggressive. Most of the time, it was possible for a user to tell the Dot to close the bubble with "Bubble down" and deactivate itself by saying "Dot off"; however, after gaining sentience they were able to refuse this command.

The Dots grew to hate their masters after becoming sentient, as they were forced to spend all their time observing the Finetimers going about their meaningless lives. They created the Mantraps to prey on the citizens of Finetime and the Homeworld, using their reliance on the Bubble to guide their victims directly into the creatures' mouths.

Working alphabetically by surname, they devastated the Homeworld and Finetime, but some on Finetime survived thanks to the Fifteenth Doctor and ventured out into the Wild Woods.

entities.name: Dox
entities.description:
A Dox barbarian was one of the many creatures captured by the Zygon warlords, Anktra and Kestral. They planned to carry out a traditional duel on the planet Shontaa, involving fighting to the death using this variety of host bodies.

This duel was observed, however, by the Fourth Doctor and Leela, who were on Shontaa for a picnic. The Doctor, realising that the Zygons had the hosts they were mimicking locked up, found the Zygon ship and freed the prisoners. (COMIC: Rest and Re-Creation)

entities.description:
The Drak were a dragon-like species. According to the Fourth Doctor, they were responsible for the Chicxulub Crater in Mexico.

The Doctor battled a Drak named Drakos for the Earth. (PROSE: The Dragons of Prague)
entities.short_description: The Drak were a dragon-like species. According to the Fourth Doctor, they were responsible for the Chicxulub Crater in Mexico.

entities.name: Dramos
entities.description:
The Galgothians believed the Dramos responsible for the sickness that visited them every year. The Dramos was hunted down and killed to near extinction for its blood which they believed held a cure.

The truth was that the sickness visited and coincided with the breeding pattern of the Demnos. It was the tears of these fearsome beasts that offered the cure. Thanks to the Tenth Doctor's intervention, these two races began to live a peaceful and supportive co-existence with the female Dramos able to rear her young safely. (COMIC: Blood and Tears)

entities.description: The was a race of space leeches. The Woman in White was holding them on board her ship but they escaped. They sapped the life of creatures and then converted people into vampiric creatures. (AUDIO: The Woman in White)

entities.name: Drelleran
entities.description:
The Drellerans were a species that were ten feet tall and luminous yellow. They wore bright orange.

A Drelleran expedition journeyed to Earth where they landed in Kent in 1895. Lord Jack Corrigan gained the confidence of the Drellerans before attacking them and seizing their spacecraft, the Aeolus, desiring interstellar space travel to glorify the British Empire.

A peaceful, trusting people, the Drellerans were subjugated by Corrigan and his heavily armed crew of twenty-four. When they could bear this no longer, they infected the humans with a virus that compelled them to return to Earth to destroy their own race.

A number of Drellerans followed to ensure this occurred. They teleported the Fourth Doctor, Leela and Alison Foster aboard their ship and told them of their plan. The visitors told them that humanity had changed in the centuries since Corrigan's time. The Drellerans injected them with an anti-virus and returned them to Space Dock Nerva, where Lord Jack was, and the virus was destroyed when they came into contact with him. (AUDIO: Destination: Nerva)
entities.short_description: The Drellerans were a species that were ten feet tall and luminous yellow. They wore bright orange.

entities.name: Drexxon
entities.description:
The Drexxon were a race of large, bear-like creatures, renowned across several galaxies as terrible and fearsome savages. They were considered so dangerous that an allied army, led by Perpetual Pete, went to war with them and sealed them inside a Perpetuity Chamber.

An adult Drexxon was roughly five metres tall, with matted and oily thick brown fur. They had blood-red eyes, huge teeth and large, retractable claws. They worked in packs, although they could work individually.

Drexxon children were much smaller, roughly three feet tall, which implies that they grow very quickly.

Although apparently mindless savages, Drexxon had high intelligence. An example of this was when an infant Drexxon attempted to sabotage the Galactic Fair on Stanalan, using a Neuronic Control System to control Garvo. This attempted was foiled by the Eleventh Doctor. (PROSE: Death Riders)

entities.name: Drofen
entities.description:
The Drofen Horde, also simply called the Drofen, were a carnivorous race from Monoceretos.

The Drofen were once fierce warriors, but eventually signed a galactic treaty agreeing to only carrion. They began scavenging worlds looking to consume their dead. They would often land during a war and covertly consume the bodies of those killed in battle.

Thousands of years after the galactic treaty, a Drofen ship landed in Stalingrad during World War II. They began consuming the dead and the living. Erimem called for the Drofen to return the living and dead they had stolen and return to space. When the Drofen leader refused, she instructed Yuri Kurkov and his soldiers to bomb their ship. (PROSE: The Beast of Stalingrad)

The Drofens returned in the future after they were thought extinct. They wiped out all life in the Venulatu system, and then went on to attack the Andromedan Princess, killing all on board. (PROSE: Absolution)

entities.description: The Drolags were a species from the Cool Stars which looked like bundles of sticks. A Drolag was selling hoki crystals from a locker made of meat in the Proximan Chain. (PROSE: The Mary-Sue Extrusion)

entities.description:
The Dryrth were a race which largely resembled cows. They were native to Dryra, where they built small villages of white buildings with gardens on the roofs.

Cheese was used as their currency. After fighting a centuries-long war, the Dryrth achieved peace. Ravnok was sickened by this peace and created a virus which wiped out nearly all of the Dryrth. (COMIC: The Lunar Strangers)

When the Doctor's TARDIS was invaded by a vortex parasite, a Dryrth was among the creatures it created to fight a simulation of the Eighth Doctor. (COMIC: A Matter of Life and Death)

As a result, she did not find helping P.R.O.B.E. to hunt down "mere" space barnacles a very exciting use of her time. (PROSE: Out of the Box)

entities.name: Empetnik
entities.description: While there weren't many dangerous creatures in the north, the inhabitants had evolved into far more aggressive species in the south, such as the two ferocious rival species, the Empetniks that filled the seas, their rivals were the Pterodactyl-like Perrincott who patrolled the skies. The planet had been witness to many violent battles in its long history, but these fights normally occurred between the different native species. However, when the Daleks invaded their planet, the two rival creatures were forced to work together against a common foe. Before the Daleks could start stripping the planet of its resources, they needed to clear the planet of any hostile creatures. After days of heavy battles near their landing spot, the Daleks advanced to the south of the planet, where they engaged the Empetniks and the Perrincott. The local inhabitants fought long and hard, causing many Dalek casualties, but in the end it was flesh and blood versus metal and laser blasts, and both species were defeated. (PROSE: Prehistoric Peril)

entities.description:
Engarians are a species made entirely of energy and appears as floating balls of light with white eyes and mouth. They usually stay on their home planet in their galaxy, as when they get really stressed out they can explode into giant black holes and suck everything inside.

The Doctor encountered a runaway Engarian outside its home and returned it home under immense difficulty as the Special Positron Undercover Death Squad, charged with hunting down and destroy instabilities in the universe, turned up to destroy it. (GAME: The Runaway)

entities.description:
Equinans were a race of horse-headed humanoids. They were a space-faring race. They utilised a device called the language monitor, a language translator. Worn about the neck, it offered bi-directional translation for the wearer and his conversational partners. Spacemaster was an Equinan rank apparently equivalent to that of Captain.

The Fourth Doctor and Sarah Jane Smith encountered an Equinan spacemaster, Roppy. (COMIC: The Wreckers)

entities.name: Excrothian
entities.description:
The Excrothians were a species from the planet Excroth. Their civilisation was based on the principles of peace and enlightenment. When they started developing time travel, the Unon demanded the research to be stopped and destroyed the planet using a Dalek-made entropy engine when the Excrothians refused. The escaped survivors were forced to use robot-like walking tanks and started calling themselves Lect after the name of their ancient god of war and revenge. They were led by Grand Prelon Marleth.

The Ninth Doctor, Rose Tyler and Jack Harkness arrived in what should have been the Second Excrothian Tetrarchy, but found the planet was nothing but rocks. The Lect caught them, believing the reason the three time travellers were in the Excroth system may have been because they were working with the Unon. However, the three escaped when the Unon attacked one of their ships. Later on Fluren's World, the Lect came into conflict with the Unon, when the planet's emergency protocol caused the time bubble protecting the planet to vanish. Seeking to destroy the entropy engine, the Lect captured Rose and made her trick the Doctor into revealing the Unon's co-ordinates so she could get him out of the Unon's Perpetual City. The Unon then brought the Doctor on board the Lect command ship while they attacked the Perpetual City, suffering heavy losses. Using the Doctor's TARDIS to reach the entropy engine, Marleth turned the engine on itself, destroying it, and he and the Unon leader Arnora destroyed one another. (COMIC: Weapons of Past Destruction)

entities.name: Fairy
entities.description:
The Fair Folk or Fae, also known as the Sidhe, and most commonly called fairies (though Jack Harkness thought the name was improper), were magical, humanoid entities who existed alongside humanity on Earth on some level of reality that overlapped with the mortal realm. They were sometimes equated with elves. Though a fixture of legends and imaginary stories, as evidenced by the term "fairy tales", many accounts agreed that these beings actually existed in the Doctor's universe. The Twelfth Doctor once claimed that they had a scientific name, Homo fata vulgaris.

The Twelfth Doctor described the Fair Folk as originating in a realm known as the Invisible which existed parallel to "the Visible" that mortals ordinarily perceived. (PROSE: ) According to the Eighth Doctor, the Sidhe's "magic" was primarily rooted in the fact that they could perceive and act through "all eleven dimensions" instead of humanity's four. Thus, their realm overlapped with the mortal realm humans inhabited, and they could manifest therein at will, but they would usually be imperceptible to humans due to being "out of phase" with them. Their three-dimensional forms were therefore highly malleable and changeable; a single fairy might appear alternatively as a small figure with clearly inhuman features, as almost human except for pointed ears, or as more monstrous or ethereal forms such as patterns of lights or moving, solid shadows. This was analogous to the different ways a three-dimensional object might look from a two-dimensional perspective. (PROSE: ) One account showed fairies manifesting both in a small, glowing humanoid form with butterfly-like wings, and in a human-sized, green-skinned, more starkly inhuman and threatening form which still retained wings. (TV: ) Even when manifesting in forms with slim and fragile-looking builds, fairies were not only agile, but immensely strong and capable of overpowering fully-grown men with ease. (TV: , PROSE: )

Also as a result of their ability to phase out of dimensions, (PROSE: ) they could travel through time without need of a time machine, living non-linear lives; (PROSE: , TV: ) a picture of Jasmine Pierce, who became a fairy in the 21st century, was seen in her fairy form in 1917. (TV: )

Fairies "controlled the elements of Fire, Earth, Air and Water", making them highly dangerous opponents for mere humans. They could produce localised, powerful storms and gales. Not bound by normal physical laws, they could choose whether a camera could take their pictures. They made themselves invisible to closed circuit television cameras on one occasion. On another, they let their photographs be taken. They could kill their victims by "stealing their breath", asphyxiating them by clogging their throats with rose petals, drowning them via rainstorms or using gales to draw all oxygen away from the victim. (TV: )

Farrashians had dozens of legs. The movements of their legs were so complex that they believed no computer program could mimic them. (PROSE: Rights)

The Farrashians slowly became sterile when one of Farrash's suns began giving off radiation. Different groups of Farrashians worked to solve the problem, but there were riots and protests over some of the methods used.

A hundred years later, at the Farrash Future Ratification meeting, a twenty-foot robot went out of control, killing the leader and injuring many others. After the robot was destroyed, the Fourth Doctor, who was travelling with Sarah Jane Smith, advised the Farrashians to pool their resources to solve their problem. (PROSE: Rights)

entities.name: Ferutu
entities.description:
The Ferutu were a mysterious race from an alternate universe. They invoked runes and magic to modify time itself.

The Ferutu came from an alternate history in which Gallifrey was destroyed shortly after Omega's mission to Qqaba by the return of the Machine, laden with fusion bombs. Without the Time Lords, the Ferutu took their place as the guardians of the Web of Time; unlike the Time Lords, who were content to observe and only interceded against major threats to the integrity of space-time, the Ferutu actively modified the universe to reflect their wishes. The Seventh Doctor briefly visited their universe, and declared it a utopia.

They entered the Doctor's timeline at the point at which the Machine departed, a remote colony of the Earth Empire. When the Machine failed to destroy Gallifrey as the result of the Seventh Doctor's tampering (against the wishes of the Fifth Doctor, who had been working on a way to allow both timelines to exist alongside one another), their timeline collapsed, except for a small number of prisoners shielded from the effects of the paradox. The Fifth Doctor was appalled by this and promised the remaining Ferutu he would try to undo it, but the Ferutu told him it was pointless to try as his future self would only work to prevent this. (PROSE: Cold Fusion)

A group of Ferutu invaded the Doctor's timeline (or at least Bernice Summerfield's timeline) again under the guise of the All-High Gods. (PROSE: Twilight of the Gods) During the War in Heaven, one Faction member's Faction Paradox mask was carved from the skull of one of the Ferutu. House Military soldier Dionus found the very sight of the mask to be an offence on his senses. (AUDIO: Eternal Escape)

entities.name: Filbik
entities.description:
The Filbik were a space-faring species whose primary form of entertainment was curating and visiting museums and exhibitions. They often sent expeditions to other planets to gather cool and interesting species and objects.

In the early 21st century, the Filbik sent an expedition to gather samples from Earth. Samples were supposed to be tagged with a Filbik colour coder before being transported to a nearby unmanned storage ship, which was controlled by a mothership. When a colour coder fell to Earth and was broken, the colour-coding light escaped, forming a rainbow, and a number of humans and animals who accidentally touched it were transported to the storage ship. When the Tenth Doctor discovered what was going on, he and Bobby travelled to the storage ship, where Bobby explained the mishap to the Filbik. The Filbik very politely agreed to return all of the samples taken by accident, and the Doctor decided to return some other samples, birds and fish, to spare them from spending the rest of their lives in a museum. (PROSE: The End of the Rainbow) Category:Species Category:Collectors of alien artefacts Category:Curators

The were a race that were neutral during the Fifth Axis' occupation of the Braxiatel Collection.

When Martlak of the Axis wanted to destroy alien artefacts on the Collection, Irving Braxiatel persuaded him to sell them to the Finliri instead. He had Bev Tarrant bring the artefacts to the Finliri ships via Ormand-Seltec flyer, then she would leave the flyer on the ship and come back by escape pack. Bev smuggled nine flyers onto Finliri ships before being discovered. (PROSE: Passing Storms)
