entities.name: Fleshsmith
entities.description:
The Fleshsmiths were a race from legends. They created bodies for their clients. The Seventh Doctor noted they had a reputation as "grave robbers and body snatchers" and were responsible for the disappearance of thousands of spaceships every year - their flesh banks contained captive humans, Draconians, Ice Warriors, Ogrons and even Daleks.

The Fleshsmiths had the technology to create any kind of body, no matter how complex the biology. They were able to fully recreate a Time Lord body, including regeneration capabilities. They had pioneered highly advanced surgical techniques and could transplant body parts with ease, presumably having overcome the problems of tissue rejection. They also used cybernetic implants to control and augment their servants. They could clone humanoids. They could surgically excise memories by altering neural pathways, although this process was inefficient and the memories might resurface, interfering with their control. (PROSE: Prime Time)

The Fleshsmiths were once a beautiful, highly civilised race of great poets and builders, but the formation of the Brago nebula laid waste to Scrantek and they became sterile. The corrosive nature of the Nebula eroded their bodies. They began using transplant surgery to replace damaged body parts. Eventually, their supplies of spare parts on Scrantek were exhausted. They began to kidnap aliens. Any captive too weak or infirm for use in surgery was used to test biological weapons or as food.

entities.name: Fliis
entities.description:
The Fliis were a symbiotic species. In their native form, they were large, green, largely shapeless creatures with limited mobility. They invaded planets with multi-limbed inhabitants and bonded with them, allowing them greater mobility. They also connected to the host's brain with a telepathic trance, making their removal impossible. The control signal operated on a Wi-Fi frequency and, by incorporating a visor into the fashion-wear, a visual link to the controlling body was created.

In the 20th century, the Fliis came to Earth and created Interconnected Clothing Experience, taking the form of leather jackets. The Eleventh Doctor thwarted the invasion by altering the pattern in the programming, setting himself as a new non-human template, causing the Fliis to detach themselves from the human bodies. (COMIC: Fashion Victims)

entities.name: Forsaken
entities.description:
The Forsaken were a species that induced fear in others, then fed on the fear, killing the other being in the process. They could also use the guise of other beings to trick them.

A member of the species landed on a remote island in Singapore during World War II in 1942 and killed several of the soldiers stationed there. It used the form of the Grim Reaper, but also used the guise of Captain Clive Freeman to trick the soldiers.

Its plan was to use the form of one of the soldiers and get onto a rescue boat sent to collect the soldiers and head to a more civilised part of Earth. It was eventually stopped by the Second Doctor, who tricked the Forsaken into feeding on the fear in itself, killing the Forsaken in the process. (AUDIO: The Forsaken)

entities.description:
The Foxkin were a humanoid species that had evolved from foxes on board the colony ship that eventually became the Twist. When they found the original colony, the humans inside it were dead. For generations, they tried to revive them, until they finally succeeded to do so. After that, they started guiding the humans in secret. However, individuals such as Idra Panatar learned of the Foxkin's existence.

When the Twelfth Doctor visited the Twist, he discovered the Foxkin, and helped them integrate into the human society. (COMIC: The Twist)

At some point, a Foxkin played for Hattie Munroe's band. (COMIC: Beneath the Waves)

entities.description:
The were a species of cephalopod-like, tentacled creatures that lived in water and fed on hate and fear. They appeared in Scottish myths and legends as water demons, and one Fuath dwelled near the shore of Moray, taking babies from the women of the kingdom, and seemingly replacing them with its own mouthless, noseless changeling children.

The Fuath was eventually driven out through the combined efforts of the Ninth Doctor, Queen Gruach, King Macbeth and their son Lulach. Its life was spared by Gruach, who wanted it to live on as a reminder to the people of Scotland not to live in fear. (AUDIO: The Curse of Lady Macbeth)

entities.description:
The Galdani were a highly-advanced, ruthless space-travelling alien race. They appeared to be roughly the size of a human, but their bodies were encased from head to feet in a cylindrical armored shell, with just a letter box slot to see out of. They had no arms or visible legs in the human sense, but a single snaking trunk from the mid chest area ended in a huge claw which was capable of crushing a man's throat.

The Galdani were discovered by Brigadier Lethbridge-Stewart and Anne Travers resting in cryo sleep inside their space ship, buried deep below the Australian opal mining town of Coober Pedy. They were awoken by psychic energy harvested from hapless humans who had come into contact with their seductive, hallucinatory devices known as "dream eggs". As with the Malus home world Hakol, the Galdani had learnt how to harness mental energy the same way humans on Earth used electricity. The Galdani were merciless to humans, whom they viewed as little more than cattle. (PROSE: The New Unusual)

entities.description: A Garaman was a creature that thrived on chaos. It was a creature made from pure written language. In 2269, it hid inside the pages of a manual for a space cargo ship nearly leading it to crash. The Eleventh Doctor was able to defeat the Garaman by using the TARDIS' translation circuits to confuse the creature's own identity enabling it to be jettisoned into space. (COMIC: By the Book)

entities.name: Garvak
entities.description:
Garvaks had green scales that were dry and flaky. They had wide nostrils and jagged rows of teeth.

A Garvak named Abel Crumpton destroyed the planet Zantor, killing almost all the Zantorans. He stole the Egg of Abundance, a device that held the genetic template of Zantor. Crumpton planned to use it to repopulate Earth with Garvaks and create a new Garvak empire. He and the Garvaks on Earth were turned into chickens and destroyed when Harry Sullivan switched the Egg of Abundance for an egg in Crumpton's machine. (PROSE: The Man from DOCTO(R))

The Gati were forced off the planet when Bazima altered the DNA of the people to make them strong enough to overthrow the Gati. (PROSE: Transmission Ends)

They and the residents of the planet on which they lived were apparently human, although they were currently at an Elizabethan stage in technology and culture, without any contact with aliens before the Eleventh Doctor arrived. (PROSE: The King's Dragon)

entities.name: Gell guard
entities.description:
Gell guards, also known as Gel Guards, (PROSE: Interference - Book One) were blob-like creatures that Omega created while trapped in a black hole domain made of anti-matter.

They had the ability to travel from Omega's anti-matter universe into that of matter. They were unaffected by gunfire and explosions and could use their claws as weapons to create explosions of their own. (TV: The Three Doctors)

Following many of Omega's first creations escaping the anti-matter universe with the Second Malika, an enraged Omega murdered his remaining creations and heated their flesh into a burning primordial soup from which a more simple servant to his power could be born, the first Gel Guard. (COMIC: Omega)

Under Omega's command they attacked UNIT HQ. They killed a number of soldiers, captured the Third Doctor and his friends, and took them to Omega. (TV: The Three Doctors)

entities.description:
Gengyrians were a species only interested in science. They believed that the Ether was the universe's very foundation, and that it was a random, blowing chaos.

A Gengyrian science crew spotted a huge orange rock falling through the fabric of the universe while they were busy trying to sew up the tear it had made. They took the opportunity to set up a permanent base there. (PROSE: Rough Magic)

They were stopped by the Doctor. The Tenth Doctor later described them as “Nasty things”. (PROSE: Peacemaker)

entities.name: Geramon
entities.description:
The s were the natives of Beedle. They were compulsive practical jokers. They were ruled by an individual known as the High Japester.

When ruins were found on Beedle, both the Knyy'ds and the Mystic Wizards claimed possession, so representatives from both races, as well as an arbiter and Bernice Summerfield, came to Beedle. It was a hoax, however, as the High Japester wanted victims for his practical jokes. When he was found out, he tried to leave the planet, but Demjely smuggled a nuclear bomb aboard his ship, and became the new High Japester. (PROSE: Beedlemania)

entities.name: Geravalon chameleon
entities.description:
Geravalon chameleons resembled Terran chameleons but were larger. They generally had green skin and their heads had human characteristics. Much like normal chameleons, they could change their skin colour to disappear into their surroundings. Absorption of DNA of other organisms could cause a chameleon to become a member of that species. (PROSE: Kiss of Life)

When one chameleon drank the blood of a human prince, Rodrique, she became a human called Sastra. She was mistaken for a slave girl by local man Padros, and later fell in love with Rodrique. When her body began to mutate, the Doctor realised that she was a chameleon native to the planet. To keep her alive, she would require a daily transference of human DNA, which Rodrique agreed to provide with a kiss. (PROSE: Kiss of Life)

entities.description:
Gesaurians were a race of mercenaries who resembled insects. They were naturally bloodthirsty.

The Fourth Doctor was able to recognise Trenix's species on sight after interfering with his DNA coder, which he correctly surmised kept his bloodlust under control. (AUDIO: The Sinestran Kill)

entities.description:
The were, according to Romana I, a race of "intelligent molluscs". They were skilled tacticians. It was their practice to provoke a planet's species to destroy themselves, after which the Glarn would take over the planet for themselves.

When the Glarn wanted to take over Earth, they tested their program on the employees of Morgan Heggarty by sending them offensive emails and telephone calls. This plan provoked the humans to aggression, but the Fourth Doctor and Romana helped the employees defeat the Glarn. (PROSE: The Glarn Strategy)

entities.name: Glass avatar
entities.description:
The glass avatars, or glass people, were a creation of the Testimony Foundation in 5,000,000,012 on New Earth to preserve the memories of humans about to die within a glass-like avatar. These avatars then were brought to the Testimony Foundation to recount their lives' testimony for the people of New Earth to learn from the past. With the memories added to the Testimony Foundation, the abducted humans were returned to their point of death without memory of their abduction in order to preserve the timeline.

The glass avatars were created, under the Testimony Foundation, by Helen Clay in 5,000,000,012 on New Earth. When Captain Lethbridge-Stewart's testimony was added, a timeline error caused by the refusal of both the First and Twelfth Doctors to regenerate caused the Captain to be returned to the wrong decade. To correct this error, the Testimony Foundation abducted the Doctors and the Captain by taking the Twelfth Doctor's TARDIS to their own ship. Here, the Doctors found the Glass Woman who served as the interface for the ship and the glass avatar of Bill Potts.

Upon finding out about the Testimony Foundation and its purpose, the Twelfth Doctor returned Captain Lethbridge-Stewart to nearly the time of his death. When the Doctor and Bill bid each other farewell, Bill allowed the Doctor to regain his memories of Clara Oswald in order to show that Bill's memories within the glass avatar were the same as the Bill the Doctor knew. The glass avatar of Nardole joined the two, and they all embraced before the glass avatars of Bill and Nardole teleported away. (TV: Twice Upon a Time)

The avatars's physical forms were transparent, humanoid bodies. Any given avatar could take the shape and mind of a human whose memories were stored within the Testimony's system as a whole. Forms taken by them included Helen Clay, Bill Potts, Nardole, and Clara Oswald. (TV: Twice Upon a Time)

entities.description:
The Glorp were a species native to the planet Plorp. According to the Thirteenth Doctor, they were fantastic engineers.

They helped the Doctor in fixing her TARDIS, which was malfunctioning after Lizzie accidentally dropped a peanut butter sandwich into a slot in the control panels. Lizzie befriended the smallest of the Glorp, Blorp, who bonded over their shared love of peanut putter sandwiches, and Lizzie smuggled Blorp home in her rucksack. (PROSE: The Runaway TARDIS)

entities.name: Go-Ray
entities.description:
The Go-Rays were the natives of the planet Go-Ray. They were humanoid except for a single wheel instead of legs. They had metal bodies, large eyes and wide mouths.

When the First Doctor, John and Gillian arrived on their planet, Go-Ray police officers arrested them after one of their cardium reactors malfunctioned. The Go-Rays thought the travellers responsible for the accident. The travellers escaped and, making their way to a cave outside the Go-Ray city, acquired mercury to replace the cardium and repair the reactor. The Go-Rays tried to capture them at the cave, but the travellers escaped. The Go-Rays later found them in the reactor room and sealed them in, intending to recapture them, but let them go after the Doctor convinced them that they had repaired the reactor and he was a magician. (COMIC: )

The Go-Rays were among the aliens stuck on Denossus when it was transported to the Time Vortex by the Vortexians. They would remain trapped for over twenty years until the Vortexians were expelled by the Second Doctor. (COMIC: )

entities.name: Golem
entities.description:
Golems were a biologically-modified species of magma forms. They took over any lifeform with which they came into contact and turned that lifeform into a living statue of gold. They were created by the Valnaxi as defenders of their art.

The Golems, however, could only extend themselves to a certain number of lifeforms, so there were a limited number of them. Any life taken over by a Golem immediately became another golem to become a guard. When fighting Wurms, however, Golems were easily destroyed by modified insectoid creatures in the mud shot by the Wurms. Golem victims included a miner and a vulture who stumbled upon a Golem in the 22nd century. (PROSE: The Art of Destruction)

entities.name: Goronian
entities.description:
Goronians were natives of the planet Goron IV. They were about three feet tall and had bright orange skin and green hair. They wore their hair plaited and woven, which Bernice Summerfield assumed was a mark of tribal status.

To Benny their language seemed to consist of repetitions of the word, "Boogie".

The Goronians had the ability to open a conduit from one universe to another, using something that the Braxiatel Collection called a joining stone. However, unknown to them, anyone who travelled from Goron IV to another universe ended up dead and dismembered on the other side. (PROSE: The Door into Bedlam)

entities.description:
The Time Lords prevented their activities before the Time War, but when the war was over they began to run amok. They collected significant historical figures and they would kill anyone or anything as insignificant. A group of Gramoryans travelled to the 16th century to capture King Henry VIII. They were attracted to the time period because had disguised himself as the King, and was proceeding to meddle in history. (AUDIO: Divorced, Beheaded, Regenerated)

entities.name: The Grand Serpent's species
entities.description:
The species of the Grand Serpent was a symbiotic species, composed of a humanoid and also a spiked serpentine creature, which could be psychically manifested outside of their humanoid form. The serpentine creature within could even manifest inside an intended target, and if needed, kill the target upon exit of their body. (TV: Survivors of the Flux)

The species did not sweat, and did not appear to breathe oxygen, as the Serpent was able to survive on an asteroid with no atmosphere. (TV: The Vanquishers)

The Thirteenth Doctor identified this species as a binary demi-species, a very rare form of species in the universe. (TV: The Vanquishers)

Members of this species were accepted as a part of society on Inston-Vee Vinder's home planet, although it is unknown whether or not the planet is the Grand Serpent's original home or merely another of his conquests. (TV: Once, Upon Time)

entities.name: Graske
entities.description:
The Graske were sentient humanoids known for their mischievous behaviour. They were conquerors from the planet Griffoth, though unlike other species they did not take a planet by force. They would instead use their changelings to systematically replace the inhabitants of the planet. This process was quick, with the Graske replacing the individual with the changeling in seconds.

The Graske were small compared to humans and had pebbly brown or orange skin and three tentacle-like features on their heads. They had difficulty speaking other languages, using odd grammar and curt sentences. (TV: Whatever Happened to Sarah Jane?, Music of the Spheres) Individuals were physically similar, leading Mr Smith to suggest that the Graske may have been a clone species like the Sontarans. They hailed from the planet Griffoth. (TV: SJAF 1)

The Groske were related to the Graske, and almost identical to them, with the difference of the Groske's being blue in colour as opposed to the Graske's brownish orange. (TV: Death of the Doctor)

Krislok used a snare cable to take people out of time and put them into Limbo. A snare gun could reverse the process, putting them back in time and space and restoring their timeline. They also used snare cables for capture and a teleportation device for teleportation. (TV: Whatever Happened to Sarah Jane?, SJAF 1)

entities.name: Great Race of Yith
entities.description:
An "eternal" race of aliens was described by H. P. Lovecraft in The Shadow Out of Time. Befitting Lovecraft's nature as a Guardian of the Gate, they actually existed.

Their true physical forms were depicted in the book as "immense rugose cones ten feet high, and with head and other organs attached to foot-thick, distensible limbs spreading from the apexes. They spoke by the clicking or scraping of huge paws or claws attached to the end of their four limbs". However, they were most fearsome for their ability to project their minds through time and take over the bodies of other species. They were constantly at war, eager to expand their dominion and spawn more of their kind.

While working on his manuscript, Lovecraft found himself transported through time by a mysterious orb. During the journey, he caught glimpses of the actual aliens. Emerging in 2023, he warned Giles about them and gave him the manuscript before returning to his own time. (AUDIO: Guardian At The Gate)

The Superiors, who colonised Yith, were also known as "the Great Race". (PROSE: The V Cwejes)

entities.name: Grel
entities.description:
The Grel were a humanoid race of data pirates native to the planet Grellor.

The Grel had bulbous heads and squid-like faces. (PROSE: Oh No It Isn't!) Grel had thick rubbery skin and could lose several layers of epidermis without harm. (PROSE: The Glass Prison)

The Grel afterlife was called Slawcor (PROSE: Oh No It Isn't!) and they worshipped the god Maa'lon. (PROSE: Where Angels Fear)

In a version of history brought about by the Doctor's changes to the timeline, the Grel invaded Earth in the 2150s. Before they landed they released a gas on the planet to make its inhabitants lose all their knowledge. They planned to harness the planet's magnetic core and turn it into a moving library. Bernice Summerfield turned their gas back on them, making them lose all the knowledge they had gathered. Bernice helped them get back to Grellor in exchange for the use of their time travel technology. (AUDIO: The Grel Invasion of Earth)

The Pythia's personal guard, Handstrong, was a Grelladian. (PROSE: Cat's Cradle: Time's Crucible)

The Griffelians were amorphous masses of protoplasm who lived on Griffelian V. When Sarah Jane Smith asked "Tell me something I don't know" to K9 Mark III, K9 took the phrase literally and began to tell her about the Griffelians. (COMIC: City of Devils)

In the Audio Visuals story Subterfuge, Cuthbert was revealed to be a former human who converted himself to a Griffelian and used Griffelian V as a core base of the Conglomerate.

entities.name: Grosche
entities.description:
The Grosche were a violent and carnivorous species with many teeth. They used soft-light disguises to walk amongst other races.

Ilmatar used sympathetic vibrations to burn his audiences and feed the corpses to the Grosche. This was the plan at Cardiff Bay Millennium Hall, but Ilmatar only killed Sigmund Wallfisch. Before then, they ate a Pansian Eargrub and tried to kill Toshiko Sato and Ianto Jones. (AUDIO: Dinner and a Show)

entities.name: Grunt
entities.description:
In the 38th century, Grunts were genetically created humans with low intelligence used for menial tasks. They could become full-grown adults in less than five years. A Grunt numbered 474 was stationed on the Le Verrier space station. They were distinguished by markings on their faces, and due to their limited speech capacity, would be unable to articulate language very well and would frequently leave out words when speaking to someone. Grunts could also be programmed to respond to any physical threat.

Clara Oswald was disgusted by the concept of them. (TV: Sleep No More) Category:Species Category:Artificial beings

entities.description:
Gug-Truckers were a "primordial" species (PROSE: Cat's Cradle: Time's Crucible) who travelled the space lanes in dumper ships which "spewed the galaxy’s industrial and unmentionable residue." (PROSE: Last Rites) They were ruled by a five-eyed "Trucker King of the Space Lanes". (AUDIO: Time Reef, PROSE: Outsourcing)

They notoriously frequented the Pleiax Space Service Station. (PROSE: Cat's Cradle: Time's Crucible)

The Twelfth Master} once viewed some Gug-Truckers in space while he was stranded on Earth. (PROSE: The Duke of Dominoes)

entities.name: Guldreasi
entities.description:
The Guldreasi were a race who attempted to make Earth a slave planet for its war machine.

In the 22nd century, the Guldreasi contacted Susan Campbell to try to gain the human race's trust with a peace treaty. The negotations failed when the Guldreasi detected the Doctor's TARDIS in London, and thought it a trap.

The Eighth Doctor revealed the Guldreasi's plans to make humans a slave race and the Earth Council banished the Guldreasi from Earth. (AUDIO: An Earthly Child)

entities.short_description: The Gurdels were a species whom the Dominators claimed to have conquered prior to 1969. (PROSE: Mutually Assured Domination)

entities.name: Gwanzulum
entities.description:
The Gwanzulum were a species of shapeshifters stranded on the planet Adeki.

In their natural form, the Gwanzulum were large, monstrous heads with muscular, stubby arms and legs.

The Gwanzulum were telepaths who could read their targets' minds and take the form of individuals from their memories. The gwanzulum were parasitic energy leeches, draining life force from and ultimately killing their targets. (COMIC: Planet of the Dead)

The Gwanzulum were the oldest shape-shifting race, predating the Whifferdills and the Kymbra Chimera.

The Haemogoth were a race which joined the Pandorica Alliance in the Total Collapse Event Incident. Their ships were part of the Alliance fleet which travelled to Stonehenge in 102 AD to imprison the Eleventh Doctor within the Pandorica. (TV: The Pandorica Opens)

A family of Haemogoth travelled to New York to eat the greatest burgers ever to have been created. (PROSE: The Forgotten Army)

entities.name: Hajor
entities.description:
The Hajor were a jellyfish-like species that existed in another dimension.

Their home was severely damaged during the Last Great Time War. After the disappereance of the Time Lords, they declared themselves the new Lords of Time. They worked to make the universe stable and smooth out time paradoxes. They allied with Giovanni Lucio since they were sympathetic to his desire for a structured world. The Tenth Doctor helped Valente banish them. (COMIC: The Futurists)

entities.name: Halassi
entities.description:
The Halassi were a species who owned the Halassi Androvar.

When King Hydroflax raided the Halassi Vaults, the diamond was driven into his skull when the Vaults exploded, and the Halassi tasked River Song to retrieve it. (TV: The Husbands of River Song)

entities.name: Halldon
entities.description:
The Halldons were a race of powerful beings responsible for the creation of the Daleks.

The Halldons engaged in a temporal skirmish with the Eternals, which ended with the Time Lords stepping in to put an end to the universe-threatening hostilities. This was one of the only two time wars in which the Time Lords had engaged before the start of their Great Time War with the Daleks themselves, which would end in their destruction. (PROSE: Meet the Doctor)

Per Bryant Anderson's findings, the Halldons conducted a scientific experiment in which they transplanted prehistoric Earth humans to the barren planet Ameron and artifically accelerated their evolution. Within two hundred years, the Halldons' test subjects had advanced to such an extent as to build fearsome weapons which frightened even their Halldon masters.

Realising the experiment was spinning out of control, the Halldons attempted to wipe out the Ameron humans, only for them to defend themselves and retaliate to the point of completely exterminating the Halldons. Free to advance unhindered, the evolved humans, determined to ensure their own survival, continued to evolve and eventually became the Daleks whom the Earth humans feared so greatly. (PROSE: We are the Daleks!)
entities.short_description: The Halldons were a race of powerful beings responsible for the creation of the Daleks.

entities.description:
Harpies were bird-like creatures mentioned twice by Auteur in his cursed Abecedarium, firstly under the letter H where they were described as "preening and squawking" up and down the Interdimensional Black Market's "twisted lane" and then under the letter I where the Black Market was stated to be their "bazaar domain". (PROSE: )

Iris Wildthyme once pondered as to whether she was an archetype, a siren, a witch, a harpy, a femme fatale, or even a Valkyrie from Nordic myth. (AUDIO: Iris Wildthyme Speaks...!)

Mehendri Solon once referred to the Sisterhood of Karn as a "squalid brood of harpies". (PROSE: Mehendri Solon)

entities.name: Harrowkind
entities.description:
The Harrowkind were a primate-like race that the Sanctified empire used as shock-troopers.

The Harrowkind resembled bipedal primates with blonde hair and beards that were tied up at the back of the head and on the chin, and had brown tendon and gristle instead of facial flesh. Harrowkind also had lower mandible tusks, and wore white tops with red shoulder guards, grey trousers and black boots. (COMIC: Rift War!)

The Harrowkind carried energy weapons and knives. Their energy weapons were not very effective against humans, only able to hurt but not kill them. They wore recall devices, grafted onto their skin that allowed them to travel through time rifts. They also rode energy boards which allowed them to fly and manoeuvre easily. (COMIC: Rift War!)

The Harrowkind served as shock troopers for the Sanctified empire.

entities.name: Harvester
entities.description:
The Harvesters were an ancient race of scavengers who scoured time and space for people considered special. Able to interface with the dimension of N-Space for a brief time, they could isolate a location in a reality bubble outside of the real universe and scan for their target, phasing out anything the didn't need. (AUDIO: Wednesdays For Beginners)

On one Wednesday in 2007, the Harvesters began to isolate Jackie Tyler from N-Space. Their intention was that she would ultimately resort to calling Rose Tyler, which would bring the Tenth Doctor to them, giving them the last two time travellers in the universe. This plot was stumbled upon by Jack Harkness as he was observing the Powell Estate. Though Jackie eventually did call Rose, she realised her error and, addressing the Doctor, insisted that he leave before the TARDIS materialised, robbing the Harvesters of their opportunity. (AUDIO: Wednesdays For Beginners)

Travelling back to his past, Jack shared word of the Harvesters to himself when he was still a Time Agent by the name Javic Piotr Thane. In a plan they concocted together, the Harvesters were lured to the bubble universe where the Council that controlled the Time Agency lived in seclusion. Jack then left the Council and their puppet leader Maglin Shank at the mercy of the Harvesters. (AUDIO: Month 25)

s were a bovinoid species with opposable hooves. They were usually vegetarians, avoiding red meat but eating chicken and fish. They were nomadic.

entities.name: Hedron
entities.description:
The Hedrons were an advanced humanoid race, native to the planet of the same name.

When the Hedrons got ahold of a time cannon, technology only Gallifrey was meant to have, they used it cast out genetic microbes that their immune systems had no defence against by jettisoning them into prehistoric Earth. These genetic microbes would have prevented the evolution of humanity, and when the Sixth Doctor and Frobisher discovered this they travelled back to prehistoric Earth to recover the sphere of microbes. The Doctor accidentally broke open the sphere, releasing the microbes into the wild.

On the return trip to Hedron, the Doctor and Frobisher learnt from a recording that the microbes the Hedrons jettisoned with the time cannon had eventually returned to them when a spaceship from Earth crash-landed on the planet. Hedron was contaminated with the toxic genes, and the Hedrons had gone extinct. (COMIC: Time Bomb) Category:Species

entities.name: Helestican
entities.description:
The Helestican were an alien species which had time travel technology. They also built their space ship with time travel technology. In 2015 a Helestican ship was inside the basement of Ross McNamara's school. Ross went into the spaceship. The chronal vapours of the spaceship sent echoes of Ross through time and briefly transporting him to the year 2115. The Twelfth Doctor suggested Ross's echos might be the legendary ghost reported at the school. After exploding Ross's school, the Doctor returned Ross to his home in 2015. (PROSE: Haunted)

entities.name: Helicon
entities.description:
The Helicon were a highly advanced and easily annoyed species and the arch rivals of the Skovox, a highly advanced and belligerent species, with whom they engaged in an interplanetary war.

The two species preferred to conduct their battles by proxy, using robots on innocent planets located between their two star systems, which would end up as radioactive wastelands or previously uncharted asteroid fields. The Skovox created the Skovox Blitzers with the intention of delivering a decisive victory. They proved successful against the Helicon, homing in on their tell-tale particles, until the Helicon found a way to convince the Blitzers that they were their superior officers and that they should attack the Skovox, homing in on their tell-tale Artron emissions. Unfortunately, they neglected to use the word "instead" in their instruction, and the Blitzers turned their fire on both the Skovox and the Helicon.

During the resulting chaos, all the Skovox who knew the shutdown codes for the Blitzers were lost, and whenever the Skovox or the Helicon tried to command the Blitzers to shut down they self-destructed with catastrophic consequences, as each carried enough explosive to destroy a planet. The final result of the conflict was a large empty patch in the galaxy where their two solar systems used to be. Most of the Blitzers were destroyed but a few survived, awaiting new orders whilst drifting through space. They continued to scan for Helicon and Artron emissions in the hope of finding new targets. The Skovox-Helicon war was covered by historians who had been allowed access to the "Monster Vaults" of the databanks in the Doctor's TARDIS, whom reported the belief that there remained over 800 Blitzers still fighting the conflict. (PROSE: )
entities.short_description: The Helicon were a highly advanced and easily annoyed species and the arch rivals of the Skovox, a highly advanced and belligerent species, with whom they engaged in an interplanetary war.

entities.name: Helicron
entities.description:
The Helicron had a nervous system, which happened to be incompatible with the Cyberon matrix. At least one Helicron was large and strong. (PROSE: A Worthy Successor)

The Helicrons had weapons, which included matter guns and skull crushers. (PROSE: A Worthy Successor)

By 2011, a Helicron, a matter gun, and a skull crusher was stored in the Vault, the original site located under the Cheviot Hills. According to director Vanessa Hardcastle, the matter gun had accidentally disintegrated two humans, Patricia and Zufran; as Vanessa believed that as the duo had no families, and that the "relevant procedures" had been carried out, the deaths weren't worth reporting. This prompted Patsy, from P.R.O.B.E., to send Giles and Archie to investigate the site. Vanessa later told Giles and Archie about the deaths.

After the Cyberon fluid escaped its container due to it being improperly stored, the Cyberon went to the cold storage, considering various hosts within, including a Helicron, but the Cyberon decided against the Helicron, chosing a young, deceased werewolf instead. After the Cyberwolf hybrid rampaged around the site, many items in one of the warehouses were knocked to the ground, including the Helicron skull crusher. (PROSE: A Worthy Successor)

entities.description:
The Hermethicans were a species native to the planet Hermethica. A group of criminals led by the Wire discovered how to convert themselves into pure energy. (PROSE: The Time Travellers' Almanac) The Wire was sentenced to death by her people and eventually executed. However, she became a being of pure energy, and escaped via a mobile communications device, and fled across the universe to Earth in 1953 where she became trapped in a television set. (TV: The Idiot's Lantern)

The true form of the Wire or her species, beyond the fact that they were not naturally formless, is unknown, since she was using the image of a BBC continuity announcer that was on the television when she possessed it.

entities.description:
The Heziri were a species who ran an intergalactic reality show, where the main race would invade a different planet every episode. They had been involved the show since its first season.

When ratings would begin to fall, they would bring in a new species, getting them to kill off the past species that ran it. They would not tell the new species that the species they'd killed off had been part of the show.

In 2007, they "invaded" Norwich alongside the "Zaross", as part of the filming of a new episode for the show. Jackie Tyler was there at the time and so, called Rose Tyler and the Tenth Doctor to help. (AUDIO: Infamy of the Zaross)

Shortly after Osefa's death, the Sixth Doctor created a hologlyph of her, hoping to find out about how she had died. The Hoth were empathic and originated in the atmospheric oceans of Belannia XII during the first lifetime of the Bel system. They colonised the outer gas giants of the system whilst their species was less than two million years old. (PROSE: Beltempest)

entities.name: Hua-Shen
entities.description:
The Hua-Shen was a giant sea creature used by the Sea Devils to "hunt", "seek" and "feast" in the oceans and seas of 19th century China. It was allowed to roam free to feed on unsuspecting sailors and bring them down below the depths to its masters.

Zheng Yi Sao initially described the Hua-Shen as a myth. (TV: Legend of the Sea Devils)

The Hua-Shen resembled a large fish similar to the sea creature found by the Twelfth Doctor and Bill Potts in the River Thames during the last Frost Fair of London 1814. (TV: Thin Ice)

In particular, it had large dorsal fins that jutted out of the water; ten orange eyes split between both sides of its head; and hundreds of razor-sharp teeth lined up in multiple rows in its mouth. This made it extremely similar to a unique Myrka found in the Pacific Ocean in 1886; placed there by the Sixth Doctor to attack a ship with Madame Vastra, Jenny Flint, Rose Tyler and the Ninth Doctor onboard, resulting in them becoming shipwrecked on an island. (COMIC: The Lost Dimension)

entities.name: Huduct
entities.description:
The Huducts were the former masters of the Anubians on Anubis.

The Huducts were red-eyed, purple-skinned humanoids with appendages on their chins.

The Huducts mind-controlled the Anubians using Torcs worn on the head. (TV: Curse of Anubis)

Thousands of years before 2050, the Huducts ruled over the Anubians for millennia. K9 went and freed the Anubians. He left the Huducts and the Anubians to reconcile in peace. However this did not last and the Anubians enslaved the Huducts, who wore the Torcs on their necks. The Anubians went on to control a vast empire, using the Huduct headbands to control conquered species. (TV: Curse of Anubis)

The Hufko were a race which looked similar to the Earth antelope, with two arms in addition to four legs. They were strict vegetarians and their society was matriarchal. The Hufko colonised the planet Teuba at some point in their history. They later became game animals for humans, who mistook them for non-sentient beings. (PROSE: The Diplomat's Story)

entities.description:
Hunters were dangerous predators that were believed to be native to the Althosian system. They lived in the upper atmosphere of Nicaea. They were presumably destroyed when the System was annihilated by Kopyion Liall a Mahajetsu.

Hunters were large hairy humanoids with lots of teeth. (PROSE: The Pit)

They could travel through space and were naturally attracted to rifts in time and space. They were also immune to time-based afflictions. Hunters generally hunted alone, since they could easily kill a humanoid by themselves, and often kidnapped small children and animals. They generally hunted by smell. They could also spit out a gold, acidic, rapidly hardening paste, which they used to trap their prey. (PROSE: The Pit)

Hussuloofians were a race of green creatures known for their kindness and gentle nature – as well as remarkably hairy ears. They had a strong attraction to the tripeberry – a large purple berry with a strong smell that was considered to be a delicacy on the planet.

For a while their King was a Trit in the guise of their former ruler. Under the Trit's reign, the rule box was greatly expanded and the subjects bullied into subservience. When the Trit was exposed by the Eleventh Doctor, the vacant position was taken on by the former King's aide, Trubbs. (COMIC: The King and the Tripeberry)

Having eradicated her conscience, she developed the creatures. (PROSE: Only Human)

entities.name: Hyperion
entities.description:
The Hyperions were a fusion of DNA, nuclear energy and hyper-intelligence. Their evolution was akin to that of suns. The final stage made them burn up, the energies within them mutating out of control, leaving the entire species on the verge of supernova.

A Hyperion could emit from the torso a blast of high-temperature flame or fireball , which could burn their enemies in an instant. (COMIC: Terrorformer, The Hyperion Empire)

Hyperions used fusion-webs to encircle suns and transfuse their energy into their own bodies, thus prolonging their existence.

Hyperion ships were semi-sentient, designed to evolve and adapt. For instance, Rann-Korr's ship took control of the Dollar Intergalactic terraforming technology on Isen VI. They also employed sensor-shields to avoid detection. (COMIC: Terrorformer) Hyperion ships were equipped with energy beam cannons. (COMIC: The Hyperion Empire)

entities.description: A hypno leech was a means of controlling someone's mind. Vienna Salvatori used one on Sargeant Lane to force him to accept her credentials and allow her access to the Kreyfin compound on Karnos Delta. Information, such as one's false name, had to be programmed into the hypno leech. Vienna noted that once the victim started to ask questions, that the battery within the leech was running dry. Before killing him, she told Lane that hypno leeches had very short battery life. (AUDIO: Bad Faith) Category:Species

entities.description:
A hybrid carnivorous hypomorph was a creature whose DNA could absorb and use surrounding proteins, minerals and vitamins from other lifeforms to regenerate its form. Once a new form has been grown the creature had a ravenous appetite for flesh.

When one hypomorph drew on the ingredients inside an ice cream shipment aboard the SS Greensleeves, it took the form of a giant blob of vanilla ice cream that needed warmth to move. The Eleventh Doctor lured it into space, where the temperature froze it into a solid scoop of ice cream. (COMIC: I Scream)

entities.description:
The Iarcho were a species destroyed by an entity which perceived time backwards.

The Iarcho were one of the last species to evolve in the universe. The Entity had perceived other species to "devolve" into savagery and tried to warn the Iarcho of their fate. When they failed to respond to the threat, the desperate entity tried to force them to do so by presenting them more immediate dangers. The Iarcho was the first of many destroyed until the Time Lords revealed the entity's perception of time. (PROSE: From Eternity)

entities.name: Iborian
entities.description: The Iborians were an extraterrestrial species sent by the Eighth Doctor to 22nd century Earth in order to help humans to recover in the aftermath of the Dalek invasion. They signed a trade agreement, according to which they intended to invest properly in Earth development. (AUDIO: Relative Dimensions) During the second invasion of the century, a Dalek plague was spread across the planet, which was quarantined; the Iborians stayed in Earth's orbit. (AUDIO: Lucie Miller)

entities.name: Identical Man
entities.description:
A Machine, also known as an Identical Man, was a construct made by the Proto-Viyrans to avoid overpopulation on inhabited planets.

The Machine at Embankment had the form of a naked man with a smooth area in place of genitalia, (AUDIO: Embankment Station) leading Rab to liken it to Action Man. (AUDIO: Ruffling)

Machines were indestructible, able to kill with a single touch (AUDIO: Embankment Station) and to send out a coded message which transformed people's brains, affecting their ability to feel empathy. (AUDIO: Seed of Chaos) They could also create copies of themselves from their bodies, called "factors", hence why they were known as the Identical Men on Earth. (AUDIO: Embankment Station)

Machines were capable of controlling people with a modification pulse, turning people into zombies and sending them to complete tasks. These zombies were capable of restoring themselves when they were damaged, although this ability was limited and they could ultimately be damaged so much that they were unable to bring themselves back together. (AUDIO: Ruffling, Seed of Chaos)

entities.name: Ikkaba
entities.description:
The Ikkaban were a highly advanced species which died out.

The Ikkaban had advanced technology rivalling those of species like the People. They had even developed some simple time travel technology. Unlike other such species, they did not form empires with this technology and left behind little but poems. (PROSE: Walking to Babylon)

The Ikkabans practised self-immolation and built pyramids dedicated to this purpose. This was believed to be linked to a belief in reincarnation. (PROSE: Walking to Babylon)

The Ikkabans travelled across the Mutter's Spiral, and at least three other galaxies, including the galaxy of the People. They travelled from at least 1450 BC to at least the 5th century AD. During their long period of space travel, they influenced the creation of pyramids in many cultures, including the Aztecs, the Babylonians and the Yamayans. They later stopped their practice of meddling with other species and eventually, the entire civilisation committed mass suicide.

entities.description:
The Ikorans were a species that were susceptible to insanity. Therefore, mental health was very important to them.

The Ikorans created a therapy chair that could extract memories and rewrite identities for therapeutic purposes. (PROSE: The Heroine, the Hero and the Megalomaniac)

They waged a constant war against the Macro-viruses. They had the ability to divide and duplicate themselves, acting as the antibodies for their home planet. (COMIC: Black Death White Life)

entities.description:
The Infinite Warriors, also known as the Infinites, were the soldiers of the Eminence.

They were composed of beings that the Eminence had possessed using its breath of forever. They were walking corpses, and were impossible to kill. (AUDIO: Destroy the Infinite, The Seeds of War, Time's Horizon) They were entirely eliminated when the retro-genitor particles inside the Eminence activated and dispersed it over an infinitely large area. (AUDIO: Rule of the Eminence)

The Nine considered calling himself the Infinite after he had silenced his previous selves using the Crucible of Souls. He dismissed this name as being too easy to confuse with the Infinite Warriors. Interstitials were creatures that were created through a temporal anormally. Interstitials were living in a state relating to the space or time between things. They were neither dead nor alive, they were beings but not beings and they existed without life.

K9 once meets these creatures. Once they had been colonists heading for the twin planets when they had collided with a ship doing warp speed. This had caused a temporal anormaly. There had nothing left exapt a cloud and the people. The people asked K9 for his help to rejoin the livestream. K9 tried to help them by letting them pass into another existence, where it was better for them. (PROSE: Interstitials)

The Iron automata were a species that the Eighth Doctor encountered on Hyspero.

They could belch fire and were able to fry their enemies on the spot. Hidden inside each of the Iron automata was an "evil and bitter" Djinn which was determined to wreak havoc on the world. (PROSE: The Scarlet Empress) Category:Species

entities.name: Isari
entities.description:
The Isari were a species who were active in the Mutters Spiral by 3000 BC. They were engaged in a protracted, destructive conflict with the Anar, which lasted for over two thousand years. In 3000 BC, the planet Iytea was "nearly destroyed" in the wars' crossfire, wiping out most of the Iyteans. (GAME: ) In the Infinity Doctor's reality, General Sontar was renowned as "the mastermind behind the victory in the two‐thousand‐year war with the Isari". (PROSE: The Infinity Doctors)

During the Ghost Wars, the vampire Garglespike owned a copy of the Isari Revised Dictionary 1978, a technologically-advanced dictionary containing definitions for multiple languages, including English, and a built-in translation matrix. When she wasn't using it, she shrank it down into a book-shaped pin on her lapel using acumancy. (PROSE: The Bloodletters)

entities.name: Iska'lanz'rm
entities.description:
The Iska'lanz'rm were an alien race created by the imagination of a human boy named Harry Ware. The Tenth Doctor encountered them while travelling with Martha Jones.

The Iska'lanz'rm were a humanoid race. They resembled upright cows with brown fur, and white patches of fur on their head and neck. They had hooves in place of feet and sharp claws on their hands. Where their eyes should have been, yellow serpents protruded, each with a singular eye and a large gaping mouth underneath. (PROSE: The Box Under the Tree)

The Iska'lanz'rm were created by the universe, which had observed Harry writing the story of their war with the Xarantharax. By the 21st century, this war had begun.

In December 2008, the Iska'lanz'rm came to Earth to stop Harry from drawing a picture which would end their war and cause the two races to declare peace with each other. (PROSE: The Box Under the Tree)

The species is simply used for a gag in Ghosts of India, and the Doctor never actually names the species. Thus Istervaalan may only be a rather than a proper name.

entities.name: Iytean
entities.description:
The Iyteans were an amoeboid, symbiotic species from the planet Iytea in Mutter's Spiral. They experienced a golden age around 3000 years BC.

The Iyteans were an amoeboid race similar to the Rutans, though smaller in size; an individual Iytean weighed only three to five pounds. They flourished in more or less the same temperature range as humans.

Their bodies were exclusively composed of "multicellular, nonspecialised tissues" which could roughly perform any function from muscular to cerebral, though it meant the Iyteans' senses were extremely limited. Capable of changing shape as needed, for example to squeeze through extremely small apertures (an Iytean could hypothetically seep into soil to escape a dangerous situation), they appeared as a viscous, liquid pool when at rest, and as a "mobile jelly" when active; either way they were translucent.

As a result of this fluid anatomy, they were extremely hard to kill: an unprotected Iytean could only be killed by weapons which could "destroy the entire creature in one attack", such as fire, distintegrators, or rapid freezers. An Iytean could even survive being cut in half, though the halves would be severely disoriented until they could rejoin, and would retain "serious psychological trauma".

entities.name: Jackalope
entities.description:
The Jackalopes were a mythical animal in North American Folklore.

Señor 105 and Sheila encountered a species of seemingly part-rabbit part-deer Jackalopes who claimed to hail from the moon. The King Jackalope was also part-pheasant. (PROSE: Jackalope)

Luna later claimed that the Jackalopes didn't understand their own history and they were in fact failed experiments from Una Contro-Mundo where all rabbits had antlers and so did the men. (PROSE: The Gulf)

As a result of not having a license to use Mondas and the Cybermen, Cody Schell used thinly-veiled terms to refer to these concepts. Therefore the Jackalopes were supposed to be early failed experiments by the Mondasians prior to them beginning to 'upgrade' humans.

entities.name: Jangrofen
entities.description:
The Jangrofens were a species native to the planet Nixtus III alongside the Zanthians.

The Jangrofens and the Zanthians evolved side by side over millions of years, stemming from the same ancestor race. Many wars broke out between the two races, until a treaty was signed to allow a symbiotic relationship between the two sides. For thousands of years, the two races lived as one, until it was discovered that the bonding between them corrupted the Jangrofen DNA, slowly causing their extinction. It was at this moment that Harmony Shoal offered to replace the void left by the Jangrofens, offering another symbiotic relationship, and the proposal was accepted by the Zanthians. With the help of the Alcyone, Harmony Shoal shut down the decentralised nervous system of the Zanthians to successfully overpower and replace them. The Twelfth Doctor and Grant, with the help of Lucy Fletcher, Jennifer Fletcher and Nemika, retrieved the gemstone and convinced the Zanthians to rebel against Harmony Shoal, saying that they could live without searching for another species to bond with and without burying themselves. (COMIC: Ghost Stories)

entities.name: Jathaa
entities.description:
The Jathaa were an alien race who used a type of transport known as the Jathaa sunglider.

The Jathaa had interstellar travel capabilities by the late 20th century and by the 1990s had begun to visit Earth.

In 1997, a Jathaa Sunglider was shot down by the Torchwood Institute over the North Sea. It was kept in Torchwood 1. (TV: Army of Ghosts) Its weapons system was back-engineered for use against alien invasions. (TV: The Christmas Invasion)

In the 2000s, a squad of at least three Jathaa ships were transported to over the Taj Mahal when the Cardiff Space-Time Rift temporarily fractured across the Earth. (TV: End of Days)

entities.description:
The were an ancient and powerful species.

In a timeline in which Emily Rutherford and Tom Charrington separated as teenagers, the Jatiri confronted the Shandance, who had intervened in an interplanetary war. The ensuing battle, called the Collision, resulted in the end of the universe. When the Third Doctor encouraged Emily and Tom to stay together, the timeline was averted, and interplanetary war was avoided. (PROSE: Separation Day)

entities.name: Jax
entities.description:
The Jax were a legendary race originating from the Cronus system, they presented as a virus. (PROSE: Kursaal)

The Jax were a virus that infected enzymes to convert another life form into a Jax. They were capable of reproduction by infecting other humanoid life forms. (PROSE: Kursaal)

Humanoids infected by the Jax virus arrived on Kursaal and built a cathedral on the planet. The humanoids were killed off by wolf-like creatures native to the planet, who became carriers of the Jax virus, turning into werewolf-like humanoids. They went into hibernation until more humanoids landed on the planet. Kursaal became their homeworld and they were worshipped by the other species in the Cronus system, who they eventually transformed into Jax. (PROSE: Kursaal)

entities.name: Jell
entities.description:
The Jells were a race of bovine creatures from the planet Jellidge. They walked upright and were locked in often pointless conflicts with their planetary neighbours on Nabrili.

The Eleventh Doctor brokered a peace between the two warring planets using a missile computer that he adapted by adding an electronic conscience (a spare part of K9's retrieved from the TARDIS) with the instruction that it was all the Nabrili's idea. (COMIC: The Peace Strike)

The Jezark were natives of the planet Jezark. They had leathery green skin, three glowing red eyes, claws and a tail.

Grimmon was a Jezark. He crashed his ship on Earth but was able to make his way back to Jezark with the Fourth Doctor's help. (PROSE: The Brain of Socrates)

entities.name: Jezrafeq
entities.description:
The Jezrafeq were a minuscule species that believed themselves to be superior to all other lifeforms. The High Regnum of the Jezrafeq claimed they were known across nine galaxies for their military strength. Their spaceships resembled Christmas ornaments.

In December 2016, after several decades of planning, the Jezrafeq launched an invasion of Earth. They broadcast a signal across the planet which - when heard with Christmas music - affected the human brain, leading to a loss of physical and mental control. Within a few hours, about 70% of the population of Earth had been affected. Erimem and Andy Hansen used the Habitat to copy the signal and broadcast it back to the Jezrafeq fleet. The pilots of the Jezrafeq fleet became unable to properly control their ships and the Jezrafeq crashed onto Earth; 20 miles from Ibrahim Hadmani's house. The Jezrafeq survived the crash, but had their spaceships taken away from them by Erimem. Erimem reasoned that since they didn't have any technology and they were the size of ants, the Jezrafeq were absolutely harmless. (PROSE: Cliff Richard Saves the World)

entities.name: Joran
entities.description:
At some point in their history, Joran scientists tried to develop the ability to control pheromones. This led to the idea of a pheromone language. However, the language became a living, sentient thing, known as the Syntax, that spread to the entire population, save Deezer. It subjugated the will of each Joran, leaving them unable to make their own decisions.

The Eighth Doctor reasoned that, as the Jorans were happy in their new condition, he would not allow Deezer to kill the Syntax. (PROSE: Syntax)

entities.name: Planet
entities.description:
Planets were celestial bodies of varying size, large enough to be rounded into a spherical shape by their own gravity, but not massive enough to cause thermonuclear fusion. Most planets existed as part of a star system. Some planets possessed an atmosphere and could support life.

Planets generally orbited stars, but rogue planets (COMIC: The Rogue Planet) and wandering planetoids were not uncommon. (TV: Revenge of the Cybermen, The Tenth Planet) Perihelion was when a planet or other body came closest to its star. (HOMEVID: The Zero Imperative)

There were a number of highly unusual planets in the universe, including Magla, in reality, an immense amoeba with a crust-like shell, (TV: Destiny of the Daleks) and the artificial planet Arcadia. (PROSE: Deceit) Unlike most planets, Tigella had an anti-clockwise rotation. (TV: Meglos)

Some planets were artificially accelerated through the interference (intentional or not) of other life forms. Normally in these cases, large starships provided the initial large mass which began the process of planetary formation. Such a fate befell a Minyan ship, the P7E, by accident (and nearly also happened to another Minyan vessel, the R1C), (TV: Underworld) and the Secret Heart, the vessel carrying the last of the Racnoss, by design. (TV: )

Jason Kane travelled to the planet in the year 6 billion BC, using one of the Seventh Doctor's personal force field emitters to survive its harsh environment. (PROSE: Eternity Weeps)

entities.name: 70 Virginis b
entities.description:
70 Virginis b was a colony planet with an orbiting space station, Dunlop Station.

In 2133, the Eleventh Doctor and Rory Williams briefly visited Dunlop Station while attempting to get back to London, 1814, to retrieve Amy. (COMIC: The Doctor and the Nurse)

In the real world, 70 Virginis b is a gas giant about 7.5 times the mass of Jupiter. Discovered in 1996, it orbits , one of the first stars confirmed to have planets in orbit.

At the time The Doctor and the Nurse was published, 70 Virginis b was believed to be within the star system's habitable zone, like Earth, and so was nicknamed "Goldilocks". Later discoveries about the planet's orbit disproved this.

entities.description:
A-Lux was a pleasure planet in the 40th century, popular with human tourists and sometimes their pets. It boasted warm artificial lakes, lush lawns, fully equipped game rooms and sub-aqua tennis courts.

The Seventh Doctor and Frobisher travelled to A-Lux in the TARDIS for a holiday, only to find that Ice Warriors led by Arryx had sabotaged the weather controls, turning the planet into a snowy wasteland. With the aid of Olla, they defeated the Ice Warriors, after which Frobisher decided to stop travelling with the Doctor and remain on A-Lux. (COMIC: )

entities.description:
The native species of Adeki were wiped out when the shape-shifting Gwanzulums became stranded on the planet and drained their life-force.

Some time later, while fishing on Adeki, the Seventh Doctor met what he thought were some of his prior companions: Adric, Sara Kingdom, Katarina, Jamie McCrimmon and Peri, as well as some of his previous incarnations. These visions each turned out to be Gwanzulums, who were stranded on Adeki and hoped to trick the Doctor into helping them leave. The Doctor realised this and escaped without taking any of them with him. (COMIC: Planet of the Dead)

entities.description:
Adipose 3, also known as Breeding Planet One, was the planet used by the Adipose or, more specifically, the Adiposian First Family, to breed their young, before being taken home by the wet nurse that took care of them. (TV: )

At some point before 2009, the planet was stolen by the New Dalek Empire, and transported to the Medusa Cascade. (TV: )

Faced with its disappearance, the first family decided, in violation of Galactic Law, to select Earth as a new breeding planet because of the number of obese humans. (TV: )

In the Medusa Cascade, Adipose 3 and twenty-six other planets formed the engine of a reality bomb with which the New Dalek Empire planned to destroy every universe. It was returned by the Meta-Crisis Tenth Doctor to its proper place in space and time after the Daleks were thwarted. (TV: )

entities.name: Agelaos
entities.description:
Agelaos was a colony on the farthest reaches of the Second Great and Bountiful Human Empire.

Agelaos was colonised for the wormhole that opened into the Time Vortex. The skies around the wormhole were full of auroras, shooting stars and ion cascades. The planet itself was covered in ice and snow, shaped into impossible looking shapes. (PROSE: The Weeping)

During the Second Great and Bountiful Human Empire, twenty thousand colonists came to Agelaos and attempted to terraform the planet, using the wormhole as a power source. They started to develop psychic powers from the wormhole, specifically precognition. Unfortunately, the wormhole also infused the inhabitants with alien DNA, causing them to develop into bizarre mutants. The source of these "monsters" was unknown, so the government quarantined the planet. They appointed Waechter to man a beacon to warn off any incoming ships. He was cybernetically connected to the Beacon, keeping him alive and incidentally keeping him clean from mutations.

Waechter watched over the beacon for five hundred years, until the Tenth Doctor and Martha came to Agelaos. The Doctor was able to break the connection Waechter had with the Beacon, allowing him to leave the planet, but this also allowed the mutations to take effect. Waechter decided to allow the Doctor to sever the connection completely, completing the mutations and allowing him to live with the other "monsters". (PROSE: The Weeping)

entities.name: Agora
entities.description:
Agora was a colonised planet located in the Centraxis system.

Agora was colonised by humans on board the New Hope in the early 22nd century. They made it an agricultural world, eschewing advanced technology.

In the 2150s, the Cybermen invaded Agora and turned it into one of their breeding colonies. After placing human Overseers in charge of conception quotas, they would return every three years to select the five hundred healthiest males for cyber-conversion. In 2175, a rebellion led by Arthur Lakesmith defeated the Overseers, but was swiftly defeated by the Cybermen when they returned the following year. In 2178, six-year-old Grant Markham and three other children were placed on a ship the colonists found on Agora and sent to New Earth. (PROSE: Killing Ground)

Although Grant knew that Agora was not technologically advanced, he suffered from robophobia. He believed it was due to Agoran folk tales about metal monsters. (PROSE: Time of Your Life)

entities.description:
Agratis was a farmworld. The Fourth Doctor claimed that it was known throughout the galaxy for the rich bounties it provided.

The economy of the planet was centred on foodstuffs and delicacies, as well as on the Jewel of Fawton, considered the most beautiful gem of the universe.

The capital city of the planet, led by a provost, was Darschon. (COMIC: A Rare Gem)

Agratis was colonised by humanoids with red skin. The discovery of the Jewel and the consequent tourism made possible the advancements of their society.

entities.name: Agrippina
entities.description:
Agrippina was a human colony planet in the Tiberian spiral galaxy (PROSE: Ghost in the Machine) which was attacked by the Eleventh Cyber Legion during the Cyber-Wars. (PROSE: Ghost in the Machine, A Girl Called Doubt) Its capital city was Agrippina Primus. (PROSE: A Girl Called Doubt)

In one timeline, the Doctor died on Agrippina during the Cyber-Wars and billions of Cybermites attempted to convert the Doctor's TARDIS. A war was fought between the TARDIS systems and the mites, leading to the TARDIS swelling to the size of a planet after its chameleon circuit was shut down. (PROSE: The Paradox Moon)

Agrippina was eventually destroyed, along with the rest of the Tiberian spiral galaxy, by a human empire attempting to eradicate the Cybermen. (TV: Nightmare in Silver)

entities.description:
Agrovan Seven was a planet inhabited by the Agrovans. Two groups of Agrovans, the Strykes and the Marat, were at war with each other and had been for over a thousand years. By the time the Seventh Doctor and Ace arrived on Agrovan Seven it had been declared a non-intervention site by the Time Lords. Someone had given the Strykes a Gallifreyan virus to use against the Marats, and the Doctor wanted to stop it spreading. They met a Marat, who took them to the Marats infected by the Strykes' new bioweapon. The Doctor then met with Doctor Treykan and gave her the antidote to the plague. (COMIC: The Forgotten)

entities.name: Akhaten
entities.description:
Akhaten, also known as the Old God or Grandfather, was a parasitic, sentient astronomical object that fed on the souls of the Sun-singers of Akhet. He was considered by the people of the neighbouring worlds to be a great and fearsome god. Within his rings was the asteroid Tiaanamat, on which was held the Festival of Offerings, which served to keep him asleep.

Akhaten slumbered for thousands of years, leaving a Mummy in a pyramid as an alarm clock, until the Long Song ended. Akhaten then awoke and threatened to consume all seven of its neighbouring planets. Eventually, the Eleventh Doctor let him take his memories instead of the valuable things of the natives of Akhet. The Doctor was then saved by Clara Oswald, who gave Akhaten 'the most important leaf in human history', the leaf that told all of her family's story, all that happened, all that didn't happen and all that should have happened. The infinite possibilities of causality caused Akhaten to implode. (TV: )

entities.name: Akoshemon
entities.description:
Akoshemon was a desolate planet located in the Akoshemon system.

The planet was a giant mass of scarlet and black. It was so near the galaxy that was by the Mutter's Spiral galaxy that one could actually see the gap in between the two, in which there were no stars at all.

The planet was infamous in its sector of space for being a planet synonymous with cruelty and death. Its history was littered with war, famine, pestilence and various other horrors. These were the results of the being known as the Dark. Circa 1482 AD, a group of humanoid space travellers arrived on Akoshemon and learned about the Dark. They then tracked it back to its lair, and destroyed its physical form with fire.

The planet was completely lifeless, with a highly toxic atmosphere and a surface that was made up of boiling mud and molten lava. (PROSE: Fear of the Dark)

entities.name: Albert
entities.description:
Albert was created when a planet that was orbiting a white hole was seeded by a quantum field the white hole was emitting. This quantum field became sentient, and grew until it merged with the planet. (PROSE: Grimm Reality)

Because of the quantum field, the terrain of Albert could be changed at will, from woods to mountains in a matter of seconds. (PROSE: Grimm Reality)

When a colony spaceship from Earth crash-landed on Albert, the colonists entered into a mutual agreement with the planet, which fed off their tales to create a magical world governed by the rules of traditional folklore.

Another quantum field from the white hole hit Albert, which soon became sentient. The quantum field also had the power to alter reality on Albert, which threatened Albert's existence. The Eighth Doctor came to an agreement with the field and it travelled to another place in the universe so that Albert could still survive. (PROSE: Grimm Reality)

One of the native life forms was the desert-dwelling, crab-clawed Kamelius. The cactus pulp eaten by the inhabitants of Aldebaran II was usually considered disgusting by outsiders. The Third Doctor visited Aldebaran II. (AUDIO: The Paradise of Death)

By 2540, Alderberan Four was a colony planet in the Earth Empire that had been recently raised to dominion status. The Twelfth Master pretended to be an official from this planet, (PROSE: Doctor Who and the Space War) although by another account, the planet in question was Sirius IV. (TV: Frontier in Space)

entities.name: Aleph-777
entities.description:
Aleph-777 (also spelt Aleph 777) was a planet in the Deneb Sector known for its tranquility and idyllic peace. It was inhabited by humans who were known to be the most peaceful in the galaxy. It was home to the ultimate armament, which the planet's inhabitants sought to protect and sacrifice, relying on it as a last resort of survival against threat. It also contained the ruins of a site of great archaeological significance to both the FHD and the Sontarans. (COMIC: Conflict of Interests)

The Sontaran Katsu arrived on the planet on a quest to find the ultimate armament for his own use. He attacked the people at a village to acquire it, but they wouldn't let him have it. Eventually he left when he was told they didn't have it anymore and saw a ship leaving which supposedly had it. He went in pursuit of it. (COMIC: The Final Quest)

entities.name: Alfava Metraxis
entities.description:
Alfava Metraxis was the home planet of the Aplans before their extinction.

Alfava Metraxis was the seventh planet in the Dundra system, in the Garn belt. It was home to the Aplan civilisation until they were made extinct by Weeping Angels in the mid 47th century. By the 49th century it had been terraformed and colonised by human settlers. The atmosphere boasted a high level of oxygen and a low amounts of toxins. The Alfava Metraxis day was about eleven hours.

The Aplans left landmarks on the planet, including temples, and the Aplan Mortaria, sometimes known as "Mazes of the Dead". These were large subterranean labyrinths with tombs in the walls, adorned with statues of the dead. The Mazes had six levels, to represent the ascent of the soul. (TV: The Time of Angels / Flesh and Stone)

In 2009, an alien device from Alfava Metraxis somehow came to Earth and fell into the hands of Sarah Jane Smith. (TV: The Nightmare Man)

entities.name: Alpha Centauri
entities.description:
Alpha Centauri was the home planet of the Alpha Centauran race. (TV: The Curse of Peladon, et. al) Alpha Centauri did not have any natural predators. As such, Alpha Centaurans were free to develop skills in politics and focus on politeness. (PROSE: The Monster Vault) The world was also a part of the Galactic Federation and served as its headquarters in 3375. (TV: The Curse of Peladon, The Monster of Peladon, PROSE: The Dark Path)

When the Cybermen allied with Rassilon to rewrite all of history, Alpha Centauri was rendered lifeless by Cyberman forces. This version of history was undone by the Twelfth Doctor and Rassilon. (COMIC: Supremacy of the Cybermen)

At some point, Alpha Centauri was host to annual Alpha Centauri Olympics. (AUDIO: A Requiem for the Doctor)

When the Second Doctor landed in Australia in 2018, he was actually trying to get to either William Shakespeare's house in Stratford-upon-Avon or the Pan-Galactic Games on Alpha Centauri, as Jamie McCrimmon had wanted some excitement and spectacle. (PROSE: Timewyrm: Apocalypse)

entities.name: Alpha One
entities.description:
was a human colony planet. When the colonists first arrived, Walter Cantrell acquired more land than the other colonists, not always by legal means. The colonists, who feared Cantrell, began keeping to themselves.

At Christmas, a blizzard forced the colonists to take shelter in the town. The Fifth Doctor, Peri Brown and Erimem arrived to help the colonists. Erimem convinced them to stand up to Cantrell, and the Doctor suggested they get together often enough to develop a sense of community.

The Doctor later told Peri and Erimem that, in the future, Alpha One would be a focal point during a galactic war, and it was important that the right people be running the colony when the war came. (PROSE: Far Away in a Manger)

It crashed into Alrakis thousands of years after the Tonska had vanished. (PROSE: ...And Eternity in an Hour)

When posing as the Doctor, Cerunnos offered to take Sarah Jane Smith to Alrakis. (PROSE: Moving On)

entities.name: Altair III

Altair III was the home planet of Light-beings. (PROSE: Endgame)

The planet was once invaded by the Daleks who were attempting to establish a base there. They planned to destroy the forests and jungles covering planet, kill all of the animal life and destroy the ozone layer. The Doctor helped the flying native creatures of the planet to repel the invasion and they made him an honourary member of their colony. This was of great help to the Sixth Doctor when the TARDIS landed on Altair III one hundred years later in search of an American envoy, and he and his companions Jason and Crystal were ambushed by the Cybermen. The Doctor was able to call the flying creatures for help using their language and they attacked the Cybermen, allowing the Doctor, Jason and Crystal to escape back to the TARDIS. (AUDIO: The Ultimate Adventure)

entities.name: Alvega
entities.description:
Alvega was a planet in the Skaro system and the planet closest to Skaro. It was the homeworld of the Amarylls and their Controller, which was situated at the core of Alvega. The planet was covered in rich vegetation and had almost no animal life save for giant earthworms.

When the Daleks first achieved space flight, Alvega was the first planet they attempted to conquer. The Dalek Fleet's landing was observed by the Amarylls who initially reserved judgement before the Dalek landing force used their gunsticks to clear a path through the vegetation. With the invaders proving hostile, Alvega rose up against the Daleks firing lethal seed barrages that destroyed the Dalek drones. When the plants advanced on the Dalek flying saucers, the Daleks launched. Leaving to continue the conquest of other worlds, the Golden Emperor ordered four ships to conduct an orbital bombardment on Alvega.

After the surface had been blighted, the Daleks began colonising the planet, constructing a city before the Controller caused an earthquake, destroying all but one Dalek ship. Activating its excavators, the last Dalek ship burrowed down near Alvega's planetary core where an earthworm crushed their ship. Though the Daleks destroyed their attacker, they could not save their ship. Braving the underground, the Daleks were picked off one by one until one remained. Confronting the Controller, the last Dalek opened fire, killing and destroying Alvega in a massive explosion. Observing the destruction, the Golden Emperor decreed that whatever the Daleks could not conquer, they would destroy. (COMIC: The Amaryll Challenge)

entities.name: Alyx Pol-13
entities.description:
Alyx Pol-13 was a mining colony invaded by the Daleks.

After it was colonised, the Intergalactic Mining Corporation set up snowbases on the planet to drill into its molten-ice core. In June 2614, the Daleks invaded the planet and began planet clearance, starting with the destruction of Snowbase Beta. The colonists were unable to fight back. However, Captain Jacobean Cahill of Snowbase Alpha ordered the Plasma Ice-Drills and Digger-Buggies to be powered up for war. Waves of Daleks swept out of the blizzard, firing. Due to the intensity of the battle, most of the crew couldn't make it to the emergency transmat station and were wiped out within the hour, leaving Jacobean the only survivor. The Daleks then turned the planet into a giant deep-freeze unit, in which they stored millions of captured aliens, frozen until the Daleks employed them in the Great War of the Rim Empires. (PROSE: The Big Freeze!)

entities.name: Alzarius
entities.description:
Its coordinates from galactic centre were -10 0 -11 00 by 0 -2, nearly identical to those of Gallifrey. However, it was situated not in the universe containing Gallifrey but a smaller universe known as E-Space. A starliner from the planet Terradon crash-landed an unspecified number of years before Adric's time.

Alzarius was most notable for its lifeforms' highly unusual biology. This manifested itself most obviously in the extremely rapid adaptive changes made by Alzarian animal life. If placed in an environment it found stressful or even uncomfortable, an Alzarian creature would rapidly develop whatever characteristics it required to make the environment less stressful, such as the ability to breathe in a different medium, or higher muscular density.

Connected to this was the ability to heal injuries at an accelerated rate. The rate of healing slowed as the individual aged.

Alzarian biology was also unusual in that the boundaries between animal and plant forms of life appeared less rigidly defined: the eggs of the Alzarian spider were discovered developing within riverfruit. (TV: Full Circle)

entities.name: Ameron
entities.description:
Ameron was a planet where, according to one account, Halldon scientists had transplanted primitive humans and artificially accelerated their evolution, thus creating the Daleks according to the research of the scientist Bryant Anderson. (PROSE: We are the Daleks!) In most other accounts, however, the Daleks arose on the planet Skaro. (COMIC: Genesis of Evil; TV: The Daleks, Genesis of the Daleks; PROSE: Doctor Who in an Exciting Adventure with the Daleks)

Later scientists and historians were unable to contradict or deny Anderson's findings. While some dismissed his theories as one of the creation myths other races sometimes formulated about the Daleks, others believed that Daleks really might have come to be on Ameron, and that the Daleks of Skaro might themselves have been the result of proto-humans being transplanted to Skaro in ages past. (PROSE: Dalek: The Astounding Untold History of the Greatest Enemies of the Universe)
