entities.name: Anathema
entities.description:
Anathema was a Remote colony located on the side of a planet-sized warship which spent centuries travelling through space towards Earth.

During the Vampire Wars, the Time Lords designed a planet-sized warship shaped like a disk and patterned with an omniscate, (PROSE: , ) which could cause neural spasms in creatures from outside the universe. At the ship's centre was the Cold. (PROSE: ) However, the Vampire Wars ended before the weapon could be used. (PROSE: , )

After Norval's TARDIS was destroyed by a ball of energy from the Needle, acting-President Voran planned to deploy the warship against the Needle, worried that the people there had control of the Effect. He called it the ultimate countermeasure. However, the Doctor and Larna stopped him from using the Great Key to activate it. (PROSE: )

During the War in Heaven, the Time Lords deployed the ship against 20th century Earth, which they knew to be a major historical nexus as well as their enemy's original homeworld. Since they knew the enemy would block the attack if they put the ship straight into Earth's orbit, the Time Lords sent it out from one of their bases at sublight speed, planning for it to reach Earth in three billion years, at which point they would decide whether or not they needed to activate it; if they chose to activate it, Earth would be destroyed, and the causal nexus of the universe would unravel, erasing the Time Lords and their enemy alike. (PROSE: )

entities.name: Andalia
entities.description:
, home to the Andalians, was a planet visited by the Tenth Doctor in the Dark Times. It was not far from Gallifrey.

After fleeing Ood Sigma's summons, the Doctor made his way to Andalia, visiting the Tombs of the Ended. His arrival coincided with Estinee demonstrating a lifeshroud to the people, meant to protect them from the Kotturuh. Shortly afterwards, Brian and the Kotturuh arrived, both seeking Estinee for the secrets of her immunity to death.

Judging the planet, the Kotturuh gave the Andalians a lifespan of one lunar orbit and adjusted the living time of the flora and fauna accordingly. They claimed to the Doctor that Andalia would one day be of strategic value and their judgement would enable it to be taken rather than won in a war. When they left with Estinee, the Doctor and Brian quickly followed to rescue her. The two tracked the Kotturuh to the planet Mordeela, where they marked the Doctor to die on Andalia.

Along with Estinee and Hana Fallomax, the Doctor later returned to the planet to seek out genetic samples of the Andalians to perfect a reverse-engineered necrotic virus to turn on the Kotturuh. Seizing control of The Doctor's TARDIS, the Kotturuh jumped the TARDIS forward five days, when the Doctor was to die. After enthralling Estinee and having her kill Fallomax, she turned her weapon on herself when they tried to have her kill the Doctor. The Doctor then released his virus, sentencing the Kotturuh to a lifespan of fifteen minutes. As they died, the Doctor left the planet, observed by a now incorporeal Estinee. (PROSE: The Knight, The Fool and The Dead)

When Bernice Summerfield visited the ruins of Andromeda she discovered a mirror from Earth which contained the imprisoned Daughter of Mine. (AUDIO: Shadow of a Doubt)

In their thirteenth incarnation, the Doctor decided to free Daughter of Mine and visited Andromeda to release her. (WC: The Shadow in the Mirror) Bernice later returned to Andromeda to find the mirror missing. (AUDIO: Shadow of a Doubt)

However, when humans expanded into Andromeda, they fought the Wirrn for a thousand years and destroyed the breeding colonies. (TV: The Ark in Space)

entities.name: Androzani Major
entities.description:
Androzani Major was the twin planet of Androzani Minor in the Sirius system. It was the home of the wealthy and influential Sirius Conglomerate.

It was colonised by Earth, and the Doctor visited the planet during its early days. (TV: The Caves of Androzani)

By the 30th century, Androzani Major was part of the Earth Empire. (PROSE: So Vile a Sin)

Centuries later, it possessed a federal government, with a ruling body called the Praesidium headed by a president and an army called the "federal forces". The Conglomerate's chairman, Morgus, had great influence over the Presidium and was influential enough for the army's commanding officer on Minor to pass information on to him before the President. Spectrox, a chemical that could slow down ageing, was a major commodity and was harvested by androids.

entities.name: Androzani Minor
entities.description:
Androzani Minor was a dry, sandy planet and the twin planet to Androzani Major.

Androzani Minor was a desert planet, its oceans having dried up billions of years ago. Due to the unusual composition of the planet, boiling hot mud flowed throughout the planet's crust, blasting its way to the surface in dangerous explosions. The planet was riddled with caves (actually blowholes) that had been excavated by the violent mud flows, some of which lacked oxygen. Despite the conditions of the planet, it had a breathable atmosphere and was home to such life as the queen bats and the Magma Beasts, but was otherwise unsuitable for habitation by humans. (TV: The Caves of Androzani)

When humans first colonised the solar system Androzani Major and Minor were located, they didn't bother with Androzani Minor and focused on Major instead because of Minor's desert climate and the nearly constant mud bursts. It wasn't until the humans discovered that Androzani Minor contained a drug in spectrox which granted nea-eternal life that they took an interest in it. (TV: The Caves of Androzani)

In the 30th century, Androzani Major was part of the Earth Empire. (PROSE: So Vile a Sin)

entities.name: Aneth
entities.description:
Aneth was the home planet of the Anethans and was ruled by a monarchy. Hymetusite was one of the planet's resources. The Fourth Doctor mentioned having visited Aneth at some point in time and considered it a pleasant place. (TV: The Horns of Nimon)

Aneth was a neighbouring planet of Skonnos (PROSE: Doctor Who and the Horns of Nimon) and was subjected under the Skonnan Empire until it collapsed. Several generations later, the Skonnans returned, demanding sacrifices of people and hymetusite which were given to the Nimon. (TV: The Horns of Nimon)

entities.description: Angvia was the home planet of the Angvians. It was known for its large trees, but had no major pits. The Angvians were once at war with the Gholos of planet Golos. (AUDIO: Bang-Bang-a-Boom!)

entities.name: Anhaut
entities.description:
Anhaut was a planet inhabited by peaceful humanoids who had two antennae on their heads. They used tame pterodactyl-like creatures as mounts.

Anhaut was invaded by Daleks twice. Both attacks were sucessfully repelled. The first invasion was defeated in the desert of Vaksh by General Nor-Din, who used a telepathic weapon which destroyed the Daleks' minds. The second invasion, which took place eight hundred years later, was defeated when Glax and Hok Nepo discovered the General's weapon, and Kuay used it to destroy her former masters. (COMIC: The Return of the Daleks)

entities.name: Anibus
entities.description:
Bernice Summerfield accompanied three students on a dig to Anibus. While there, one of the students, Tony Deek, sabotaged the equipment of another student, Steven Mead, unintentionally causing Steven's death. Before he died, Steven gave an Anibusian Memory Stone to his fiancée, Vivian. (PROSE: Christmas Spirit)

entities.name: Anima Persis
entities.description:
Anima Persis was a geo-psychic planet. Its deserts and vegetation had psychic auras which could communicate with strangers.

Biochemical weapons built from the planet harnessed its psychic atmosphere. Bombs could blew the souls from their victims' bodies, leaving behind vengeful ghosts which fed off fear and tortured their victims to death. (WC: Death Comes to Time) The Seventh Doctor told Michael Ashworth that the Talichre had "played with" Anima Persis and done something unspeakably horrible there. (PROSE: Relative Dementias)

The Kingmaker sent Ace to Anima Persis to defeat the tortured spirits. Upon arriving, she met a few survivors of the wars, driven mad with fear by the spirits who penetrated their minds during storms. Together, Ace and a survivor child named Magan journeyed to the crater of a volcano from which the spirits emerged. However, the spirits captured Ace's mind, and Ace had to sacrifice Magan to prevent the spirits from abusing her new Time Lord powers.

Around the same time, Tannis banished Golcrum to Anima Persis as punishment for insubordination. Golcrum found only Ace's TARDIS, Ace lying unconscious nearby, and a ruined village without bodies. Together they left the planet, with Ace convinced that she had abused her powers and killed all the survivors. The Seventh Doctor later told her that the planet had been abandoned for centuries, and Magan and the other survivors were themselves constructs of the spirits. (WC: Death Comes to Time)

Antagonista was a planet which was home to hordes of hungry zombies. Charles Abbott teleported Sammy Jones to Antagonista using Incredulitas 4. He then wrote a series of books based on what happened.

After discovering Sammy's fate, the Twelfth Doctor and Eliza Jones came to Antagonista and rescued Sammy from zombies which were about to eat him. (COMIC: Shock Horror)

entities.name: Antalin
entities.description:
Antalin's ocean world, more often referred to as simply Antalin, was a planet covered entirely in water, with no islands, continents, or any land masses. There seemed to be no native civilisations, but marine life included fish.

The planet was discovered and hastily surveyed 50 years prior to c.4000, located in human space but close to the Daleks' border. At some point, most likely c.4000, the Daleks built a drilling rig on Antalin to gain new supplies for their war efforts, but the rig was destroyed by Space Security Service agent Dryn Faber. (PROSE: War of the Daleks)

entities.description:
Antara IV was a planet. The Energies Black Market was a market on Antara IV. Bloorm Vungah Bart Slitheen, Dax Fex Fize Slitheen and Korst Gogg Thek Lutiven-Day Slitheen were planning to sell Luke Smith's telekinetic energy on the market. They put Luke onto a machine and were starting to harvest his energy. Only a few seconds later, Luke was able to escape. In the end, the Slitheen weren't able to sell his telekinetic energy. (PROSE: The Lost Boy)

entities.name: Anu
entities.description:
The planet Anu was home to an advanced civilisation. The inhabitants of Anu were humanoid, but taller than average humans. They had white hair and lifespans of almost a thousand years. They had the technology to regrow lost limbs, but not brain tissue. Anu was destroyed by Qataka. (PROSE: Timewyrm: Genesys)

An Azukoi was a creature native to Anu. (PROSE: Timewyrm: Revelation)

"" is also the name of the king of the gods in Sumerian, Assyrian and Babylonian religions. In Sumerian, the name can also be the term for "the heavens" and is used interchangeably. In Egyptian mythology, Anu is one of the many names Anubis went by.

entities.name: Anubis
entities.description: Anubis was a planet in a binary star system. It was home to the Anubians and possibly the Huducts, who enslaved the former. The predatory Yakoclaws and their prey the Glombs also lived there. K9 Mark I visited the planet thousands of years before 2050 and liberated the Anubians from the Huducts. Although he left with the understanding the Anubians and the Huducts would reconcile in peace, this peace didn't last. The Anubians subsequently enslaved the Huducts and went on to create a large empire. (TV: Curse of Anubis)

entities.name: Aoris
entities.description:
Aoris was a planet where the past and the future were engaged in a complex temporal war.

While travelling through the Time Vortex, the TARDIS accidentally collided with a Time Tank which had come from the planet Aoris. Arriving on the planet, the Fourth Doctor discovered that soldiers from the planet's future were going back thousands of years to steal vital resources from their "negligent" ancestors while the past soldiers planted bombs on timed circuits to attack their descendants. Naturally concerned about the temporal implications of this struggle, the Doctor was eventually able to help the leaders of both sides realise the dangers of this approach. He arranged matters so that the inhabitants of the future timeline could travel forward another thousand years while a select few remained in their present to oversee the start of the planet's reconstruction and allow it to repair itself in the absence of its population. (AUDIO: /)

entities.name: Apalapucia
entities.description:
Apalapucia was a paradise planet and the native world of the Apalapucians.

Apalapucia was a fabulously beautiful planet of soaring spires, silver colonnades and the mirrored Glasmir Mountains. The planet had a pinkish-purple sky and an oxygen-rich atmosphere. According to the Eleventh Doctor, it was 2 billion light-years away from Earth, and it was voted the #2 destination for the discerning intergalactic traveller. (TV: The Girl Who Waited)

By the time the Eleventh Doctor, Amy Pond and Rory Williams landed on Apalapucia, the planet had been infected by an outbreak of Chen-7, a disease swiftly fatal to two-hearted races such as Time Lords and the native Apalapucians.

The Two Streams Facility was set up to care for the infected population, and through the use of temporal technology, allowed them to live through their entire life in a day. The facility was staffed by the Handbots, robotic nurses who patrolled the facility.

entities.description:
Aprilia III was the third planet in the Aprilia star system, in Mutter's Spiral.

The planet had a unique radiation belt that prevented the functioning of transporters and apparently interfered with subspace communications.

The planet had green vegetation and animals, including a lizard-like creature with six legs and bird-like creature. (COMIC: Assimilation²)

An alien civilisation built a relay station on Aprilia III some centuries before the 23rd century. It was abandoned and left untouched, but was still powered.

entities.description:
The Aqua planet was a planet home to the aquamonsters. The planet was partly dry, but there were oceanpheric currents of invisible liquid which moved around the surface, usually carrying aquamonsters within them.

When the First Doctor, Ian Chesterton and Barbara Wright landed on the aqua planet, Ian noted fish flying. It turned out that they were actually swimming in invisible liquid. The oceanpheric current caught up to them but quickly moved away. (COMIC: Dr. Who on the Aqua Planet)

entities.name: Aramuko
entities.description:
Aramuko was a planet, on which the Zokadyll founded the Xenopsychology Library of the Zokadyll.

The days and nights on Aramuko were longer than those of Earth. (COMIC: Vortex Butterflies) The planet also had multiple moons. (COMIC: The Good Companion)

The Tenth Doctor, Gabby, Cindy and Noobis visited Aramuko, where Noobis stayed behind. He met an Osiran, Siffhoni, who was actually Aspect Blue in disguise. (COMIC: Vortex Butterflies)

The Doctor later returned to Aramuko, along with Cindy and Cleopatra Hunsicker, where they met with Noobis and "Siffhoni". While they were there, the Time Sentinels moved the Circle of Transcendence above Aramuko, destroying one of its outer moons. (COMIC: The Good Companion)

entities.name: Arcadia
entities.description:
Arcadia was a human colony located in the Damascene Cluster. (TV: Kiss Kiss, Bang Bang)

The colony was established in the 26th century, (PROSE: Deceit) though the Matrix had record of it existing in the 24th century. (AUDIO: Neverland) The Seventh Doctor visited Arcadia and found it to be a non-technological paradise which served as a living specimen for a centuries-long experiment. (PROSE: Deceit)

The Sixth Doctor once decided to take Frobisher and Peri to Arcadia. He told of its "rolling fields, glittering still lakes and vast cloudless skies". However, he landed on the Mayflower by mistake. (COMIC: Profits of Doom!)

Later, the Eleventh Doctor took Amy Pond to Arcadia. She told the Doctor that he was being exceptionally nice to her by taking her to Arcadia, suggesting that she had had a pleasant experience. (TV: Vincent and the Doctor)

entities.description: According to the non-narrative source The Torchwood Archives, Arcateen V was one of six civilised planets in the Arcan system. It was home to more artistic Arcateenians than Arcateen IV and most of the population were artists, singers and poets who travelled the galaxy spreading their talent.

entities.name: Archetryx
entities.description:
Archetryx was a planet with temporal shields (powered by gravity wells) which kept the planet a minute ahead of the rest of the universe. It was located in the same system as Etra Prime. (AUDIO: The Apocalypse Element)

The Morestran Orthodox Church was based on Archetryx. (PROSE: Zeta Major)

Archetryx was host to the treaty attended by twenty of the Temporal Powers. This was later known as the Archetryx Convention. At the time, the Daleks returned Etra Prime to the universe on a collision course with Archetryx. The planet suffered extreme damage, but there were survivors. Romana II, Lady President of Gallifrey, promised the Sixth Doctor that she would aid the planet in its recovery. (AUDIO: The Apocalypse Element)

A convention was held on Archetryx to settle a dispute between the Unvoss and the Nekkistani. (AUDIO: Enemy Lines)

entities.description:
Archimedes was a planet which was home to a human colony owned by the Fountain Corporation. The Seventh Doctor arrived on Archimedes by accident, having attempted to travel to Maruthea.

UniMedia reporter Huksley went there to investigate the Fountain Programme and discovered a connection between it and a number of strange deaths on the colony. The Doctor, who had arrived in Huksley's flat, helped her uncover the truth, which was that her story was a hoax manufactured by UniMedia to increase their ratings. (PROSE: The Infinity Season)

During the Last Great Time War, it acted as a sanctuary for the sick and injured. It was protected by a planetary sized state of temporal grace, which was also sentient. (AUDIO: The Good Master) Arcking originally contained a power source which could have won the war for either side. When the Daleks got there first, the planet was time locked. (AUDIO: The Devil You Know)

Arcking was itself a fixed point in time. (AUDIO: The Good Master)

entities.description:
Arcturus was a planet in the Galactic Federation and the home world of the Arcturans.

The Osirans had an orbital Mobius strip near Arcturus. (PROSE: River of Time)

A Von Neumann probe landed on Arcturus and started to build a city, despite the planet already being populated. (PROSE: The Big Hunt)

Arcturus lacked mineral wealth. Its ambassador, Arcturus, attempted to prevent the planet Peladon from joining the Federation so it could forge a personal alliance to take their minerals. This plan failed when Arcturus was killed. (TV: The Curse of Peladon)

entities.description:
Arden was the homeworld of the Shenn. It was a planet of hills and forests. It had more than one continent.

In 2670, humans established the stage one colony on Arden. They constructed many bases. Among them were Touchstone Base, located on the northern continent, and Oberon Survey Camp, near the Phebe mountain range. (PROSE: Shadowmind)

Hypergems were found in great quantities on Arden, though the colonists named the gem oberonite (due to the proximity of where they were found). (PROSE: Shadowmind)

Ardethe was a planet in the constellation Kasterborous. It was the seventh in its ten planet system and was entirely covered in blue rocks. It had a great secret protected by the Knights of Jeneve, who would instead give hopeful travellers the coordinates of a mysterious planet where they had built a booby-trapped replica of Emmanuel College in Cambridge. (PROSE: Deadfall)

The Mother and Father of the Shadow Spire saw campfires of "ritual and bone" hiding in Homeworld ruins on Ardethe. (PROSE: The Story So Far...)

entities.name: Argentia
entities.description:
Argentia was a densely-populated planet and tax haven visited by the Fifth Doctor (AUDIO: Serpent in the Silver Mask) and the Seventh Doctor. (AUDIO: Kingdom of Silver)

The Fifth Doctor arrived with Adric, Tegan and Nyssa, looking to acquire a diothanine crystal so he could make a new sonic screwdriver. Here they were admitted into the funeral of wealthy mining magnate Carlo Mazzini. When his son Angelo was murdered the planet was put on temporal lock-down, with no time travelling vehicles being able to come and go. (AUDIO: Serpent in the Silver Mask)

entities.name: Argolis
entities.description:
Argolis was the barren planet located in the Mutter's Spiral galaxy that was the homeworld of the Argolins. The Argolins' warmongering culture led to the devastation of their world and the near-extinction of the race.

Argolis was located in a star system with four suns, and was located ninety-three light years from Earth. (PROSE: Doctor Who and the Leisure Hive)

Argolis was originally known as Xxbrmm and was home to a large number of tribes which shared a warrior culture and chivalric values. The tribe known as the Argolins eventually subjugated the rest of the planet and renamed it Argolis, which was generally considered to be an improvement. (PROSE: Doctor Who and the Leisure Hive)

The development of high technology did not curb the aggressive ways of the Argolin people, which eventually led to catastrophe when they encountered the equally belligerent Foamasi. In 2250, a 20-minute war between the two devastated both Argolis and Foamas, leaving all the Argolin survivors sterile.

entities.description:
Argone was the planet to which Piritus Elgon was confined for his "scientific crimes". Confined to a castle prison, however, Elgon managed to continue his genetic experiments resulting in the creation of a new species, the Screamers, a product of human and Argonian DNA. The Screamers were confined to the castle following Elgon's death by the authorities on the Eleventh Doctor's request. (COMIC: Screamers!)

entities.description:
Argos was a planet located three or four galaxies away from the Pristatrek Galaxy. The Doctor once defeated Luminus there, and "averted a catalogue of disasters". (PROSE: Tragedy Day)

When the Tenth Doctor gave Gerry Hobbes-Mayhew a portable immersion heater, Kate Maguire asked whether he had got it from Planet Zog. The Doctor replied, "No. Argos." (PROSE: Autonomy)

The Doctor mentioned her sonic screwdriver had been made at Argos, which her companion Gayle Tuesday confused for the shop. (TV: Untitled). Category:Planets Category:Planets visited by the Doctor

entities.description:
Arides was a planet that was home to a species of flowering plants, the pollen of which was deadly to all human and animal life. At some point, these plants mutated into a giant form. If they flowered they would spread the pollen through space, destroying life on all planets in the universe.

To prevent this, the people of Jevo sent an expedition commanded by Kirid to Arides to spray the plants with poison. The mission was successful, but at the cost of the Jevo ship, which was destroyed by the Daleks. (COMIC: The Emissaries of Jevo)

entities.name: Aridius
entities.description:
Aridius was a planet originally covered by oceans. Due to a stellar incident, its orbit around its suns turned the planet into a desert over a thousand years.

Aridius had high levels of oxygen and its gravity was a little greater than Earth's. (TV: The Chase)

After the ocean planet had become a vast desert, the only remaining species were the amphibious Aridians and the octopus-like Mire Beasts. To control the Mire Beasts the Aridians blew up sections of the city that had been overrun.

The First Doctor, with companions Ian Chesterton, Barbara Wright, and Vicki Pallister, visited Aridius, but were tracked by the Daleks, who pursued them in a time machine. The Daleks tried to force the Aridians to hand the Doctor and his companions over, but they escaped before the Aridians could do so. One of the Daleks guarding the TARDIS was tricked into falling into the tunnels, enabling the TARDIS crew to escape. (TV: The Chase)

entities.description:
Arkannis Major, also known as Colony world 4378976.Delta-Four, was a planet far away from Earth. It was colonised by humans by 2775, by which time it had a population of 20 million. Its inhabitants knew it by many names, such as Journey's End, Discovery, and Pioneer.

Due to micro-organisms in its atmosphere, anyone living on the planet started to believe things they imagined (as well as fictional works) were real, resulting in the outlawing of fiction in the planet's only city. (PROSE: The Stealers of Dreams)

entities.name: Arkheon
entities.description:
Arkheon, also known as the Planet of Ghosts, was a planet located near the Crab Nebula, just past the Pleiades, and left of the Blue Star Worlds. Temporal echoes resembling ghosts roamed the surface due to the Arkheon Threshold, a time rift in the planet's core. The world was virtually destroyed by the Daleks.

During the First Dalek Incursion of the Second Dalek War, Arkheon was hit by a "Planet-splitter" missile. The missile strike destroyed half of the planet, exposing the core. The fallout killed most of the Arkheonite inhabitants. The survivors eventually mutated into mindless, savage beasts.

Forty years later, the Doctor and the crew of the Wayfarer discovered that the Daleks had turned the area around the core into a slave labour mine using the colonists who evacuated Auros in an attempt to locate the Threshold and use it to become masters of time. They also used the base for experimentation. The group was captured by the Daleks and the Doctor admitted who he was. He was tortured by Dalek X before being given a tour of the base. The Doctor defeated the Daleks, and Earth Command sent in forces that destroyed the remaining Daleks and freed the prisoners, and the Doctor sealed the Threshold, so that the Daleks could not exploit it. (PROSE: Prisoner of the Daleks)

entities.name: Armagedos
entities.description:
Armagedos was an Earth Empire colony planet that was invaded by the Daleks.

The people of Armagedos had a conflict with the Daleks. When they found out that the Daleks were planning an invasion, they organised an evacuation to a colony where they wouldn't be found, gathering every ship they could find but realising that the Daleks would reach Armagedos before everyone could escape. The only option was to fight them and hope the Daleks could be held off until the last transport ship could enter hyperspace. Captain R'ar'Han'e reported the Dalek fleet to the the fleet at the moon of Devokos. Armagedos' best warships armed to the teeth with atomic cannons and polaron missiles engaged the Dalek fleet in battle, which numbered at least a dozen, pouring out armies of Daleks. Soldiers were sent into space to fight the Daleks but were swiftly exterminated.

Armagedos then found a solution, by reversing the polarity of the neutron flow in the cannons it could penetrate the Dalek's shields, managing to destroy a few of them. Although the defence force was suffering heavy casualties, the Daleks weren't breaking through and transport ships managed to escape. As the last transport made a move, a Armagedos ship flew headlong into a Dalek warship, destroying it and sending its Dalek crew spinning out in to space like "little broken toys" as R'ar'Han'e described. It set them back long enough for the last transport to get away. The defence fleet then went into hyperdrive and escaped. Although Armagedos was taken by the Daleks, the evacuees were determined to defeat them and return. (PROSE: Battle of Armagedos)

During the Last Great Time War, Romana II acknowledged Armagedos as a planet which had been invaded by the Daleks. (AUDIO: Beyond)

Armstrong's Colony was a planet "verdant and lush with valleys and hills that seem to roll on forever". It was located in the Van Koll system. (PROSE: The Heroine, the Hero and the Megalomaniac)

The Seventh Doctor visited Armstrong's Colony with Ace and Hex. (PROSE: These Things Take Time)

Bernice Summerfield and Iris Wildthyme also visited the planet. (AUDIO: Excelis Dawns, Excelis Rising, Excelis Decays, The Plague Herds of Excelis) Bernice Summerfield searched for the Doctor's remains on the planet, but found nothing. (PROSE: The Shape of the Hole)

AS4 was a small rocky planet near Quadrant 747 and Quadrant 746 in the Arcturian system. It orbited the star Arcturus, had two moons, and was home to palm-like plants and birds.

AS4 was the site of the wrecked command ship of a long-lost Cyberfleet, where the body of Cyber-leader Zogron was found. (COMIC: Junk-Yard Demon)

In an attempt to tempt the Doctor into joining the Krillitanes in their plans in 2007, Brother Lassar suggested they could save Ascinta, as well as Perganon and the Time Lords, by using the Skasis Paradigm. (TV: ) Later, the Doctor, as Time Lord Victorious, suggested that Ascinta, Perganon, and Gallifrey could be among the worlds that would be saved as he contemplated stopping the Kotturuh from introducing death to the universe. entities.description:
Asgard was, according to one account, a planet-sized theme park where the Eleventh Doctor and River Song once picnicked on 5 May 5147. (PROSE: Picnic at Asgard) According to another, River Song's visit to Asgard saw her dine with the "old Gods" alongside the Tenth Doctor. This was one of the many times she asked him if he had ever counted the children who were on Gallifrey when he (supposedly) destroyed it, and, as always, he refused to answer. (PROSE: The Day of the Doctor)

Whatever its circumstances, River recorded the adventure in her diary. (TV: Silence in the Library, The Husbands of River Song)

entities.description:
It was the second planet in its system, orbiting a minor star at a distance of eighty-nine-million miles in a sparsely clustered area of Mutter's Spiral. It had an atmosphere with sulphuric acid clouds and an average surface temperature above six hundred degrees Celsius.

Ashkellia was in fact a giant particle accelerator built over a million years before the Fourth Doctor and Romana visited there. The Palace of the Old Ones was the control centre. It was used to explore the higher dimensions. (PROSE: Tomb of Valdemar)

entities.name: Ashtallah
entities.description:
Ashtallah was a planet that was the home of the Ashtallan race.

Ashtallah was an idyllic planet with "rolling green hills" and "blue sky". It was similar to Earth, but was much smaller than the human homeworld, despite having some similarities in its atmosphere and appearance. A large mountain range existed on the planet, bordering the valley of the Ashtallans. According to the First Doctor, it was on the other side of the galaxy from Earth. (AUDIO: The Invention of Death)

After the First Doctor, Susan, Barbara and Ian had left the Great White Hurricane in 1888, the Doctor attempted to use a temporal slingshot to return to 1963 London. Seventeen separate system failures caused the temporal slingshot to throw his TARDIS off-course and onto Ashtallah.

After the four had met the Ashtallans and discovered their immortality, the Ashtallans began dying off. It was soon discovered that Sharlan was the cause, using a sample of Barbara's blood, taken after she'd been injured, to kill her people in the hopes that a shorter lifespan might increase innovation. After Sharlan fell to her own plague and a vaccine had been developed for the rest of the Ashtallans, the TARDIS crew left the planet, pondering the impact that they'd had on Ashtallah. (AUDIO: The Invention of Death)

Askenflatt Minor was a leisure planet once visited by the Tenth Doctor and Rose Tyler. While they were staying at the Warp Hotel, which bragged about having the "best tea in the known universe", the pair were interrupted by several alien natives with microphones who started asking Rose what it was like to travel with the Doctor, whom they believed was the Champion of Askenflatt and would defend the native population against Hasval the Destroyer. (PROSE: The Hero Factor)

entities.name: Asmoray
entities.description:
Asmoray was a quartz planet wrapped around a copper core which acted as a giant natural electrical transmitter. It had two moons.

The Twelfth Doctor took Clara Oswald to Asmoray's Quartz Wastes, calling it a "stunning natural phenomena". He believed the planet to be devoid of life and was surprised to a building on the planet used for harvesting electricity. The Doctor and Clara were taken to Luther, the man in charge of the harvesting, and accused of trespassing. Upon investigation, they discovered alien entities lived within the planet's electricity and were killing the harvesters in defence after being repeatedly routed through the harvester. The Doctor used his sonic screwdriver to shut the machine down and free the Asmoray natives. (COMIC: The Body Electric)

entities.name: Astra
entities.description:
Astra was a planet, whose native inhabitants were known as the Astrans. In the 21st century, it was the core of the Astra Space Empire or Astran Empire, the closest space power to the solar system. There were frequent skirmish at the borders of the solar system between human space forces and Astran space fleets, ultimately resulting in a Space War in 2065. By the 25th century, however, the planet was home to an Earth colony.

The Astrans' capital city, located on Astra, was the city of Kapland.

In 2061, an election on Astra reelected the 610th Kaplan with 90% of the vote. (PROSE: Kaplan Assassinated!)

On 5 June 2065, after the Kaplan of Astra was assassinated, the new Kaplan departed Unity City to return to Astra. (COMIC: The Amaryll Challenge)

entities.name: Atharna
entities.description:
Atharna was a water planet with large oceans and pleasure cruisers. It had a floating city called Moslin which contained the Statue of Kithal, one of the Wonders of the Universe. It was populated with colonists from all over the universe.

As a result of time alterations from the Time Fracture, as well as the Kotturuh crisis caused by the Tenth Doctor, (PROSE: What the TARDIS thought of "Time Lord Victorious") the planet was re-written as being a desert planet with two suns rather than one.

In this altered timeline, Felicity, Sophie Russell and Brian the Ood crashed down when Brian was contracted to kill Sophie. After Sophie fled into the town of Moslin, the Eighth Doctor landed, expecting to find a water planet as well as the statue. He helped them to Moslin in order to get them healed from their wounds, none the wiser that Brian was an assassin or that there was another survivor of the ship crashing due to them fabricating a story about bandits. (AUDIO: He Kills Me, He Kills Me Not)

On their way to Moslin, the Eighth Doctor recalled Godfather Death, the situation they were in reminding him of it, and told Brian the story. The story caused the two to debate the morals of death, wondering if it was a natural part of life or if it could be fought against. (PROSE: The Knight, The Fool and The Dead)

The planet was eventually deserted when the Atkyans died out. (PROSE: One Step Forward, Two Steps Back)

entities.name: Atrios
entities.description:
Atrios was a planet which was devastated by a nuclear war with its neighbour Zeos. It was ruled by a monarchy, which was represented by Princess Astra. The planet's war effort was led by the Marshal of Atrios.

The third planet, sometimes called the 'Planet of Evil', blocked the view of Zeos from Atrios and vice versa. The Doctor destroyed this planet by rerouting missiles fired by the Marshal originally directed at Zeos. (TV: The Armageddon Factor)

Without the energy of the segment to keep her together, Astra's role as the sixth segment was passed on to Romana after the latter's regeneration. Astra began to unintentionally drain the life-force from her subject Atrions, causing the extinction of the Atrions. (AUDIO: The Chaos Pool)

In 2050, K9 Mark 2 absorbed the Hunger to prevent it from destroying Earth. He planned to evacuate the swarm the next time he was on Atrios because, as he explained, the planet had no carbon-based lifeforms. (TV: Black Hunger)

entities.description:
Atrox 881 was a planet with conditions similar to that of Mars. It was located eight light years from Hereafter. With the Eleventh Doctor's help, Ixyldir and the Tanssor clan colonised the planet.

The Doctor returned the planet nine-thousand years later, where he discovered that Ice Lord Azylax had named him Belot'ssar. (PROSE: )

entities.description:
Aubis was the homeworld of the Aubertides. The Grand Circle on Aubis was made up of thirty-six members comprised from six complete families.

When the Dubraxine family was thrown off of Aubis, they conquered six solar systems in the local area using biological weapons, used the proceeds of their economies to fuel new weapons research and conquered several more, after which they returned to Aubis to conquer it and slaughter their former tormentors. (PROSE: Human Nature)

entities.name: Augea
entities.description:
Augea was a planet whose days were equal to three of Earth's months.

Through an odd coincidence, the Doctor was involved with twelve quests which mirrored the . One of these tasks was to clean out the Augean Stable in a day, though due to the length of a day, Hercules and the Doctor finished the task with plenty of time to spare. The next task was to clean up after Cerberus, which the Doctor found to be much more difficult. (PROSE: Sting of the Zygons)

entities.name: Aurichall
entities.description:
Located in the Amazolian system, the planet was dominated by a nootropic volcano. Forced by the collision of rival noospheres to continuously erupt with flows of the Cyberon drug contained within, this volcano led to the creation of the Cyberons themselves, as well as the various pools and rivers which dotted the glass surface of the First City of Aurichall. (PROSE: The Blue Scream of Death)

Fred had some experience with the planet at a point in its history before the Cyber-War. There were multiple cultures with different languages at this point, with Lorelise being what the largest culture spoke. After the Cyberons made the planet more homogenous, Lorelise was the only language spoken and thus it also became known as "Aurichallian". (PROSE: Cyber-Hunt)

Humanity was aware of Aurichall during the Cyber-War, with Myna Nevaryn thinking of it as an "awful volcanic planet". (PROSE: Cybergeddon)

The "original Cyberon homeworld" was destroyed in 2989, along with the Cyberon King. When foreseeing these events in 2892, Box had theorised that Lauren Anderson would play a part, although she was uncertain. At any rate, the loss of the planet only slowed the Cyberons briefly (COMIC: Before the Storm) before they found themselves a new Cyberon Controller in the person of Dracula. (COMIC: Before the Storm, AUDIO: Curse of the Cyberons)

entities.name: Auros
entities.description:
Auros was a human colony world in the Kappa Galanga sector. It was a beautiful planet with equatorial rainforests, mountains, deserts, grasslands and oceans. Stella, Jenifa, Kuli and Vanessa Lakestaad lived there.

After it was attacked by the Daleks, the human colonists were forced to surrender. Rather than have their world fall to the Daleks, the survivors destroyed their own planet using Osterhagen technology. However it was a trick by the Daleks, who destroyed the flagship on the orders of Dalek X and enslaved the colonists, who were taken to help gain access to the Arkheon Threshold.

After the Daleks were defeated on Hurala, throwing the fleet into disarray, Earth Command dispatched a fleet to free the prisoners. The Tenth Doctor later told the immobilised Dalek X that the mission had been successful, the prisoners rescued and the guarding Daleks destroyed. (PROSE: Prisoner of the Daleks)

entities.description:
Autopia was a human colony devoted to meditation and luxury. All the work was performed by robot slaves. The Autopians shielded themselves from the rest of the universe's gaze with a planet-wide force field.

After the Tenth Doctor and Donna Noble helped free the robots, Autopia was turned into a spa planet. (COMIC: Autopia)

entities.name: Avalon
entities.description:
Avalon was a planet which was native to a species which later became known as the Cephlie, who had formed a highly advanced civilisation which used nanobots to manipulate the world around them. After their technology backfired, the Cephlie returned to a simple life. The planet was colonised by humans in the 22nd century, who were forced into a medieval lifestyle in response to the nanobots.

Avalon was divided up into several nations, one of which was Elbyon. The capital of Elbyon was Glazebry, and the capital of the South Share (one of the four regions of the nation) was Fluxford. The settlements Thule and Borea were located in the north of the nation, and Silverwood and Westhold were two other locations in Elbyon that were not far away from one another.

Avalon had several rivers, including the River Dellberry and the River Flux. The River Flux fed into the Circle Sea, a sea 500 miles in diameter formed by the impact of a meteorite. The Sea contained a group of islands called the Shadow Isles, and bordered the south and east of Elbyon. An ocean bordered the northwest of Elbyon, and in the southwest there was a Crystal Forest. (PROSE: )

The Cephlie were an advanced civilisation which ruled over and inhabited Avalon. They invented a system which was focused solar energy on large astronomical objects, such as the large array of dangerous asteroids present in the planetary system. This system included six artificial moons positions equidistantly around the planet, which simultaneously became a source of power for the planet. As well as this, the Cephlie invented highly advanced self-replicating nanobots, which were powered by the moons. Eventually the nanobot system became so highly sophisticated that it allowed the manipulation of energy, force, and matter via the mind. An immensely powerful master control was created to handle the most complex tasks.

entities.name: Avalone
entities.description:
According to one account, Melanie Bush travelled with Glitz for about six months before deciding to try to go home. On her way, she detoured to Avalone, where she worked at a holiday camp owned by Avalonian Resorts, Inc. Her progress towards Earth stalled and she resigned herself to life on Avalone. Two years after this, she chanced another run at Earth.

She hacked into computer systems to send a message to Glitz, asking her pick her up. Instead, she was "rescued" by Dr. Who and Jason, who imprisoned her in the Galactic Prison in the Land of Fiction. There, she met another prisoner, the Seventh Doctor. He, however, was a changed and considerably darker man than she had known. He revealed to her that he had manipulated her into leaving him on Iceworld because he knew what was coming (as Time's Champion) and couldn't have her as a companion. Incensed, she avoided his company and refused to travel with him in the TARDIS ever again. Ace, who was also much changed from the person that she had left behind on Iceworld, tried to calm her and explain the reasons why she and the Doctor were so much "harder" than the people she had known. Although the explanation did little to dispel her disillusionment, Mel accepted a ride from Ace. Mel thus returned to Pease Pottage in the 1990s thanks to Ace's time hopper. (PROSE: Head Games)

entities.description: Averon was a planet located in the Adelphine Cluster on the Galactic rim. The native sentient species, the Averonians, were reptilian humanoids. They controlled the worlds known as the Averon Union. The planet was decimated by the Landoran Alliance, but Averon inflicted a ninety percent casualty rate on the Landoran fleet. (PROSE: A Device of Death)

entities.name: Axista Four
entities.description:
was a previously-uninhabited planet colonised by the Tyrenians and then humans during the 25th century.

When the Earth Federation outlawed genetic engineering circa 2439, Stewart Ransom organised the escape from Federation space of the Tyrenians, genetically-modified human super-soldiers with canine features created by his colleague Gustav Tyren. The vessel took the Tyrenians to the uninhabited Axista Four, where they established their own settlement.

In that year, Axista Four was also chosen by Ransom an as ideal planet to establish an Independent Earth Colony. The colonisation was part of the Back to Basics movement, which argued that humans had grown too reliant on technology since the 20th century. 5,000 human colonists travelled to the planet in a ship called The Big Bang. Ransom did not know the Tyrenians had already settled there, having mistakenly used the same raw data to select the planet that he had used to program the Tyrenian escape vessel.

As a result of the mix-up, initial probes of the planet by the Federation discovered the Tyrenian presence and Ransom was instructed to wipe them out. Overcome with guilt, Ransom allowed his ship to be shot down by Tyrenian defence satellites. The ship crashed, killing many of the colonists, including Ransom, and leaving others, like his daughter Kirann, trapped in suspended animation without the medical experts to safely release them. While much of the details surrounding the crash were unknown to future generations of the colonists, the event became remembered as Planet Fall Day.

entities.description:
The aquatic world of the planet Azarius was home to an advanced species of aquatic creatures. They were technologically advanced, and had a desire to protect the ecological balance of their world. They constructed giant whale-like bio-bots to harvest the fish from the sea, which were designed to meet their needs as well as maintain the balance of life under the water. (COMIC: Whale Tale)

entities.name: Azimuth
entities.description:
Azimuth was a planet located at the nexus point between two solar systems. It was once invaded by the Daleks, but after they were defeated by the Seventh Doctor and Ace, the populace erected a statue of Ace naked with her baseball bat. (AUDIO: Daleks Among Us)

After the destruction of Skaro, (TV: Remembrance of the Daleks) Davros's escape pod crashed on Azimuth, where he contacted the Daleks and took over the planet. The Doctor, Elizabeth Klein, and Will Arrowsmith arrived while searching for the persuasion machine, twenty years after the Doctor's first visit. (AUDIO: Daleks Among Us)

entities.description:
Azure was a planet which was home to a human colony.

In the early 22nd century, the Empress cruise liner regularly made runs between Station 9 and Azure.

In 2116, Tryst, with the aid of Dymond, attempted to smuggle vraxoin to Azure. They were arrested by Fisk and Costa, with the aid of the Fourth Doctor, Romana II and K9. (TV: Nightmare of Eden)

In 2157, Azure was attacked by the Daleks shortly before their invasion of Earth. (PROSE: Lucifer Rising)

was a forbidden planet. It sat beneath a layer of atomised carbon. It had a human colony which was cut of from the rest of the Earth Empire after the colonists wouldn't agree to trade tariffs. This lead some to believe the colony had failed. Its original settlers were of Chinese and European descent. The planet had a vampire curse, and since vampires attacked during the night the cities needed to be mobile in order to follow the light. (PROSE: The Badblood Diaries)

The Seventh Doctor noted a place of worship on Betrushia was familiar to a Gallifreyan hall, English college or Balanystran learning block. (PROSE: St Anthony's Fire)

Balhoon was the planet from which the Balhoonians came. The solicitors Jolco and Jolco conducted business here. (TV: The End of the World)

Balhoon was also a member of the Galactic Federation. (COMIC: Reunion of Fear). A representative from Balhoon met with galactic presidential candidate Alpha Centauri. (AUDIO: Run)

The Beheaded Boy of Balhoon participated in the Intergalactic Fringe Festival, using his eponymous severed head during his juggling routine. (AUDIO: War Stories)

entities.description:
Ballustra had lush terrain and large bodies of water. It was abundant in Genellium. It had a population of eight billion. Letrus was Ballustra's moon. (AUDIO: The Invasion of E-Space)

A CVE appeared near Ballustra. It was the size of Letrus and growing. It quickly grew larger than Ballustra.

The CVE let out pressure waves that caused earthquakes and tsunamis. Fifteen percent of the population was said to have died on the first day.

A joint military and scientific group set out to investigate the CVE. They took the Doctor's TARDIS. Romana II and Adric were taken prisoner and delivered to Letrus. There they were questioned by Marni Tellis.

entities.name: Bandraginus V
entities.description:
Bandraginus V was a Vegan shipyard (PROSE: First Frontier) with a billion inhabitants. The Fourth Doctor called it "a planet of a thousand million souls".

Around 1878, Zanak materialised around Bandraginus V and destroyed it, (PROSE: First Frontier) mining all of its mineral wealth. The minerals extracted from the planet included oolion, an element which could only be found on Bandraginus V and Qualactin. Following this, the Captain super-compressed the planet and added it to his collection. Its remains were dropped into Zanak's core and expanded to fill in the space.

Some oolion stones were scattered around Zanak as a result. (TV: The Pirate Planet)

The name "Bandraginus V" is likely a reference to "", the home for one of the key ingredients in in Douglas Adams's The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy. The Pirate Planet was Douglas Adams' first contribution to Doctor Who.

entities.name: Baralda
entities.description:
Baralda was a planet in the Third Galaxy, neighbouring the galaxy's intellectual heart, Urbinia. It had "a vivid, abundant ecosystem."

In an alternate timeline in which the First Doctor's TARDIS landed on Urbinia instead of Kembel, the Daleks developed the Time Destructor. The Dalek Fleet attacked Baralda as a show of force prior to the Harvesting of Urbinia. First Citizen Togrok sent a distress call to Chancellor Atrias, the head of state on Urbinia but all the Baraldans were subsequently aged to death by the Time Destructor and the planet disintegrated in a matter of hours.

The Second Doctor later averted the timeline by averting the temporal collision which caused it. (AUDIO: Daughter of the Gods)

Barampa was an planet that was seen as a credible threat to the Braxiatel Collection. (PROSE: Parallel Lives)

Harmonious 14 Zink gave Zara the Time Ring he found on Barampa. (AUDIO: The Judgement of Isskar)

Markwood brought Bernice Summerfield to Barampa to assess the damage to the Trib Museum. (AUDIO: The Lost Museum)

entities.description:
The planet Barastabon was home to the Masterbakers of Barastabon, known for their high-quality confectionery.

Romana II went alone to Barastabon to get a sponge cake as a surprise for K9's birthday. The cake's trip through the Doctor's TARDIS, combined with the strange properties of the confectionery-based planet on which the crew had found themselves, caused the Cake to gain sentience. (PROSE: The Not-So-Sinister Sponge)

Romana also visited Barastabon with Clare Keightley to obtain edible ball bearings for the Doctor. (PROSE: Shada)

The Fifth Doctor offered to take Erimem and Peri to Barastabon to pick up a chocolate gateau. (AUDIO: The Church and the Crown)

entities.name: Barcelona
entities.description:
Barcelona was a planet where the inhabitants included dogs with no noses.

Having told Rose Tyler that she would've "love[d] it" prior to his regeneration, (TV: The Parting of the Ways) the newly regenerated Tenth Doctor set a course to Barcelona at 6PM of a Tuesday in October 5006. However, because of Roses’s uncertainty of the Doctor’s new incarnation, he cancelled this trip to take Rose back home to the Powell Estate on Christmas Eve 2006. (TV: Born Again)

After defeating Es'Cartrss of the Tactire, the Tenth Doctor decided he would venture over to planet Barcelona. (COMIC: The Forgotten)

While Christel Dee was describing where she planned to go on a summer holiday, she specified that she was going to Barcelona. She then clarified that she was referring to 'the city Barcelona - Spanish Barcelona - not the planet Barcelona', and that the planet had 'too many no-nosed dogs'. (WC: Doctor Who Minecraft)

entities.name: Barclow
entities.description:
Barclow was a dirty, unappealing planetoid in the Fostrix Galaxy. It was approximately four hundred miles in diameter. The sky was grey, the planet was muddy and there was no native life. The planet's usable atmosphere was only in a thin, fifty-mile belt.

Despite its lack of usability, Barclow was the cause of a war that lasted over a hundred twenty years, albeit not the most enthusiastic of wars. Though originally discovered by the Chelonians near the end of the Humanian Era, the humans from Metralubit found it shortly after.

Though neither side particularly wanted a war, they were influenced into setting up bases and preparing for it. Since the planet was so unwanted, the humans stalled with red tape. In the meantime, the human and Chelonian soldiers got along well and developed deep friendships. (PROSE: The Well-Mannered War)

entities.name: Barzilla
entities.description:
was a human-populated planet. Sara Kingdom once used it as a decoy to attract a Dalek invasion force. The plan, authorised by the Space Security Service, was to lure the Daleks to Barzilla to prevent them from attacking "the Big Four".

Sara made the semi-barren and largely defenceless world attractive to the Daleks by spreading a rumour that the planet's leader, Harker Libra, and she had discovered a huge vein of gold in one of the planet's abandoned diamond mines. This rumour got back to the Golden Dalek through one of the Daleks' humanoid spies. Because the Daleks saw the acquisition of wealth as a valid route to power, they were easily diverted to Barzilla — only to discover that the SSS had laid an effective trap for them. The entire Dalek fleet was annihilated.

Little was known about the planet outside of this incident. However, it had suffered from a nuclear attack some two thousand years before the Dalek invasion. This had rendered the planet less habitable. It was prone to long periods of drought because the nuclear bombardment had permanently changed the planet's weather patterns. (PROSE: The Outlaw Planet)

Some members of the colony ship, when they turned 18, decided to travel to Basla 19 after they learnt the truth about where they were living. In exchange, the inhabitants of the colony ship allowed Basla 19 colonists to visit their ship from time to time. (PROSE: A Good Life)

On one visit to Baspral, the Doctor prevented a seer from drowning a young boy. The boy grew up to be a ruthless dictator, responsible for the Great Cleansing in which millions of people died. The Doctor later visited Baspral in his sixth incarnation, during which time he underwent interrogation by the Inquisitor regarding his previous actions on the planet. entities.name: Bellus IV
entities.description:
Bellus IV was a planet on which a war was fought between humans and robots.

When the Seventh Doctor arrived a human commander, Deldran, took him quickly to the human headquarters. There, the remnants of a great experiment to simply turn off the robots had been halted by the death of the chief scientist. The Doctor finished the work, flipped the switch — and promptly discovered that the "human" side were robots, too. As he powered down for good, Deldran explained that the humans had died ages before, leaving the war running by robot proxy. When Deldran used his last bit of power to explain that the robots wouldn't have known what to do with peace, the Doctor echoed the sentiment, wondering if anyone was really built for peace. (COMIC: War World!)

entities.description:
Bessan was a planet home to the species of the same name.

As Brother Lassar disclosed whilst speaking with the Tenth Doctor, the people of Bessan had "some rather lovely wings". Before the year 1140, and ten generations prior to 2007, Bessan was invaded by the Krillitanes, with Lassar recalling that Bessan made a million widows in one day. The Krillitanes adapted the wings of the Bessan people to assume a bat form for their newer generations. The Esteemed Father, of the older, wingless generation, was recognised as the "Beast of Bessan". Following his encounter with Lassar from his perspective, the Doctor met Krillitanes who he surmised were of the first generations to have adopted the wings of the Bessan. He was aware that the entire Bessan civilisation was slaughtered. (TV: School Reunion, PROSE: The Krillitane Storm)

entities.name: Beta Caprisis
entities.description:
Beta Caprisis was a 26th century human colony. Bernice Summerfield was born there in 2540. (PROSE: Love and War) It was a member of an Earth-controlled alliance of planets that eventually became the Earth Empire.

Beta Caprisis, a Class M (Earth-like) planet, was the fourth planet in the Gamma Delphinius system. It orbited a binary, both of whose stars were Class G (Sol-like) stars; consequently, it was a warm planet, and snow did not fall. Benny remembered it as a "nice place" — full of parks and trees. (PROSE: Sanctuary)

Beta Caprisis was evidently a prosperous society, its citizens healthy and usually tall — Bernice Summerfield, at approximately 5'9", was of average height. (AUDIO: Just War) Society was very open-minded; it did not attach any stigma or shame to nudity, (PROSE: Just War) and was apparently quite tolerant of cross-species mating — in contrast to some contemporary societies, such as the Fifth Axis. (PROSE: Life During Wartime)

Animal-derived foods might have been enjoyed by the wealthy as a decadent luxury, (PROSE: Ship of Fools) but, in the 26th century, most food was artificially created — vat-grown meat was common. (PROSE: The Evacuation of Bernice Summerfield Considered as a Short Film by Terry Gilliam)

entities.description:
Betelgeuse V, (PROSE: Lords of the Storm) often called just Betelgeuse, was a planet mentioned several times by the Fourth Doctor. (TV: Destiny of the Daleks, et al.)

Betelgeuse V used to have a moon, though it was later destroyed. (PROSE: Lords of the Storm) The Third Doctor remembered seeing a double sunrise on Betelgeuse. (PROSE: The Loneliness of the Long-Distance Time Traveller)

On Betelgeuse there was no sarcasm, and shame was a terminal disease.

In the language of Betelgeuse V, "Ix" translated to "boy who is not able satisfactorily to explain what a Hrung is, nor why it should choose to collapse on Betelgeuse Seven". This was used as a nickname for Ford Prefect, whose father would not tell him about his experience of the Great Collapsing Hrung Disaster of Gal./Sid./Year 03758.

Romana II was once absent during a visit the Fourth Doctor made to Professor Chronotis, as she was standing for election as President of Bethselamin. (PROSE: Doctor Who and the Krikkitmen)

Bethselamin was a planet mentioned in The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, which had an overflow of tourists.

entities.name: Betrushia
entities.description:
Betrushia was a planet in the Massatoris system, rich in minerals and jungles.

Millions of years in the past, an advanced civilisation on Betrushia created an organic catalyst. It was meant to test species for survival traits, but it worked too well and consumed any living thing. Before being wiped out, the inhabitants built an artificial ring system to confine the catalyser to Betrushia.

By 2148, the new inhabitants of Betrushia, the Cutch and the Ismetch, were at war with each other. The Seventh Doctor and Benny became involved in the war, but it became moot when the Chapter of Saint Anthony targeted the planet, inadvertently freeing the catalyser. Betrushia was destroyed. (PROSE: St Anthony's Fire)

entities.name: Biblios
entities.description:
Biblios was a library planet which collected all the known data of the universe, except for data about weapons. It was tended by robot librarians.

The Vromyx and the Garynths each desired the data Biblios had collected on weapons and they fought to prevent the other from getting it, refusing to believe the robot librarians' claims that there were no such records. The war lasted for 47.63 years, preventing anyone else from gaining access to the library, until the Fourth Doctor arrived and learned of the situation from one of the librarians. He then blew up an empty storage building and told both the warring sides that it contained the super-weapon data, tricking them into assuming that there was nothing left to fight over. (COMIC: War of the Words)

At some point before the 21st century, Biblios was placed under the protection of the Galactic Heritage. (PROSE: The Tomorrow Windows)

In the 51st century, Jonathan Smith acquired on Biblios a diary entry by H. G. Wells describing the death of the Tenth Doctor at the hands of Smith himself. He was unaware that the Doctor had forged the entry so that he could capture Smith. (COMIC: The Time Machination)

entities.name: Birinji
entities.description:
Birinji was the first planet to be judged by the Kotturuh and later became home to the Free Undead.

Sometime during the Dark Times, the Kotturuh arrived on Birinji and judged how worthy the inhabitants were to the universe. They arrived at the decision of allocating the indigenous Birinjians a lifespan of three months while the native crystal moths lived on for eternity. (PROSE: The Dawn of the Kotturuh) One of the Kotturuh who judged the planet was Inyit, who, upon allotting a lifespan to a certain type of grass, determined they had arrived too early, which caused her to develop doubts towards the Kotturuh Design. Determined to stop the rest of her race, she fought against them and began a war against the Kotturuh, at the end of which nothing was left on Birinji. Inyit was exiled to rule alone over the dead planet. (PROSE: All Flesh is Grass)

Inyit dedicated herself to maintaining a garden on Birinji in a biodome, even after the beginning of the extinction of her people by the Tenth Doctor’s necrotic virus. She was visited by the Ninth Doctor and Ikalla who were seeking the last of the Kotturuh to try to save her. A Dalek scout ship attacked the dome to complete their orders of finishing off the Kotturuh, however was shot down by the HMS Donna commanded by the Tenth and Eighth Doctors. Whilst the Doctors and Inyit spoke, the mercenary crew of the Donna set to work repairing the dome. Whilst the Doctor and the Donna set off to defend Gallifrey from the looming Dalek attack, Ikalla remained on Birinji with the ailing Inyit. The Dalek Symbiont arrived on the planet to assassinate Inyit however she used the last of her power to judge it, leaving it with a lifespan of mere seconds, which also saved the Doctors from the onslaught of hybrids with it’s DNA. Having saved Gallifrey, the Ninth and Tenth Doctors returned to Birinji in time to witness Inyit’s death, passing on her energies into Ikalla. Becoming “something new”, Ikalla summoned her fellow freed vampires to Birinji and became their scion, freeing them from the fates of their former masters. The two Doctors reconciled as the Free Undead settled on the planet. When they eventually departed, the Tenth Doctor’s companion Brian chose to remain behind on Birinji. (PROSE: All Flesh is Grass)

entities.name: Birling
entities.description:
Birling was a human colony planet governed by HomeWorld, a planet in the same star system.

A Lopo outbreak occurred on Birling after those in opposition to the Governor of the HomeWorld, specifically the Professor of Acupuncture and Astrology, convinced the public on the system's planets that the vaccines against this old disease stunted children's growth in an attempt to prevent them from voting, and therefore prevent them from voting for the Governor. This, plus the restriction on ships carrying the vaccine to the outer colony, caused Birling to go into quarantine while the Honorary Chair of MedAuth, Helen, who was also the Governor's wife, was visiting, thus trapping her there. This was the first stage of the Governor's downfall as he spent so much time communicating with his trapped wife that he neglected to focus as much as he should have on the upcoming election.

The disease soon mutated and affected even the adults who were vaccinated as children. Many people died, including Helen. The government was then blamed for not having supplied enough vaccines, despite much of the reason that people weren't being vaccinated was due to the propaganda of the opposition. This bad publicity made the Governor fear not being re-elected, causing his Chief Advisor, Marianne Globus, to perform a "slight statistical correction" of votes to make sure he still won. (PROSE: The Blood Cell)

On his return visit, he discovered that a Rostrow space mission led by Lahk had arrived to gather plant specimens, unaware that they were taking intelligent beings prisoner. In return the Verdants were preventing the Rostrow ship from leaving. The Doctor, with the assistance of Duh, helped to make peace between the two peoples. (COMIC: Mission for Duh)

entities.name: Bixor
entities.description:
Bixor was a planet to which Duotheros sent the Sixth Doctor in order to find out its fate. It was destroyed because a worker creating a pair of trousers was distracted by the materialisation of the Doctor's TARDIS, causing a butterfly effect which lead to the planet's destruction. The incorrectly made trousers were purchased, and one day while the buyer was wearing them, the trousers fell down while in a crowded street. When people stopped to laugh at him, a pickpocket stole keys from the pocket of one of the laughing people. Upon locating the car the keys went to, the pickpocket gave away his bicycle to a nearby kid. The boy tried out his new bike, which was also the first bike he ever owned. His unsteady attempt at riding the bicycle caused him to go out onto the road, in the path of a large truck. The truck swerved to avoid the boy, and crashed into a substation which caused a power outage of an entire manufacturing sector. Once the power outage was repaired, the machinery in one of the affected facilities reactivated, causing sixteen vector modules to receive double printed circuits. The modules were installed in an aerial transport drone's guidance system. The drone was responsible for transporting dangerous materials to the capital's central nuclear power plant. The guidance system malfunctioned, just as the drone was passing over Bixor's only active volcanic fissure. The drone dived as fast as it could into the fissure, causing a chain reaction that destroyed the planet.

Upon learning that his own arrival had caused the destruction of the planet, the Doctor travelled back in time and planted a tree that would be fully grown by the time of his past self's arrival, blocking the view the worker would have had of the Doctor's arrival, meaning the worker was never distracted and made the trousers correctly. However, the Doctor noticed that other workers in a nearby building had noticed his most recent arrival. Not taking any chances, he travelled back one more day, and during the night, set up a series of mirrors to prevent his second arrival from being seen. With the changes he made, the planet was never destroyed, and only the Doctor retained the memory that it had ever been destroyed. (AUDIO: The Wings of a Butterfly)

entities.name: Blue Planet
entities.description:
The Blue Planet was a planet that was visually similar to Earth apart from the fact that everything was blue, including animals.

Viewed from space, the centre of the planet seemed to be bright white with in colour which turned into a dark blue around the edges. On the surface, blue trees, bushes and daisies flourished on very flat ground with there also being areas where only small rocks were present, with no plant life visible at all, similar to a desert. Another entirely blue celestial body could be seen from the surface which was either a sun or a moon to the planet. The planet had clouds that were white not blue.

The intelligent natives of the planet were blue humanoids and were all psychically identical to each other with silver-blue hair reaching just above the eyeline, small round noses and two round eyes of equal size. They all wore the same blue outfit which included boots which matched the shade of their faces. Blue dogs, birds, and earthworms also existed on the planet roaming freely with there even being a counterpart of a specific individual - Walter the Worm. In comparison the blue version was slightly longer than its Earth double. (PROSE: Dr. Sixth)

At some point, landed her TARDIS on the planet in the form of a pyramid and hypnotised the locals, taking control of their minds. She then set about building a clock that would twist time itself. Rather than a key, she used a corkscrew to wind up the Time Continuum.

entities.name: Boda
entities.description:
Boda was a forested planet with a forest moon in the Plim Galaxy. It had native forests, and gravity slightly stronger than that found on Earth.

Boda is home to a species of psychic trees, and a peaceful race called Producers who act as the trees' self-appointed guardians. (PROSE: Paper Moon)

The Thirteenth Doctor and her companions Yaz, Ryan and Graham visited Boda in the 54th century. Here they met the Producers, who were using the wood from fallen psychic trees to manufacture Psychic paper. The Producers only used wood from trees that had already died, and would not kill the trees deliberately.

At some point in her future, the Doctor is destined to save the Producers from a species of bark-eating wasps.

entities.description:
In a parallel universe, the Borg homeworld was located within Borg space in the Delta Quadrant. After breaking their alliance with the Borg, the Cybermen set a course for the Borg homeworld in order to take complete control of the Borg Collective. Ultimately, however, they were defeated before reaching their goal by the combined forces of the Eleventh Doctor, the USS Enterprise-D, and surviving Borg. (COMIC: Assimilation²)

Officially, the existence of a Borg homeworld is a hypothetical one as it has yet to be revealed in a Star Trek source. However, an identity for the Borg homeworld is given by the non-canon novel , which names it Arehaz.

entities.name: Bortresoye
entities.description:
Bortresoye was a planet located in the Divergent Universe. The planet was divided into a number of zones, with each zone containing vastly different environments and cultures. (AUDIO: The Last) The borders and spaces between the zones were occupied by the Interzone, and transit between the zones was carefully controlled by the Kro'ka. Some of the zones were fully aware of adjacent zones, while others were oblivious to their existence. (AUDIO: Scherzo, The Creed of the Kromon, The Next Life)

The Eighth Doctor and Charley Pollard arrived here when they were banished to the Divergent Universe, and spent many weeks crossing from zone to zone. (AUDIO: Zagreus, Faith Stealer)

The planet also had its own territories, containing at least two societies locked in national rivalry. These two regarded themselves as the pinnacle of evolution, going so far as to abandon natural procreation for their species. (AUDIO: The Last)

The Divergent Universe had an unending cycle of birth, progress, death and rebirth lasting tens of thousands of years. The Divergence, a powerful race trapped in this universe when it was created by Rassilon, resolved to break the cycle and escape to our own universe. As part of the experimentation to this end, they constructed a mobile platform (a planet, really) where they could conduct evolutionary experiments. The planet carried its own cycle of death and rebirth, similar to the surrounding universe, but with a much higher frequency. (AUDIO: The Next Life)

Bouken was a large, sandy world under human control. By the 40th century, large qualities of oil were discovered underneath the planet's surface.

Oil Corp began drilling on the planet using large mobile oil rigs. To make the planet warm enough for human workers, two artificial suns were placed in its system in addition to the single natural sun.

Captain Kaliko and her crew on the Black Gold also wanted the oil, by bringing down the rigs using ropes, as they and others like them couldn't afford Oil Corp's prices. (TV: The Infinite Quest)

After his arrest by the Judoon, Androvax had acquired a disk from a Bouken pirate he met on a swamp prison planet in the Calysteral cluster. He could use this to enter the vault on Earth owned by the Alliance of Shades. (TV: The Vault of Secrets)

On Britzit-247, there was a river which resembled the Thames, except it was made of molten lava. There was also a building that looked like Big Ben. (COMIC: Remembrance)

After defeating the Bannermen, Delta the Chimeron Queen, along with former human Billy, reached the brood planet with the Chimeron princess. After a few years, Delta said she would be able to reproduce the nucleus of an entire community, after which they could return to Chumeria and repopulate it completely. entities.name: Bruhl
entities.description:
Bruhl was the home planet of the Glacians, located beyond the G-star in Ambivalence Five. It was covered in snow and ice, with temperatures below 30 degrees Fahrenheit, and had several moons of various sizes. The alien Zilgors came to Bruhl and helped the Glacians advance their civilisation. Many years after they first arrived, they were trapped in ice by Rraprro, who made himself ruler of his people.

The First Doctor arrived on Bruhl and rescued Grahm, who had been accused of stealing a Zilgor thought-cube. They were both captured by the police and imprisoned, but were freed by Ffreuf, who hoped that the Doctor could help discover how to use the cube. After the Doctor learned from the cube what had happened to the Zilgors, Ffreuf and his rebels set out to rescue them, while Grahm took him back to the TARDIS. (PROSE: Justice of the Glacians)

As attacks by Natrium Worms on the outposts increased, relievingsalt traders of their cargoes, the salt trail was abandoned and was believed by many to be cursed. Only a few tribes of the bravest warriors remained to collect salt. These tribes of nomads lived in tents, moving between oases and watering holes using andromedaries for transport. entities.name: Cadoni 4
entities.description:
Cadoni 4 was an aquatic planet colonised by humans and later conquered by the Daleks.

Humanity had colonised Cadoni 4 in 3667 and the settlers had grown used to life in the Stanzari solar system during the following fifteen years, living in harmony with the native creatures and adapting to the extreme weather conditions that battered their home nine months of the year. In 3682, the Daleks invaded the planet, sending in hundreds of troops deep in the depths of the Kaye Ocean, surrounding an exploratory group, wasting no time and opening fire almost immediately, taking out one of the settlers' research vessels. As they fought for control of the seas, the crew sent radio communications back to base, passing on final messages to family and loved ones, already knowing they would not survive. The settlers returned fire but it was already too late. Within an hour the entire force had been wiped out and it was only a matter of days before the Daleks exterminated every last human on the planet. (PROSE: Sea Bed Struggle)

Brook allocated a force of 300 men, thought sufficient to take care of such a small force of Daleks. On landing, the 300 men were reduced to zero in less than five minutes. The Dalek Survival Guide counted this as the third greatest victory of the Special Weapons Daleks. In the aftermath of the "spectacular" victory, the Dalek Emperor deemed that the Special Weapons Daleks had proved their worth in battle and so ordered their full-scale reproduction. (PROSE: Dalek Survival Guide)

entities.description:
Calbaron III was a planet which during the 51st century was ruled by the tyrannical emperor Vimlox. In 5083, Vimlox was overthrown. In the same year, the Twelfth Doctor and Clara attempted to reserve a table at a restaurant. After being told they would have to wait three years, the pair returned in 5086, only to find the restuarant closed. They then travelled back in time to 5080 to book a table for their original arrival time. On this visit the Doctor noticed his TARDIS had been scratched, and after discovering this had been done by the emperor Vimlox the Doctor decided to overthrow him. (COMIC: Planet of the Diners)

entities.description:
Calderon IV was a planet the Third Doctor and Sarah Jane Smith visited. On Calderon IV, they met the android maker, whom they defeated in an hour and a half. The Doctor left a signal device behind in case they were needed again.

Five years later, the android maker made a perfect replica of the Doctor. He programmed it to murder and replace the Doctor so he could have an audience with Praesidium and assassinate him with an explosive in his head. However, the android became useless when it turned out the Doctor had regenerated. (PROSE: The Android Maker of Calderon IV)

entities.description:
Calderon Beta was described by the Eleventh Doctor as "Boring. Planet of the Chip Shops". However, it was home to a four-hundred-foot-tall tree "growing out of a clifftop on the north side of a mountain in the middle of the sea". At 12:12am on 21 September 2360, one could see more stars in the sky from the top of the tree than in any other point in history. The Doctor said, "You could read a book by it," before he took River Song there on their first night out during her imprisonment at Stormcage Containment Facility; however she indicated an interest in something other than reading. (HOMEVID: First Night)

entities.name: Calfadoria
entities.description:
Calfadoria (PROSE: Deadfall) or Calfedoria (PROSE: Legacy) was an inhabited planet. The Doctor had at one point met representatives of the Tri-Planet Alliance of Calfadoria. (PROSE: Business Unusual)

Calfedoria was home to the famous hospital and science base Cal-Med One. (PROSE: Legacy) Dr Aynn Kranten ran the Cal 2 Medical Research Facility on Calfadoria for eight years. (PROSE: Deadfall)

The people of Calfadoria illegally sent bio-engineered assassins to kill Sancroff, as they found his continued existence to be morally abhorrent. To preserve their alliances with other worlds, they programmed the assassins to kill all witnesses as well. (AUDIO: The Sirens of Time)

Calfadoria originally appeared in Gary Russell's 1986 Audio Visuals story Maenad.

The Tenth Doctor and Donna Noble visited Calibris to fix the TARDIS' fluid links. The criminal known as Gully was on Calibris searching for Time Reaver guns, which were brought here by Cora. This caused the Vacintians to come and enforce law and order on the planet.

There was also a smuggler's tavern locaten on this planet called Vagabond's Reach. (AUDIO: Time Reaver)
