Caligaris Epsilon Six was a holiday planet active in the 77th and 78th centuries. It was designed and constructed to resemble a fantastic medieval European version of Earth, complete with genetically engineered elves, cyborg dragons and robotic fairies.

On 19 April, 7711, Caligaris Epsilon Six was placed under planetwide quarantine for recombinant yersinia pestis, by the order of Chief Administrator Aethelred, who placed the planet under quarantine as part of his plan to become king. The quarantine was lifted some hundred fifty years later, with the assistance of the Eleventh Doctor and Amy Pond. (COMIC: A Fairytale Life)

His actions went unnoticed by the Time Lords as he delivered the shipment of Swenyo to Narvin. Originally, it had been Teremon's idea to wipe out the colonists. entities.name: Callufrax Minor
entities.description:
Callufrax Minor was one of the planets taken by the New Dalek Empire in 2009 and transported to the Medusa Cascade, where it joined twenty-six other planets. (TV: ) It was returned after Donna Noble defeated the Daleks and Davros. (TV: )

According to a computer readout at the Shadow Proclamation, the planet was uninhabited by 2009. The readout also said that its "size" was 62,137 kelix, its mass was 100,297.5 gaats, and its atmosphere was 27% olb. (TV: ) However, according to another account, a parasitic race called the Tactire lived there. (COMIC: The Forgotten)

Callufrax Minor was seemingly named as a reference to Calufrax, the last planet crushed by the space pirates of Zanak, and which was, in fact, a disguised segment of the Key to Time. (TV: The Pirate Planet)

entities.name: Calufrax
entities.description:
As a planet it was rich in voolium and madranite one-five, and the only place where they were known to naturally occur. This drew it to the attention of the crew of the pirate planet Zanak who needed the crystals to subdue the psychic Mentiads. However, Fibuli noted that it was "in an unexpected sector", and was hesitant in recommending the planet to the Captain, saying there was something "rather curious" about it.

Prior to this, the Doctor had visited Calufrax, which he found to be completely uninhabited, cold, wet and ice-coated. He considered the prospect of returning to Calufrax to be "paralysingly dull, boring, and tedious", and was immediately disappointed and angry that the tracer indicated that one of the segments of the Key to Time was there. He described it further as a "horrible place" and a "mean little planet".

It was the last world captured by Zanak and reduced to a trophy the size of a football. Its metricized structure, having a variable atomic weight, betrayed its origin as not a natural planet, but the second segment of the Key to Time. It was recovered by the Fourth Doctor and Romana I. (TV: The Pirate Planet)

Calufrax and the other carefully balanced planets inspired the Daleks' use of missing planets to transport the Earth in The Stolen Earth/Journey's End, one of which was named Callufrax Minor seemingly in reference to the planet.

entities.name: Cantus
entities.description:
At some point before the 27th century, the Cybermen invaded Cantus, converting all humans on the planet. The Cybermen created tombs beneath the surface of the planet and went into hibernation.

Irving Braxiatel travelled to Cantus with a Gallifreyan crystal and placed Ronan McGinley as the Cyber-Controller of Cantus, under his control. The Gallifreyan crystal became known as the Crystal of Cantus and gave a sense of mythology to the planet.

Years later, Braxiatel needed a new Cyber-Controller, and manipulated Jason Kane into going to Cantus with him. Braxiatel installed Kane as the new Cyber-Controller. After learning that this had happened to Kane, Bernice Summerfield took the Crystal of Cantus and used it to destroy all the Cybermen on the planet. (AUDIO: The Crystal of Cantus)

entities.description:
Capella Four (also known as Auriga) was a small, uninhabited world.

Capella Four was the fourth planet orbiting the double star Capella in the constellation Auriga. As both stars were quite hot, Capella Four was a warm world, with a desert-like biome.

Its native life was remarkable for its uniformity: native flora was dominated by plants resembling Earth's bracken fern (twenty-six species, all identical except for size), while native fauna was restricted to eighteen species of a nocturnal spider-like creature, also identical except for size. The fern-like plants and spider-like creatures were all consumable by humans. (PROSE: )

At one point in its distant past, the planet was an outpost of the now-vanished Aurigan civilisation.

A passing neutron star threatened to disrupt Caresh's orbit, making it uninhabitable. Lord Roche tried to change the neutron star's path to put Caresh into a closer orbit to Beacon, its warmest sun, though that would have caused the deaths of those living on Caresh's Southern Archipelago. With the Third Doctor's help, Roche instead moved Caresh into a closer, more stable orbit around its cooler sun Ember. (PROSE: The Suns of Caresh)

entities.description:
Carson's Planet was one of the many planets conquered by the Dalek Empire during their invasion of the Mutter's Spiral. It was later liberated from Dalek occupation by the Earth Alliance. Post-liberation, Carson's Planet became essentially a half-way house, being officially neutral. According to one bartender, the planet was swarming with thieves and murderers as well as spies from both sides, half-jokingly commenting that half of his customers could well have been Dalek replicants. (AUDIO: "Death to the Daleks!")

Carson's Planet originated as the main setting of Nicholas Briggs' Audio Adventures in Time & Space story Cyber-Hunt, where it was a warzone in the conflict between humanity and the Cyberons. The Audio Visuals Doctor visits Carson's Planet and frees it from the Cyberons, allowing it to be resettled by humans. In 2021, this story was adapted into a novelisation.

The solar system which Carsus belonged to also included the planets Minerva, Schyllus, Tessus, Lakertya, Molinda, and the lifeless outer gas planets Hollus and Garrett.

The surrounding area of space was known for its spatio-temporal anomalies, including temporal waves, reports of strange matter fragments and chronic threads, and rumours of a supernova that exploded in the distant past but mysteriously left no traces. (PROSE: Spiral Scratch)

entities.name: Cartago
entities.description:
Cartago was a colony world of the Homeworld. The Homeworlders' occupation of the planet was centred around a domed city, known simply as Cartago. It was built close the green ocean, which was home to large, carnivorous chelonians. Silverleaf palm trees could be found near the shore. The "southern plate-steppes", under which aquifers ran, were home to the native Riverfolk.

It was ruled by the Governor, and the Governor's scion, the Corsair, was born on Cartago. As a young boy, he was accompanied to the Homeworld to undergo initiation; he was accompanied by the Monk, another colonist, rather than his father, who was busy with "an urgency in the Cartago colony". He attended Cahlough Academy for a while but found little in common between himself and the autochthonous Homeworlders, choosing to return to Cartago against the Governor's wishes. There, the Monk undertook the younger Corsair's education personally, teaching him fencing with the silverleaf palm trees for target practice. (PROSE: The Bloodletters)

In the first Corsair Queen story, The Tigress of the Seas!, shortly after the Governor (whose name was given as Cedric Evans) returned to Cartago from an official visit to another unspecified colony, Cartago was ransacked and burnt down by a pirate crew. Escaping with the help of a seasoned sailor nicknamed "Monk", whom the Governor had assigned to protect his daughter but who ended up teaching her "roughneck ways" instead, Lila snuck aboard the pirates' nearly-abandoned vessel and took control of it, before sinking the pirates' rowboats with their own ship's cannons. Taking control of the ship, she named herself "the Corsair Queen" and swore revenge on all other pirates, with the Monk remaining by her side.

entities.name: Carthedia
entities.description:
was a planet which acted as a government state for the Sunlight Worlds. It was recorded as a member of the Earth Alliance but was more closely affiliated with the Dalek Foundation.

Terrin and Alyst Blakely, along with their children, Sabel, Ollus and Jenibeth, all came from Carthedia, as did Hellic Dansard.

On a mission from Gethria to Carthedia, the charter ship KS55NZ/4 was attacked by Daleks, and Terrin and Alyst committed suicide to avoid revealing vital information to their attackers. The Eleventh Doctor answered their distress call, and discovered their three children, Sabel, Ollus, and Jenibeth. He then piloted the ship to Carthedia himself. (PROSE: The Dalek Generation)

entities.name: Catalog
entities.description:
Catalog was a library planet. According to the Seventh Doctor, it was "the greatest library in the universe". At the time he visited, the planet's staff had relatively recently converted their storage system. Instead of trying to locate their wealth of data across the planet's physical space, they archived it in time. Things beginning with the letters A-L were housed in the past, M was the present, and N-Z were housed in the future.

Because Catalog's resources were so great, however, the collection reached so far back and forward through time that it was a major temporal event. It attracted the attention of bugs that, according to the Doctor, were "forces of chaos" which usually resided only at the Big Bang and the collapse of the universe. The bugs' continued feeding on the Catalog-generated timelines was a serious threat to the stability of the web of time.

The Doctor ended the threat only by depriving the bugs of their food. He collapsed Catalog's collection back into real space. Suddenly, the entirety of the collection returned to physical books and records scattered across the surface of the planet. Typically, the Doctor left the Foreign Hazard Duty team called in to deal with the bugs to clean up — something he estimated would take about a century. (COMIC: Hunger from the Ends of Time!)

entities.name: Catastrophea
entities.description:
was the second name of the planet originally called Kastopheria after its discoverer, Elias Kastopherious. By the time the Third Doctor and Jo visited the planet, it was almost exclusively called "", and its capital city was Catastrophea City.

It had a temperate, subtropical climate and was incredibly fertile. Though possessed of no minerals to speak of, a variety of exotic fruits and rare medicinal plants grew there. This fecundity proved a double-edged sword, bringing both bounty and tragedy to the planet.

After Kastopherious discovered the planet, human colonisation came slowly. When it did, the humans discovered that the natives were pliable. They were apparently happy being farmhands. Eventually, the human colonists sold out to the Kastopheria Company. All the humans became wealthy but, reduced to the role of overseers, they turned on the native population. Since their wealth was now tied to hitting productivity targets imposed by the company, they began to mistreat the natives to get them to work more.

Over time, some of the agricultural land was converted to growing more dubious drugs. The mild, somewhat-legal Jokkarta and the harder, absolutely illegal skar — which Jo Grant called "a cross between LSD and cocaine" — were grown on the planet.

entities.name: Cathon
entities.description:
Cathon was a planet inhabited by mole-like people that was ravaged by war in the distant past. This war ultimately resulted in one of the sides cybernetically enhancing their soldiers, creating what would be come to known the Silex. When the time came to deactivate the Silex, they revolted against their creators and poisoned the air of the surface, forcing them to flee underground. The Cathonians constructed large drilling vehicles in order to navigate the through the planet's brittle crust. These vehicles sustained themselves by constantly consuming various ores that could be fed into their furnaces to keep them running and could be as big as a house or the size of small town. Eventually the Silex pursued the Cathonians underground and systematically hunted down all the drill towns, harvesting their people and converting them into Silex. Over the years the number of drill towns dwindled until only a handful remained unclaimed by the Silex. The Silex were ultimately defeated by the Fourth Doctor and Romana II, and shortly after it was discovered that the poison on the surface had long since cleared up, allowing the Cathonians to start rebuilding their civilisation. (AUDIO: Subterranea)

entities.name: Celeste
entities.description:
Celeste was a planet owned by Intra-Venus, Inc. which was mined for its rubies. When the miners revolted, Josiah W. Dogbolter brought in soldiers and the Wrekka to deal with them.

The Fifth Doctor and Gus Goodman landed on Celeste. They were pursued by soldiers for breaking curfew until they fell into an underground tunnel. While looking for a way out, they were captured by the Wrekka and taken to Dogbolter, who mistook them for the rebel leaders. When he was told that the Doctor came to Celeste in a time machine, he offered to buy it from him, but the Doctor turned him down. When the miners attacked Dogbolter's office, the Doctor and Gus ran back to the TARDIS and left the planet. (COMIC: The Moderator)

The Death's Head Interactive Archive mistakenly referred to the planet as Corundum, perhaps in reference to the Corundum Mining Company. (COMIC: The Incomplete Death's Head)

entities.name: Centauri-Beta
entities.description:
Centauri-Beta was a habitable planet twenty-six light-years away from Earth. It was known to human scientists in the 2060s.

Centauri-Beta had pink skies and golden light, and a cool and still atmosphere through which constellations of stars were visible during the day. In at least one region, it had sweeping valleys bordered by tall rocky crags.

Long meadowy grass was found all over the ground on Centauri-Beta. At high altitude, the grass emitted pheromones which could be intoxicating to humans.

In 2070, after designating Centauri-Beta as a potential “new Earth”, humans sought to colonise the planet. This occurred early on in the Unified Earth era, a time of planetary unification which followed a great war. During this time, the colony ship Heart set out to reach Centauri-Beta. This mission became a symbol of hope for all of humanity, and the launch was watched by nearly everyone on Earth. However, this mission was doomed to fail since the technology humans possessed at the time was insufficient to make the journey safe. However, project Heart was allowed to continue, with the ship’s inevitable disintegration being explained as a “hyperdrive” transporting the ship and crew far away from the Earth in a split-second.

entities.description:
Centuria was one of Earth's colony holiday worlds. It had its own police force and was powered to an extent by nuclear energy. It had two suns, a large yellow one and a smaller, orange one which rapidly orbited. A newspaper was published on the planet, called the Centuria Times.

Large portions of the planet were temperate, and had attactive beaches which were popular with holidaymakers. Other areas were less populated, such as Azlon, Centuria's most deserted continent, (COMIC: Drones of Doom) and Centuria's arctic zone, which was home to Ice Snakes. The arctic zone was rich with the precious resource of Hargstones, which could be mined beneath the ice. (COMIC: Enemy Mine)

During the 41st century an interplanetary info-thief stole Cybermen blueprints from the Torchwood Archive and used them to built new Cybermen with the intent of auctioning them off as hi-tech soldiers. The Cybermen took over and threatened the planet, but were shut down by the Tenth Doctor and Jayne Kadett. (COMIC: The Power of the Cybermen / Drones of Doom / Enemy Mine / Time of the Cybermen)

entities.name: Ceres
entities.description:
Ceres was a dwarf planet in the Sol system, located in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter. (AUDIO: The Bounty of Ceres)

Ceres was home to the Cerulians before their civilisation was destroyed by an incoming asteroid. (TV: Sirens of Ceres)

Ceres was later visited by the First Doctor, Vicki and Steven. By this time, the dwarf planet was devoid of any native life forms. A Cobalt Corporation mining base was located there. (AUDIO: The Bounty of Ceres)

In Steven's time, the political situation on the dwarf planet was akin to that of East and West Berlin in the 20th century. Steven and his fellow students weren't allowed to talk about Ceres, so they instead alluded to it through the 5D representations of East Berlin they built in class. (AUDIO: The Anachronauts)

WorldCorp, under the guidance of its employee Gaskill Tyran, undertook a programme to actively conceal the existence of Ceres Alpha's former inhabitants, lest they ruin their profit margin. (PROSE: Dark Progeny)

The Eighth Doctor told Scarlette that he had recently had an adventure in "Ceresalpha, where the children were as ghosts". (PROSE: The Adventuress of Henrietta Street)

entities.description:
Chaos was a planet where the rain never stopped.

This fact showed the Fifth Doctor that there was another force was present when he met Amy for the first time, as this force, which was actually the Grace, had stopped time, making it seem that the rain had ceased. (AUDIO: The Judgement of Isskar)

Chaos was the place where the Chaos Pool, the forge for the Key to Time, was hidden.

It was located in a hyperspatial fold, making the extreme ends of the universe co-adjacent to each other, making the Atrions and the Teuthoidians fight each other in their respective searches for the Pool. This fold was ironed out when the segments in Zara's satchel came into contact with the warp manifold and other equipment within Professor Lydel's laboratory, even though the Doctor warned him not to put the bag near it.

entities.name: Checkley's World
entities.description:
Checkley's World, or the Horror Planet, was settled in 2290. It was determined to be ideal for special advance scientific research. By 2300, the laboratories there were no longer under state control. Some of the defence systems they developed were Freire's gas, compression grenades and Hercules Devastators.

Project FXX Q84 was the culmination of their genetic research. In 2389, Sheldukher raided the planet and stole the Project to help him find Sakkrat. Unable to find the criminal, the owners of Checkley's World found Hogsumm and modified it to closely resemble the legends of Sakkrat, hoping to lure Sheldukher there and recover the Project. Before that happened, however, Checkley's World was destroyed in a misdirected missile attack. (PROSE: The Highest Science)

entities.name: Cheetah Planet
entities.description:
The Cheetah Planet (PROSE: First Frontier) was a mysterious sentient planet and the homeworld of the Cheetah People and Kitlings.

Located outside of the Mutter's Spiral, (PROSE: Survival) the Cheetah Planet had a red-tinted sky, red sun, and peach-coloured moon. It had rough terrain, featuring rocks and sand. Due to the Cheetah People and Kitlings' hostility to extraterrestrial visitors, the planet was littered with the bones of dead humans and other creatures of the galaxy. There were also the ruins of an earlier civilisation. (TV: Survival) The magnetosphere was rich in artron energy, which is how it was able to metamorphose living matter. (PROSE: First Frontier)

The planet was in some sense, sentient and empathic, connected to the Cheetah People and when they fought in the Dead Valley, the planet became unstable and started to destroy itself.

The water on the planet had healing properties for the Cheetah People. The world allowed the Cheetah People to teleport to other planets to bring back prey. It also allowed people who wished to come home enough to return by teleportation. Humanoids such as humans and Gallifreyans slowly began to metamorphose, turning aggressive, causing them to fight with each other and they would physically begin changing into Cheetah People. described the world as dying because of its inhabitants' aggression. (TV: Survival)

entities.name: Chirracharr's World
entities.description:
Chirracharr's World, previously known as The Laboratory, was an artificial planet located in the Seven Systems. It was created by the Ixites for the purpose of studying the evolution and developments of extraterrestrial lifeforms. (PROSE: Caged)

After years of failed attempts to find alien life on other planets, a team of Ixite scientists created their own planet and gave it the conditions for organic life to emerge. They referred to this planet as The Laboratory, and closely documented its geological and meteorological development. A race of small, sentient, guinea pig-like creatures evolved. Over time, the Ixites abducted specimens of this species via a "conveyancer" and studied them.

The existence of The Laboratory was kept secret from the Ixites, whose race had expanded across the Seven Systems. The Ixites were facing a housing shortage, and when The Laboratory's existence became public knowledge there was a huge outcry of Ixites demanding the experiments be halted, the specimens destroyed, and the planet's forests and towns bulldozed to make way for new, Ixite, property development.

At the same time, a young native of the planet - Chirracharr - set out to re-discover the strange people who had abducted and experimented on her as a child. On her quest, Chirracharr met the Fifteenth Doctor and Ruby Sunday. Together they worked out that the planet, and subsequently all of the species on it, had been created by the Ixites for the purpose of study. They also worked out that the planet was scheduled for demolition. With the help of the Doctor, Chirracharr persuaded her people that alien life was real, and that their planet was in immanent danger.

entities.name: Chloris
entities.description:
Chloris was a verdant planet, covered in dense, foggy forests. Its climate was ideal for growing super-caffeinated coffee beans. (PROSE: )

A species of native, mobile plants called Wolfweeds were found on the planet, along with a group of primitive humanoids. (TV: )

The Chlorians were ruled by courts, still used astrologers, and fought with simple swords and daggers. Despite this, they did have an idea of space travel and races beyond their solar system, though they couldn't go into space themselves.

The humanoids of Chloris were kept at a primitive level due to the scarcity of metals on the planet. This stopped any mass production of materials and also stopped any clear cutting of the forests which always spread rapidly and made it very difficult to move through. Whoever held the monopoly of metal held the power.

entities.name: Christmas-land
entities.description:
The , as Gillian nick-named it, was covered in snow and pine trees, resembling a typical Christmas scene. It was home to reindeer, squirrels, and polar bears. Santa Claus moved his workshop there because of all the noisy aeroplanes which were now passing over the North Pole.

When the First Doctor, John and Gillian arrived there, a team of reindeer pulling a sleigh arrived to take them to Santa Claus, who told them that he was falling behind on making toys due to demands for model TARDISes and interference from the Demon Magician. The Doctor helped Santa out by using his "magic box" to increase toy production and, later, to defeat the Demon Magician. (COMIC: A Christmas Story)

entities.name: Chrone
entities.description:
Chrone was the oldest planet in the universe. It was home to a rare real-space access point into the Time Vortex. The Vortex Code both contained the exact coordinates to Chrone and the means to control the access point, thus allowing the user to time travel. The Tenth Doctor followed the coordinates to Chrone where he and the Mark 9 Servitor containing the Code were confronted by the Stellion Core pirates who were after the Code. The Doctor repaired the Servitor and left it there with the pirates, who were not yet aware that he had secretly altered the Code so that it would only take them to the top three theme parks in that sector of the galaxy. (COMIC: The Vortex Code)

entities.name: Chronos
entities.description:
Chronos was a planet, and the location of a temple or palace made entirely of rock and containing a temporal portal, which was used by the original population to travel into the future.

The planet was initially covered in water, but became a desert world devoid of any bodies of water, and was located light-years from a research station.

A day on the planet measured eighteen hours, and at daily intervals a wave of temporal energy washed from the temple, acting like a trawler net that flowed out then receded, dragging anything with it inside the temple. Any life on the planet's surface caught would be aged to death, and only organic matter could pass through the portal.

The Sixth Doctor and Evelyn Smythe fought the Cybermen on Chronos in 3286. (WC: Real Time, AUDIO: Real Time)

At some point after 1959, Chumeria was attacked by the Bannermen and all Chimerons except their queen, Delta, were destroyed. The planet was left barren and rocky. (TV: Delta and the Bannermen)

entities.name: Cimmeria IV
entities.description:
was a planet in the Cimmerian System enveloped in total darkness. The surface of the planet was very rocky and bitterly cold, due to the lack of a sun's heat to warm it up. Throxillian explorers and miners set up a base there, intending to exploit its apparent lack of indigenous life for commercial purposes.

A system of mini-suns were rigged up in orbit to light the planet. Their activation was stopped when the Cimmerians living on the planet blanketed the base in particles that disrupted electronic circuits, disabling the system. The particles also burned out the eyes of the base personnel.

The Eighth Doctor mediated the subsequent conflict between the Cimmerians and the ROSM rescue ship, and activated the orbital sun system. Shortly afterward he learned that the Cimmerians had kept the planet in darkness to hide from their supposed persecutors, the Solarians. With the suns active, the Solarians' solar sail ships found the planet and the two groups reconciled an ages-long misunderstanding. (AUDIO: Embrace the Darkness)

After Charley Pollard escaped from the Ever-and-Ever Prolixity, a Viyran agent was stationed in the Cimmeria system to search for her. (AUDIO: The Fall of the House of Pollard)

Clom, also spelt Klom or Cloume, (TV: ) was the twin planet of Raxacoricofallapatorius and home planet of the Abzorbalovians. (TV: )

As a member world of the Raxas Alliance, the treasures of Clom were held in the Raxasian vaults. (COMIC: )

Descendants of the Huspick Degenerate known as the Clom colonists settled on Clom. (WC: )

Clom was inhabited by an intelligent species. (TV: ) They were members of the Raxas Alliance, along with Raxacoricofallapatorius, Clix and Raxacoricovarlonpatorius. (TV: ) Despite this, there was an adverserial relationship between Clom and Raxacoricofallapatorius. (TV: ) Clom was used in an oath by a Slitheen as "for the love of Clom". (TV: ) Similarily, the Tenth Doctor was once heard to curse "for the mists of Clom." (PROSE: )

Cluut-ett-Pictar was a planet located in the Rataculan system. When the Ice Warriors embarked on their Great Exodus following the end of the Thousand Day War, their exodus fleet made a brief landing on this planet which they named Cluut-ett-Pictar. They ultimately left to found a new homeworld, which they called Nova Martia. However, a small number of the Martians stayed behind at the nest on Cluut-ett-Pictar. At some point, the nest was attacked by an Arcturan strike force but was successfully defended from their incursion. (PROSE: GodEngine)

entities.name: Cogen V
entities.description:
Cogen V was the fifth planet in the Cogen star system, in Mutter's Spiral. It was the homeworld of the Cogenians.

In 2368, the combined Borg–Cyberman fleet assaulted Cogen V and began assimilating the world and its people. In the process, they abducted the entire Cogenian population. However, the Cybermen then turned on the Borg, battling in the streets. The Cybermen took the Cogenians for cyber-conversion.

The USS Enterprise-D followed the fleet to Cogen V, but discovered that it had abruptly changed course and left. Commander William Riker, Lieutenant Commander Data and Lieutenant Worf, together with the Eleventh Doctor, Amy Pond and Rory Williams, beamed down into a Cogenian settlement, discovering it left in flaming ruins. Surviving Cogenian sentry drones attacked the group on arrival, but were soon shot down. They discovered Borg and Cyberman bodies left on the surface and soon learned of the battle amongst their enemies. (COMIC: Assimilation²)

The plan was stopped by the Eighth Doctor, Liv Chenka and Helen Sinclair. (AUDIO: World of Damnation, Sweet Salvation)

entities.name: Colony 34
entities.description:
Colony 34 was one of 49 colony planets in a binary star system.

After being settled, it was realised by the government that there were fewer natural resources than originally thought. With energy in short supply, public confidence in the government declined. To maintain control, they staged fake terrorist attacks and other distractions to postpone new elections.

Eventually, it was realised that people could be used as fuel, so the government encouraged immigration to increase the supply of potential bodies for that purpose. The truth of what was happening was finally revealed by the Seventh Doctor, Ace and Hex. (AUDIO: LIVE 34)
